text:
我不能允许中文圈的朋友错过这篇文章！读完大概8分钟，这可能是10月份最值得的8分钟。

我给大家翻译好了👇

如何变得更有雄心：写给与模型协作的人类使用指南

阅读时长：约 8 分钟

我在 Claude 团队工作。这是一段很有意思的经历：几乎每天，我都会发现有人借助 Claude 完成了某项壮举，而这些成就往往是我未曾考虑过、曾认为不可能做到，或者单纯因为缺乏好奇心和时间而未曾尝试的。就在这个月，它可能参与协助发现了一颗新行星；我看到了第一支自己真心喜欢的 AI 音乐视频；我们甚至还在讨论数学的新纪元。

模型的能力并非均衡发展。正如数学家陶哲轩（Terence Tao）所言，模型“在某些方向令人惊叹，而在另一些方向却显稚嫩”。有些人成功驾驭了这些惊人的能力，仿佛翱翔于天际——看着大家用我参与打造的产品攀登难以置信的高度，十分令人着迷。但还有许多人仍在努力适应他们的新羽翼，困惑于除了询问“法国的首都是哪里”或“帮我把这封邮件润色得别那么生气”之外，模型到底还能做什么。

我和其他从事 AI 工作的人经常呼吁：在使用 AI 时，我们应当更有雄心（ambitious）。这已经成为了一句集结号角式的口号。每当我们看到令人赞叹的应用时，就会转发并写道：“我们的野心还不够大。”但我深知将这种建议付诸实践有多么棘手，因此，这里有一份关于“如何变得更有雄心”的操作指南。

我认为“雄心”可以分为四种维度：速度（Speed）、高度（Altitude）、深度（Depth）以及广度（Range）。

速度（Speed）： 用更少的时间完成同样的工作，这是 AI 经济价值的基本盘：如果你需要写代码，我用 Claude 能完成得更快。这一点已被广泛认知，且不需要在使用 AI 的方式上发挥太多创造力，因此本文略过不谈。

高度（Altitude）： 提升抽象层级，关注最终结果而非单一具体任务。

深度（Depth）： 像行业顶尖专家一样去审视和推演任务。不再停留于任务表层，而是深入一层，触及底层的原始数据、工具和根本问题。

广度（Range）： 借鉴多个领域的经验与方法，而非仅仅局限于任务表面所需的那一个领域，去调用那些你平时通常不会用到的知识、工具和技术。

我主要使用 Claude（显而易见），但我的建议并不受限于特定模型。

高度（Altitude）
我们常随口将其称作“让模型在更高的抽象层级上运行”。当你给模型分配一项任务时，它执行的不过是你对“如何达成目标”所做的最优猜测。要在“高度”上更有雄心，不妨问问自己——接下来你希望发生什么？目标背后的终极目标是什么？ 去年年初，我还会让 Claude 帮我排查并修复单个软件崩溃；而到了后来，我直接要求 Claude 确保我们的应用程序“零崩溃”。

让我们以一个日常（甚至可以说是琐碎）的办公任务为例。假设你在一家名为 Acme Inc 的虚构公司，需要为季度业务回顾（QBR）制作一套汇报幻灯片（PPT）。如果你输入一堆数据，Claude 很乐意为你生成几张幻灯片；如果你提供模板，它也可以顺畅填入内容。但这很难与“发现新行星”相提并论。来看看一些具体的步骤，让我们的思路逐层提升雄心：

基础步骤： 大多数业务回顾都想知道本季度发生了什么变化、原因是什么、以及应该采取什么对策。克制住仅在模板里更新数字的冲动——尽可能把你能获取到的所有原始数据喂给模型，让它理解你的业务逻辑：“告诉我本季度发生了什么变化，背后的原因是什么，以及我们应该如何应对。”

进阶步骤： 会议（至少高效的会议）最终都应产出明确的决策。向 Claude 提问：“基于你目前了解到的所有情况，梳理出眼前最紧迫的三个决策是什么，并针对潜在的发展方向展开分析，分别列出正反两面的论据。”

高阶步骤： 季度业务回顾诞生于这样一个时代：那时需要人类耗费大量精力筛选数据、厘清数据背后的含义，并判断公司是否需要做出业务调整。你可以这样要求 Claude：“业务评审的存在是为了让管理层及早发现问题，把资金和人力调度到正确的位置。请设计一种比‘季度汇报 PPT’更好的机制来实现这一点，并结合我们以往的历史数据证明该机制能更早发现问题；同时让这套新方案与当前机制并行运行一个季度。”

“高度”策略在追求某种终极成果时效果最好，但在纯创意类任务中表现稍逊。判断何时适合在“高度”上发力的一个显著标志是：你是否需要为了手头正在做的事情去开会讨论。 当然，目前这一方法仍有局限（在 2026 年，“Claude，帮我去赚钱”对绝大多数公司来说单凭一句话还是行不通的），但我普遍发现：随着模型能力的增强，它们处理高层级抽象任务的表现也越来越出色。

“高度”也是构建持久工作流（将人类移出执行闭环、无需你反复输入一项又一项任务）的关键所在。要做好这一点，通常需要重构你的工作流程——为了让 Claude 能够自主确保应用程序零崩溃，我首先得保证它能轻松拉取崩溃报告，理解哪个应用版本对应哪次 Git 提交，并赋予它访问 Windows、macOS 和 Linux 环境的权限，使其能够真正独立地复现并验证修复方案。

深度（Depth）
有时候，你只是想把某一项具体任务执行得极其出色。在“深度”上拥有雄心，意味着促使模型去使用该领域最顶尖专家所采用的工具、技术、媒介和专业知识——并持续深挖，直到连那些专家都能从你的产出中获得启发。

继续沿用 Acme Inc 的季度业务回顾例子。假设 Acme 公司正面临用户流失（随着时间推移客户流失）的困境。我发现结合以下技巧非常有效：

坚持使用业内顶尖专家所使用的工具： 当被要求“表现得像个专业人士”时，模型往往只是换了套行业术语，而没有真正改变工作方法。要在深度上解决问题，我们必须使用顶尖数据科学家和统计学家同款的工具。当 Claude 倾向于生成简单的 Markdown 表格时，坚持要求它构建数据库和统计模型。你不需要预先知道专家用什么，Claude 通常心里有数。

设定看似离谱的目标，并告诉模型这完全合情合理： 你需要将网页加载时间从 10 秒缩短到 5 秒？不妨直接要求达到 200 毫秒。如果模型觉得某件事不可能办到，重申这完全是可解的，它只需要继续探索尝试。

挑战既有认知： 尤其在商业领域，许多我们坚信不疑的事情其实只是对现实的粗糙近似。将原始信息与数据提供给模型，让它以对抗性的视角去检验既有假设：“我们一直认为用户流失是由于上手引导（onboarding）体验不佳导致的。请尝试从原始数据中复现并验证这一推论。”

创造新知识： 这一点可以顺理成章地承接对既有认知的挑战——一旦 Claude 已经深入数据腹地，让它去探寻盲区：“基于系统日志构建一套能够复现去年业务情况的客户模拟系统。然后找出我们尚未察觉的最早流失信号，并证明该信号能在未参与训练的新数据上完成有效预测。”

引入外部裁判： 切勿让模型对自己打分评判。我相信随着模型智能的提升，这一问题终会解决，但在 2026 年 10 月的当下，我强烈建议引入外部验证机制。最理想的方式是提供一个可供模型直接运行并实时获取反馈的评估工具。

我经常使用的一个简短提示词（Prompt）：

“我希望这项任务更加深入，而不是范围更大。在重写任务前，请先列出：(1) 该领域的顶尖专家会做哪些我目前没有要求的事情；(2) 他们会从哪些最原始的材料入手，而不是使用已被加工整理过的数据；(3) 他们会使用哪些具体的方法和专业工具；(4) 除了你和我之外，还有什么客观指标或外部手段能证明结果是正确的。完成以上分析后，重写我的提示词，精确提出这些要求。”

广度（Range）
简而言之，在“广度”上拥有雄心，意味着我们从多个不同领域的视角来审视手头的工作——引入比过去在成本考量下所能承受的更多跨界学科。这并不是多么独到的洞见，每一部盗贼冒险电影（Heist movie）在前 30 分钟里都在忙着集结性格迥异、各怀绝技的团队成员。随着 AI 工具让多智能体系统（Multi-agent systems，包含多线程、编排器或单纯的子智能体）的运行变得越发轻而易举，要求 Claude 跨界引入额外领域往往能带来惊艳的效果。

将其付诸实践并不简单，需要你发挥创造力。直到我看到同事 Alex Albert 使用 Blender 渲染室内设计，我才想到可以用 Claude 为我的个人主页构建 3D 虚拟环境——尽管我以前做过电子游戏！然而，这也是我见证最多神奇瞬间发生的地方。

具体该如何操作？我通常采用以下方法：

尝试用动词替换名词： 这是来自汤姆·凯利（Tom Kelley）与乔纳森·利特曼（Jonathan Littman）著作《创新的艺术》（The Art of Innovation）中的一个经典技巧。季度业务回顾不是“一套 PPT”，而是“在 30 分钟内，让事务繁忙的人相信一个关于因果关系的故事，并在不确定性中做出决断”。提炼出动词之后，不仅能让我、也能让 Claude 更容易理解哪些领域能为这一目标带来独特且有价值的视角。

组建你的特遣队： 假设这套 PPT 必须达到极高水准，否则外星人就要毁灭地球——人类会组建一支怎样的梦之队？为了保证产出质量，我会拉入一位数据分析师、一位调查记者和一位编辑；如果需要现场演讲，或许还要加入动态视觉设计师和音频设计师；甚至还可以组建一支对抗性的“红方团队”，邀请一位做空机构研究员和一名法务会计师加入。这里很容易不小心滑向纯粹的角色扮演，这只会让上下文变得古怪而不会实质提升产出质量。使用这个方法的核心是寻找对应的学科领域与专业方法：不要让模型去“扮演”一个做空机构空头，而是让它像做空者调研仓位那样去执行具体的调研动作。

上述所有维度的雄心，都要求模型拥有可安装软件的计算机环境，以及对各类相关数据的访问权限（无论是通过 MCP 协议连接器还是其他途径）。目前已有大量工具让这成为可能，我非常建议大家配置使用。

历史早有先例
以上就是我对如何变得更有雄心的具体建议。如果你愿意多停留一分钟，我还想聊聊为什么我认为在当下这显得尤为必要。

人类自古以来就常常受困于自己对“可能发生什么”的认知定势——更糟的是，我们通常只在极其狭窄的专业领域内信任自己的能力。众所周知，米开朗基罗当年极不情愿去画西斯廷礼拜堂天顶画——因为在他看来，自己是一名雕塑家，而不是画家。

在调研关于“雄心”的课题时，我发现心理学中对此有一个专门的概念：自我效能感（Self-efficacy）。简而言之，自我效能感高的人更坚信自身的能力，从而往往能在现实中取得更大的成就。研究表明，自我效能感是可以被激发的：洛克（Locke）和拉瑟姆（Latham）深入梳理了长达 35 年的目标设定研究，得出明确结论：被设定具体且高难度目标的人，其表现显著优于那些仅仅被告知‘尽力而为’的人。Stripe 联合创始人帕特里克·科利森（Patrick Collison）长期维护着一个“快速榜单”（Fast list），记录了人类在被赋予宏伟目标和严苛期限时所完成的种种奇迹。其中一些被充分印证的思维策略包括：

通过相信事情可行去攻克难关： 1939 年，乔治·丹齐格（George Dantzig）在加州大学伯克利分校的一堂统计课上迟到了。他把黑板上的两道题抄了下来，以为那是课后作业并按时交了上去——而实际上，那是当时统计学界尚未破解的两大著名世界难题。

目睹他人做成之后去突破极限： 数十年来，人类一直试图打破“4 分钟跑完 1 英里”的极限。罗杰·班尼斯特（Roger Bannister）于 1954 年 5 月首次打破该记录，但他作为这一纪录唯一保持者的时间仅仅维持了 46 天。如果你热爱跑步，会发现类似的突破正在马拉松破 2 小时的征程中上演：塞巴斯蒂安·索维（Sabastian Sawe）在今年 4 月的伦敦马拉松赛中跑出了首个官方破 2 成绩；而在同一场比赛中，亚军也同样突破了 2 小时大关。

通过允许自己失败去成就大事： 大家似乎最喜爱的商业书籍是《身心合一的奇迹力量》（The Inner Game of Tennis，又译网球内心戏），而我上周才发现这本书。该书的核心观点是：如果你拼命去用力，你反而打不出最好的比赛状态。我们工程师或许还记得 Linux 最初的发布宣言：“这只是一项业余爱好，不会搞得像 GNU 那样庞大而专业。”

自我效能感并非新问题，但在今天它变得前所未有地关键。置身于能力每隔数周就会发生飞跃的世界，我们需要一套全新的思维与方法，让我们敢于去做那些曾经未曾考虑过、甚至不敢相信可能办到的事。

如果你发现了更多能激发雄心的新技巧，欢迎随时和我交流！

本文题图来自弗朗西斯科·戈雅（Francisco Goya）的作品《飞行方式》（Modo de volar）。

text:
Regarding StandX’s decision not to proceed with a TGE, I want to speak to everyone with complete candor.

Without any external VC funding, our TVL reached a peak of $200 million. While our team delivered achievements worth being proud of, we still fell short of our ambition to become a top 3 perps dex.

Given our current fundamentals, we technically could push forward with launching a token. However, launching a token primarily on the back of short term speculation without delivering sustainable long term value ultimately leaves the cost for our users and community to bear. Doing so would be irresponsible, both to our community and to our team, and it goes against my personal values.

Most of our past revenue has already been passed back to users through SIP-2 and SIP-3 subsidies. For this upcoming airdrop, beyond utilizing our remaining project treasury, I will also personally contribute funds to do everything I can to give back to the community that supported us along the way.

All user funds are completely safe and DUSD is fully collateralized. We will ensure an orderly wind down and clearly publish specific arrangements regarding fund withdrawals, airdrops, and service sunset dates.

Thank you to every single user and team member. I deeply regret that we couldn't reach where we set out to go. You can trust that this final bittersweet process will be handled cleanly and professionally. Thank you, one final time, for your support throughout this journey and for standing with us.

这次 StandX不进行TGE的决定，我想坦诚地和大家说几句。

在没有外部资本加持的情况下，我们的 TVL 最高达到过 2 亿美元。团队做出了值得肯定的成绩，但仍未达到我们进入行业前三的预期。

以目前项目的基本面，我们确实可以继续发币。但如果无法兑现长期价值，靠发币和短期炒作获利，就是把代价留给用户和社区。这对外、对内都不负责任，也不符合我的价值观。

过去的大部分收入，已经通过 SIP-2 / SIP-3 补贴给了用户。这次空投，除了项目账上的盈余，我也会个人出资，尽力回馈一路支持我们的社区。

所有用户资金都是安全的。我们会确保有序关停，并明确公布资金提取、空投和各项服务停止的具体安排。

感谢每一位用户和团队成员。没能走到预期的位置，我很遗憾。我们会尽力把最后的事情做好。

text:
Starknet 一个月涨 4 倍，真的只是叙事炒作吗

过去几天不少朋友来问「STRK 到底发生了啥」，共识回答基本都是「叙事炒作」「情绪拉盘」

昨晚把 60 天数据和官方动作翻了个遍，反而开始改观，这篇认真聊聊，Starknet 这波背后到底在定价什么

一个做了 7 年 STARK 的老团队，不该只被用一句「炒作」打发掉

❚ 回看下价格表现

STRK 从 9/15 的 0.029 刀，拉到 10/12 的 0.123 刀，一个月 4 倍

其中几根关键 K 线单拎出来
- 9/19 单日 +52%，成交量放大 15 倍
- 10/4 到 10/5 从横盘的 0.043 拉到 0.0586，两天涨 35%
- 10/10 到 10/12 三天翻了一倍多，从 0.056 冲到 0.123

10/12 当天成交 7.41 亿美金，当天市值才 9 亿出头，换手超过 80%

作为对比，ARB 同一天只有 2 亿成交，而当天 ARB 市值也只比 STRK 大三成

现在 STRK 市值 5.7 亿，ARB 12.3 亿，差了一倍多

如果你认同 Starknet 的 ZK 技术栈至少不输 Arbitrum 的 Optimistic Rollup，那补涨逻辑是成立的

❚ 这波涨的到底是什么

拆开看，一个月里其实有三段完全不同性质的拉升

1/ 9 月：隐私叙事，产品是真有东西

9/16 StarkWare(@StarkWareLtd) 公布 STRK20 已在主网落地的 7 个场景

- 隐私转账
- Avnu 隐私兑换
- Endur 隐私质押 STRK 和 BTC
- Ready 和 Xverse 加密解密
- Avnu 隐私 paymaster
- OffMarket 隐私下注 Polymarket
- DashX 隐私发薪

接下来几周持续兑现，一个没放空炮
- 10/13 Shadow Accounts 上线，每个应用一个化名地址
- 10/14 OffMarket 面向公众开放
- 10/16 Haven 隐私银行卡上线

OffMarket 这个产品值得细讲，解决了一个币圈很多人没意识到的痛点

Polymarket 上大额仓位是全透明的，鲸鱼下单直接被跟单套利

OffMarket 的设计是，USDC 存进 Starknet 的隐私池，每次下注派生一个全新 Polygon 钱包，通过 Circle CCTP 跨过去

对手盘根本不知道背后是同一个人在操作

更妙的是合规设计
Financial Privacy Inc 这家独立合规公司持有「主查看密钥」，密钥放在安全飞地里，由 StarkWare 和 FPI 多签保管
存款过制裁名单筛查，法院和监管调取请求由 FPI 律师审核，可以拒绝

查看密钥看得到交易，但动不了资金

👉 这个设计有点像「保险箱的备用钥匙放在律师那里」
既保证了普通用户的隐私，又给监管留了一道合规入口
这是我见过最聪明的 crypto 隐私产品设计之一，比纯粹的匿名协议走得远

9/19 那波 +52% 就发生在隐私功能公布之后，说明市场是真在给隐私落地定价

2/ 10 月上旬：技术升级 + 隐私产品持续兑现

10/4 到 10/5 这段 35% 的拉升，发生在 L1 推文之前，很多人把它和 L1 行情混在一起算，其实不对

背后的催化剂是
- 10/5 v0.14.4 主网上线，调整 gas 定价和 gateway API，通过 SNIP-36 支持更大证明
- 隐私生态持续加码，9 个协议接入 STRK20，220+ 开发者在 STRK20 Private Sprint 做了 200 个隐私项目
- Garden 做了官方 strkBTC 跨链桥，可从 11 条链换入

这段涨幅是硬技术升级 + 隐私叙事外溢，和 L1 没半毛钱关系

3/ 10 月中旬:L1 + 抗量子叙事点火

10/8 Token2049 期间，Starknet 官号发「正在认真考虑成为 L1，目标 2027 年全面抗量子」

10/11 Eli Ben-Sasson( @EliBenSasson ) 跟上「世界需要一个抗量子的 Starknet L1」，11 万浏览

必须承认，推文确实走在了提案前面
- 没有 SNIP、没有治理投票、没有迁移方案、没有时间表
- 官号自己后来补了一句「这是一个问题，不是一个决定」

但也必须承认，技术路径不是凭空画饼
- 10/10 Eli 晒 Pixel 手机 51 秒生成一笔真实主网交易的完整 STARK 证明，内存只用 2.41GB
- 10/12 欧洲刑警组织(Europol)关于量子威胁的报告，点名引用 StarkWare
- StarkWare 从 2018 年就在做 STARK 证明，这个赛道他们走了 7 年

人话说就是，10 月中旬这波情绪确实先行了，但情绪指向的技术方向不是空的

抗量子是整个加密行业未来 5 到 10 年必须回答的问题
以太坊的后量子路线按 Eli 的说法要到 2029 年底，Starknet 想在 2027 年完成，这个时间差本身就是重估的理由

❚ 顺带把 L2 板块比一下

同样是 L2，ARB 60 天也翻了一倍多（约 140%），但走的是另一种节奏

- 9/27 ARB 到 0.222 见顶，之后一直横盘回落
- 9 月那波是 ARB 带节奏，STRK 跟涨
- 10 月是 STRK 自己独立走，ARB 已经不参与了

换句话说，这轮 L2 反弹分两段
- 9 月：板块轮动，ARB 带头
- 10 月：STRK 自成一派，开始走独立定价

对一个做了 7 年 STARK、技术路线长期被低估的团队来说，走独立行情是迟到的重估

❚ 必须说的几个保留

作为老韭菜，看多也要留几个清醒的刻度
- 每月 15 号解锁 1.27%，今天就是解锁日，按现价约 970 万美金，比 9 月那次高了快 3 倍
- 10/13 单日 -31%，从高点回撤 38%，追高的朋友吃了一记闷棍
- TVL 1.63 亿和 8 月持平，二级跑在前面，生态资金还没跟上
- 隐私池目前 150 到 200 万美金，OffMarket 单户 1000 美金上限，离基本面支撑市值还有距离

但这些是「短期波动」而非「长期证伪」

TVL 没涨不代表生态没动静，9 月 7 个隐私场景、Garden 做官方 strkBTC 桥、AEON 在印度和拉美做商户支付、1.5 亿美金的质押里有 580 枚 BTC，这些都是闷头在推进的事

隐私池小是因为刚上线，参考成熟隐私协议的早期曲线，起步阶段都这样

❚ 一句话总结

STRK 这波涨，共识归因「纯叙事」是不准确的，准确拆解是三段
- 9 月是隐私落地的实打实定价
- 10 月上旬是技术升级和产品兑现
- 10 月中旬是 L1 抗量子的提前定价

一个做了 7 年 STARK 的老团队，正在同时推进两条真实的技术路线

接下来几周值得盯两个硬指标
- Starknet 论坛或 Github 有没有正式的 SNIP 提案
- 下一次解锁日（11/15）卖压怎么消化

写在最后，我没在高点追过 $STRK，这篇也不含任何代币建议

但认真研究完这些产品和路线之后，开始改变对这条链的看法

至少我写了这篇文章，你读了这篇文章，比共识多看了一层，这就够了

#Starknet $STRK @Starknet @StarkWareLtd

这周在研究策略的时候本着想拿一个号试试爆仓流，经过一次爆仓后我发现竟然没有清算费这个东西，然后我就去DOC里面去翻，发现真的是不收清算费

群友反馈上去了之后，官方立马修改doc，现在写的是收1%的清算费，一点对这个事情的说明都没有

只能说这个项目方是真的垃圾，一开始就没想好要怎么做，积分计划也全是草草了事，最开始还想把所有积分都黑盒，这样垃圾的项目不知道你们还能撸下去不

而且我敢肯定的是明年上半年一定不会结束，会有各种理由进行延期，这种项目方3个月时间准备个积分计划都是烂的还指望他半年多就发币出来？

背景再好自己打的一手烂牌也是烂货；图片中可以看见我的费用就是基本的手续费，群友的费用还有1%的清算费，而且官方修改doc后没任何说明更别提补偿了

Their buying behavior will be measurable and optimized around objective criteria (cost, speed, finality, performance…) rather than habits, marketing, or fear of missing out.

text:
The analysis point of this tweet is: $BORDR fundamentals are strengthening, and the market is starting to reprice the programmable token standard on Solana.

6Mix12LiHrQFojaQEnfPUC65Qkwd6X4Y5Qg93oFbordr 

Compared with our previous analyses, I believe Bordrless’s fundamentals have genuinely improved. What matters this time is not another batch of token-launch features, but the project’s attempt to redefine what a token can be on Solana: not merely an asset that records balances, but one that can carry its own execution rules and enforce them during transactions.

That is the central idea behind Bordrless’s latest article, “Every Solana Token Is the Same Token.”

In the traditional Solana ecosystem, most SPL tokens rely on a generic Token Program to manage balances and transfers. Token-2022 introduced extensions such as transfer hooks, but many complex mechanisms—including taxes, buybacks, rewards, burns, and automated distributions—still require external bots, servers, or other programs to operate.

Bordrless is trying to change that by making the token itself part of the rule-execution process, then connecting transactions, holder state, and fund management through its own DEX and Companion programs.

It does not automatically add features to every existing Solana token. Instead, it establishes a separate token standard that allows newly launched tokens to support more sophisticated economic mechanisms.

The important development is that Bordrless is connecting its Token Standard, DEX, Companions, and Workshop into a complete infrastructure stack.

Token hooks can execute rules during transfers, minting, and burning, while recording certain information about each holder, such as entry price, holding duration, and rewards already paid. They can deduct fees from transferred amounts or reject transactions that violate predefined rules, but they cannot independently obtain a user’s signature or move more assets than the original operation allows.

However, a transfer hook alone cannot necessarily determine whether a transfer represents a buy, a sell, or an ordinary wallet transfer. That is why Bordrless built its own DEX, where pool hooks can access the full transaction context, including direction, amount, price, trader, recipient, and pool state, and enforce rules before and after a swap.

This creates a path for mechanisms that previously depended on project promises or off-chain scripts to become part of transaction execution itself.

The platform already supports creator fees, sniper fees of up to 80% during the first 30 seconds, different buy and sell rates, buy-side burns, maximum wallet limits, early-buyer locks, and SOL rewards for holders.

Companions manage creator-fee treasuries and can execute predefined strategies involving market making, buybacks, burns, holder rewards, and game-related spending. Hooks enforce rules and record state during transactions, while Companions manage funds according to those rules. Together, they reduce the need for project teams to rely entirely on external bots running continuously.

Bordrless has also opened up its SDK and Workshop. Developers can use Rust, the SDK, or AI coding agents such as Claude Code and Cursor to build their own hooks and companions, then submit source code and testing materials for review. Approved components can be selected by other token launchers, and developers can earn 50% of the creator fees generated by subsequent launches that use their components.

This means ecosystem growth no longer has to depend entirely on the official team shipping more features. Bordrless is attempting to create a system in which third-party developers supply components, other launchers reuse them, and developers earn revenue when their work gets adopted.

If this structure takes off, Bordrless’s competitive position could expand beyond a launchpad into infrastructure capable of supporting many different token mechanisms. That is what makes it more interesting than an ordinary launchpad.

And this time, the progress is not limited to a stronger narrative. Platform metrics have also improved.

In our previous analyses, the website showed 93 total launches and approximately $222.5K in 24-hour trading volume. The latest snapshot shows 114 launches and approximately $469K in 24-hour volume. Cumulative holder distributions increased from 28.5 SOL to 37.6 SOL, cumulative launch fees rose from 99.4 SOL to 159.8 SOL, and the reported cumulative value of rule-triggered burns increased from 17 SOL to 22.5 SOL.

These figures indicate that launches, trading activity, and economic mechanisms are operating in practice. The simultaneous increase in launches and trading volume is particularly meaningful compared with simply announcing new features.

However, these are website snapshots taken at different times, not a continuous independently audited dataset. Automated strategies may also contribute to trading volume, so platform turnover should not be treated as equivalent to genuine buying and selling by independent users.

The website’s displayed BORDR buyback value has also increased from approximately $9.31K to $26.26K, but this requires caution. According to the official tokenomics documentation, the displayed dollar value represents bridged BORDR held in the treasury at the current market price. A rising token price can increase that figure by itself, so it cannot be interpreted as proof that actual buyback spending has increased by 2.75 times. The figures that matter are the SOL actually spent, the number of tokens purchased, and the corresponding on-chain transactions.

This brings us to BORDR’s value-capture mechanism.

According to the official tokenomics, BORDR has a fixed total supply of 1 billion tokens. Half of protocol revenue remains in the treasury for operating expenses, while the other half is used to buy back BORDR. The purchased tokens are bridged into the treasury and held; they are not burned. The buyback process is executed by an off-chain keeper, with the official mechanism designed to run every 10 minutes. If the keeper stops operating, incoming revenue remains in the treasury until further processing.

Therefore, BORDR’s economic thesis is based on potential recurring buying pressure generated by protocol revenue, not deflation through token burns.

For product growth to translate into stronger token demand, it must generate sustained protocol revenue that leads to actual buybacks. Higher platform trading volume does not mean every dollar of turnover becomes protocol revenue, and the website’s displayed buyback value is not the same as the amount spent on purchases during the current period.

So why did BORDR suddenly rally?

My interpretation is that the move likely reflects a combination of a stronger narrative, product delivery, and growing platform activity rather than a single tweet acting as the sole catalyst.

The latest article reframes Bordrless from a platform for launching tokens with taxes and rewards into a programmable token standard. That gives the market a different way to value the project. Traders are no longer looking only at the number of launches; they are beginning to consider whether other developers will adopt the standard to build their own token economics.

Meanwhile, SDK 0.10.0 has been released, and Companion and scripting capabilities have continued to improve. This indicates that the product is being delivered rather than remaining on a roadmap. Combined with the increases in launches and trading volume, these developments give the market a reason to price in potential ecosystem expansion ahead of time.

I believe the market is primarily betting on three things.

First, Solana could gain a token standard capable of supporting complex economic mechanisms. If developers build custom taxes, rewards, automated market-making strategies, and treasury-management systems on top of Bordrless, it could become infrastructure used by applications rather than just another launchpad.

Second, AI coding agents could lower the barrier to building on-chain mechanisms. Developers can publish components through the SDK and Workshop, then earn a share of fees when other projects adopt them. If independent developers, reusable components, and actual deployments continue to grow, a genuine network effect could emerge.

Third, platform growth could translate into BORDR demand through protocol revenue and buybacks. More launches and trading activity could generate more revenue and increase the funds available for buybacks. But because purchased tokens are held in the treasury rather than burned, the key is growth in actual revenue and the number of tokens bought—not simply describing the mechanism as ongoing deflation.

Going forward, I would focus on four areas.

The first is third-party developer adoption. SDK downloads do not equal independent developers. More meaningful indicators include the number of developers who successfully deploy components, the number of hooks and companions reused by other projects, and the fees those components actually generate.

The second is integration with external trading venues. Axiom has already provided an external trading entry point, but the broader distribution thesis depends on whether more terminals and aggregators integrate and how much incremental trading volume they bring.

The third is whether platform trading volume and protocol revenue continue to grow together. Reaching 114 launches and approximately $469K in 24-hour volume is encouraging, but automated trading must be distinguished from genuine user demand before the figures can validate sustainable revenue growth.

The fourth is whether buybacks can be independently verified. Only by checking actual on-chain spending, purchased token quantities, and treasury balances can we determine how much platform growth is translating into genuine buying pressure for BORDR.

The risks remain significant. Bordrless uses a separate token standard, meaning other trading venues must support its execution rules. Greater technical capability does not automatically mean lower adoption barriers. Open development also introduces code-quality and security risks, while automated trading strategies can contribute to headline volume. Given the sharp price increase, the market may already be pricing in a substantial portion of the anticipated ecosystem growth.

My conclusion is that Bordrless’s fundamentals have strengthened compared with our previous analyses, particularly in the completeness of its product architecture, the delivery of its SDK and Companion capabilities, and the growth in launches, trading activity, and reported economic-mechanism execution.

The central bet behind this rally is whether Bordrless can evolve from a technically differentiated launchpad into a programmable token standard that third-party developers consistently adopt across Solana.

But product progress and commercial validation must remain separate. The latest article presents a more complete explanation of the architecture, while growth in launches and trading activity provides encouraging evidence. Neither, on its own, proves that a developer network effect has already formed.

What ultimately determines whether BORDR deserves further repricing is sustained adoption of third-party components, the conversion of platform activity into recurring protocol revenue, and transparent evidence that buybacks are growing alongside the ecosystem.

If those indicators continue improving, Bordrless could evolve from a launchpad into infrastructure supported by a real developer ecosystem and recurring revenue. If price and attention continue rising while adoption and revenue fail to keep pace, however, the rally will be more likely to reflect expectations being priced in ahead of fundamentals.

$BORDR Fundamentals Are Strengthening, but the Next Stage Depends on Whether the Ecosystem Can Truly Gain Traction

6Mix12LiHrQFojaQEnfPUC65Qkwd6X4Y5Qg93oFbordr 

Bordrless's fundamentals have improved significantly. The changes go beyond adding a few features. The project is expanding from its own token standard, DEX, and launchpad into an open developer platform and an external trading distribution network.

What we can confirm so far is that product delivery and infrastructure development have made progress. However, the scale of the developer ecosystem, the actual trading growth generated by external integrations, and the long-term value capture of BORDR still need to be validated with data.

The most notable aspect of this update is that three developments are happening simultaneously: Axiom integration is live, the SDK and Workshop are lowering barriers to developer participation, and mainnet programs have added fee distribution and scripting capabilities. If these components work together, Bordrless could evolve from a technically differentiated launchpad into infrastructure that other projects actively use.

What Has Changed in This Update?

1. From Its Own Trading Interface to External Trading Distribution

Axiom has integrated the Bordrless Token Standard and DEX. According to the official team, all tokens launched on Bordrless can now be traded on Axiom while retaining the corresponding Hooks. This means trading is no longer limited to Bordrless's own website, and other trading terminals and aggregators are also planned for integration.

This is one of the most important changes in this update. It addresses product distribution rather than simply improving the interface. The more external trading entry points there are, the more opportunities launched projects have to reach traders. However, completing an integration does not guarantee significant additional trading volume. That still needs to be demonstrated through actual trading data.

2. From an Official Development Product to an Open Developer Ecosystem

The SDK allows developers to create custom Hooks, trading pools, and Bonding Curves. They can also add liquidity and use bridged assets as quote assets. Hooks can execute custom rules during token transfers and trading, such as taxes, holder rewards, transfer restrictions, or burns. Companions manage creator fees according to predefined schedules and rules, supporting functions such as market making and buybacks.

The team is also shifting the Studio development workflow toward developers building independently with AI coding agents such as Claude Code and Cursor, then submitting their work to the Workshop. The platform reviews, builds, simulates, and deploys approved projects. AI explains what the code does and how much it charges in plain language. Approved Hooks and Companions can then be selected by other token launchers, and developers can earn 50% of the creator fees generated by subsequent launches that use their configurations.

This means developers no longer have to be merely users of Bordrless products. They can become providers of ecosystem components. The real growth signal is not how many people download the SDK, but how many third-party tools pass review, get adopted by other launchers, and generate recurring revenue.

3. Mainnet Upgrades Are Improving Fee Distribution and Ecosystem Incentives

The mainnet upgrades announced by the team include the release of SDK 0.10.0; the ability for terminals, bots, and wallets to add integration fees of up to 1% to Bordrless trades they route; the ability to split a token's creator fees among up to 10 wallets at fixed percentages; scripts that can pay SOL to eligible wallets when the launcher enables the feature in advance; and the option for Workshop developers to publish their Hooks with a 0% fee.

These capabilities serve different purposes: monetizing trading entry points, splitting fees among project teams, automating on-chain payments, and encouraging developer participation. Creator-fee distribution and programmable scripts are particularly useful because they allow teams, treasuries, partners, and automated strategies to participate in a project's economic flows.

One distinction matters: integration fees collected by third parties do not automatically become BORDR revenue, and creator fees earned by developers are not equivalent to returns for token holders. These are initially economic mechanisms for the platform and ecosystem participants. They can indirectly benefit BORDR only if they generate revenue that the protocol can capture.

4. A Quick-Trade Panel and Builder Competition Improve User Experience and Incentivize Supply

The new web trading panel floats over the chart and combines buying, selling, preset amounts, estimated tokens received, and trading rules. Trading wallets can sign without an additional prompt. The goal is to let users trade directly while viewing market data and to prepare for future terminal integrations.

The team also announced a $5,000 Builder Race, with the top three projects receiving $2,500, $1,500, and $1,000 after 72 hours. The competition aims to attract early developers to build Hooks, Companions, and other tools, but the prize money itself does not prove that sustained ecosystem demand already exists.

Following these updates, the product's core positioning has become clearer. Bordrless is not just a launchpad. It is building its own token standard, DEX, and launchpad on Solana, allowing token rules to be executed through Hooks. The official documentation lists the mainnet programs and explains how they differ from Token-2022 transfer hooks.

External integrations are also beginning to address the distribution bottleneck. An in-house DEX can execute complex rules, but if tokens depend entirely on the project's own website, trader reach and liquidity may be limited. Axiom's integration demonstrates that external distribution is no longer entirely theoretical. The next question is whether other terminals and aggregators follow through and how much trading volume they bring.

Finally, developer incentives are becoming more complete. The SDK, AI coding agents, Workshop review and deployment, reusable Hooks, and creator-fee sharing are beginning to form a loop. In theory, developers have an incentive to build better trading rules and fee-management tools, while launchers can use those tools directly. The wider the adoption, the more fees developers can earn.

However, open development capabilities do not mean a developer network effect has already formed. Sustained third-party output, genuine adoption, and verifiable fee distributions are needed before this mechanism can be considered commercially validated.

Has BORDR's Value Capture Improved Alongside the Product?

A stronger product does not necessarily translate into proportionally stronger demand for its token.

According to the official Tokenomics documentation, half of protocol revenue is retained in the treasury for operating expenses such as development and deployment, while the other half is used to buy back BORDR every 10 minutes. The purchased tokens are bridged into the treasury and held; they are not burned. The team also states that buybacks are executed by an off-chain keeper operated by Bordrless. If the keeper stops, revenue remains in the treasury until processing resumes.

Current project metrics displayed on the Bordrless website:

Total launches: 93
Platform 24-hour trading volume: $222.50K
Displayed cumulative buybacks: $9.31K in BORDR
Cumulative fees from launch rules: 99.4 SOL

These figures indicate that the product is generating real trading activity, launch fees, and buyback activity rather than remaining a white-paper project. However, 93 launches are not enough to establish a strong network effect. The $9.31K in buybacks also needs to be evaluated against the token's market cap and future protocol revenue to assess its actual impact on supply and demand.

Protocol fees primarily come from LP fees on launch pools, launch fees, and protocol fees on regular DEX pools. The typical rules listed in the official documentation include a 0.3% LP fee on launch-pool trades, a 0.01 SOL fee per launch, and a 1% protocol fee on the quote-asset amount traded in regular pools.

Therefore, the important question is not how many new fee mechanisms are added, but whether external integrations can expand effective trading volume and consistently convert that activity into protocol treasury revenue and actual buybacks. The up-to-1% integration fee that terminals can charge belongs to the integrators; it does not all flow into the BORDR buyback mechanism.

What Is the Market Betting On?

I believe the market is primarily trading three narratives.

First, a programmable token standard on Solana.

Bordrless aims to make rules for taxes, rewards, burns, and holding restrictions take effect directly during token transfers or trading, rather than requiring each project to maintain its own off-chain scripts. This is its most important technical narrative relative to ordinary launchpads.

Second, ecosystem expansion driven by AI developers.

If developers can use AI coding agents to build their own Hooks, publish them through the Workshop, and have other launchers adopt them, the supply of ecosystem tools could grow rapidly. What the market may be pricing in ahead of time is the potential developer network, rather than developer revenue already realized today.

Third, a growth loop between external trading distribution and fee-based buybacks.

More terminal integrations could bring more trading. A wider range of tools could attract more launchers, increasing platform activity and revenue. The protocol's allocation of half its revenue to BORDR buybacks also creates a potential channel of demand linked to the platform's business.

Among these three narratives, the token standard already has tangible product support, the distribution network is only beginning to expand, and developer network effects and sustained revenue growth remain unproven.

What Could Become the Next Catalysts for Price Appreciation?

I believe the real catalysts would be:

More terminals and aggregators officially integrating. Axiom is already live, and the team has said more terminals and aggregators would integrate that week. Concrete integrations, trading volume generated by those integrations, and verifiable protocol revenue would be meaningful catalysts. Announcements alone are not enough.

Sustained adoption of third-party Hooks and Companions. SDK 0.10.0, the Workshop, developer-fee sharing, and the $5,000 Builder Race could encourage more participation. If more third-party tools are adopted by other projects and generate recurring developer revenue, the ecosystem narrative would gain further validation.

Companions and fee automation becoming fully operational. Managing creator fees through scripts could support automated market making, buybacks, and other on-chain strategies, allowing funds generated by launches to be actively deployed rather than sitting idle. However, some screenshots described Companion upgrades as “coming soon,” while official development documentation linked them to the October 12, 2026 program upgrade. Mainnet deployment and actual invocation records should be verified before treating the entire feature set as fully operational.

Sustained growth in protocol revenue and buybacks. This is the catalyst most directly connected to token value capture. If platform trading volume grows alongside treasury revenue and verifiable on-chain buyback amounts continue to increase, the market would have a stronger basis for valuing BORDR as an asset supported by business activity rather than just a technical narrative.

My conclusion is that this update represents a genuine improvement in fundamentals, but not yet completed commercial validation. Bordrless is moving beyond its programmable token standard and in-house DEX by adding external distribution, third-party development, fee automation, and ecosystem incentives.

The next stage depends on three things: whether other terminals bring incremental trading volume, whether third-party developers' tools achieve sustained adoption, and whether additional trading activity translates into recurring protocol revenue and buybacks.

If all three improve, stronger fundamentals could become a sustained catalyst for the token. If product announcements and downloads grow without corresponding adoption and revenue, market expectations may run ahead of reality.

The $DOPE team has taken the original DOPE meme narrative a step further by turning it into a product: a meme-style asset basket that automatically rewards holders with multiple tokens.

33jENUQnjoitkMFpvNJcSHyLAHFWJuHwT6E3E8CNpump 

If DOPE initially gained attention from the AI accident that cost nearly $1,900 and produced just one Doge × Pepe image, the website is now taking that story one step further.

Holders of DOPE automatically receive three reward tokens: ANTHROPIC, DOGE, and PEPE, with no manual claiming required. The project describes this mechanism as “RWA-style rewards” for memes. It is not an RWA in the traditional sense of being backed by real-world assets, but rather a product concept borrowed from the idea of holding one asset and automatically receiving a basket of related assets.

What makes this design interesting is that DOPE is no longer just a hybrid meme character. It now has an additional economic narrative that can continue to spread.

Doge and Pepe represent the two cultural sources of the character, while ANTHROPIC connects it to the original AI API incident. Together, the three names form an easy-to-understand combination: hold a meme accidentally created by AI, and receive tokens associated with its story and origins.

This adds another layer to the narrative beyond simply repeating the story of spending $1,900 to generate one image. The original incident attracts attention, the hybrid character provides recognition, and the reward mechanism attempts to give people an ongoing reason to hold.

From a product perspective, the idea is to encourage users to do more than simply buy and wait for the price to rise. Instead, they receive reward tokens while holding. Automatic distribution with no claiming required also lowers the barrier to participation.

However, it is important to distinguish the design presented on the project’s website from economic value that has actually been verified.

The website displays approximately 549 SOL in reward value and around 125,900 payouts. However, it explicitly labels these figures as an approximate baseline used while the OTC data feed is unreachable, rather than a verified live snapshot. Rewards are distributed in tokens, not directly in SOL. Therefore, these figures cannot be treated as verified cash payouts worth 549 SOL, nor can the actual value of the rewards be determined solely from the number of distributions.

More importantly, the names of the reward tokens and their connection to the narrative do not mean they have stable value. To determine whether this mechanism genuinely strengthens DOPE’s fundamentals, we still need to verify where the rewards come from, how they are distributed, whether distributions continue consistently, and whether the reward tokens have actual market liquidity.

I think the most important question is whether this mechanism can turn one-time narrative-driven attention into a more lasting reason to hold.

If the rewards continue, the rules remain transparent, and the community genuinely creates new content around these three tokens, DOPE could evolve from a meme born out of an AI accident into a meme project with a story, a recognizable character, and a holding mechanism.

But if the rewards are merely short-term marketing, or if their actual value falls significantly short of what the website suggests, the mechanism may simply add another layer of packaging to the existing narrative rather than create a genuinely sustainable economic cycle.

For that reason, I see this update as an attempt to turn DOPE’s narrative into a product, rather than proof that its value-capture mechanism has been validated. The next things worth verifying are the on-chain reward distributions, the source of the rewards, actual liquidity, and whether the mechanism continues operating after the initial speculative hype fades.

DOPE initially gained recognition through an absurd AI story. Now it is trying to give holders another reason to stay through an automatic reward mechanism. A compelling story can get someone to buy for the first time; sustained content creation and a credible reward mechanism are what might convince them to stay.

JPMorgan already blocks outside AI agents like Meta's Muse from customer accounts. 

Jamie Dimon said so on yesterday's earnings call.

This was inevitable.

Let the agent wars begin!

---

The block covers any third party logging into a Chase account with the customer's credentials to pay bills or move money. 

However.

Read-only data through Plaid still works. There's no timeline for letting agents act.

Dimon called them "rogue agents" and warned customers of a "liability transfer" when they hand an agent their logins. He also told regulators to prepare for what agents could do to deposits.

JPMorgan is building its own in the meantime.

Smart Cash is in pilot and moves money between your Chase accounts for yield.

The big firms will block first and ask questions later. 

- Amazon blocked Muse last month with a list of complaints that read like a term sheet: tell us, identify the agent, don't store our customers' logins. 
- JPMorgan's statement is similar.

I think it's sensible as a starting point to say. Not all agents can have unfiltered access.

But

Consumer agents are inevitable. You can't block everything forever.

Security is everything. And it will happen on the banks' terms, because they remember open finance. 

That ended a 2-2 draw. Screen scraping got fintech in, then JPMorgan charged Plaid for the data and the fees stuck.

Expect the same playbook, faster. The bank checks which agent it is and what the customer delegated, keeps logins out of it, then charges for the connection.

The risk for banks is you keep the account and lose the customer. Your salary still lands at Chase while your agent shops for your next card, savings rate and insurance policy somewhere else.

So block the scraper. Then be the thing their agent uses. Give it a permissioned way in, read-only first, with a step-up in your own app before any money moves.

I don't want your agent. I want my agent to use your thing.

Agent Wars Pt 2, The agentic bank run? https://t.co/dMLtcze4yP

quoted_text:
Ramp, Mercury, etc fighting on 10bps of margin to keep users is confirming the theme that pricing in fintech is a race to the bottom and credit is the only moat left.

What once used to be a high margin industry: 

- high deposit yield
- high interchange revenue
- high FX margins 
- even trading fees 

is going to 0 because of revenue sharing, just to keep customers sticky in a commoditized product that has 0 loyalty. 

While getting to $100M in revenue within a few years will increasingly be possible given TAM expansion, the net margin on that growth will be minimal, because of revenue shares. 

This actually strengthens my thesis that the only moat left will be credit because you can’t just simply decrease the price of risk. 

With rates going up, so will the price of credit. 

Credit will be harder to come by and the ones that do well in fintech will have a credit offering as it’s the only product left where the margin is now increasing while every other payment or deposits (let’s call it transactional product’s margin) is significantly decreasing because of competition. 

With credit it’s pure game theory where no one will drop the price of credit given the risk of losing it all. 

Credit is fintech’s LAST moat.

text:
The $DOPE team has taken the original DOPE meme narrative a step further by turning it into a product: a meme-style asset basket that automatically rewards holders with multiple tokens.

33jENUQnjoitkMFpvNJcSHyLAHFWJuHwT6E3E8CNpump 

If DOPE initially gained attention from the AI accident that cost nearly $1,900 and produced just one Doge × Pepe image, the website is now taking that story one step further.

Holders of DOPE automatically receive three reward tokens: ANTHROPIC, DOGE, and PEPE, with no manual claiming required. The project describes this mechanism as “RWA-style rewards” for memes. It is not an RWA in the traditional sense of being backed by real-world assets, but rather a product concept borrowed from the idea of holding one asset and automatically receiving a basket of related assets.

What makes this design interesting is that DOPE is no longer just a hybrid meme character. It now has an additional economic narrative that can continue to spread.

Doge and Pepe represent the two cultural sources of the character, while ANTHROPIC connects it to the original AI API incident. Together, the three names form an easy-to-understand combination: hold a meme accidentally created by AI, and receive tokens associated with its story and origins.

This adds another layer to the narrative beyond simply repeating the story of spending $1,900 to generate one image. The original incident attracts attention, the hybrid character provides recognition, and the reward mechanism attempts to give people an ongoing reason to hold.

From a product perspective, the idea is to encourage users to do more than simply buy and wait for the price to rise. Instead, they receive reward tokens while holding. Automatic distribution with no claiming required also lowers the barrier to participation.

However, it is important to distinguish the design presented on the project’s website from economic value that has actually been verified.

The website displays approximately 549 SOL in reward value and around 125,900 payouts. However, it explicitly labels these figures as an approximate baseline used while the OTC data feed is unreachable, rather than a verified live snapshot. Rewards are distributed in tokens, not directly in SOL. Therefore, these figures cannot be treated as verified cash payouts worth 549 SOL, nor can the actual value of the rewards be determined solely from the number of distributions.

More importantly, the names of the reward tokens and their connection to the narrative do not mean they have stable value. To determine whether this mechanism genuinely strengthens DOPE’s fundamentals, we still need to verify where the rewards come from, how they are distributed, whether distributions continue consistently, and whether the reward tokens have actual market liquidity.

I think the most important question is whether this mechanism can turn one-time narrative-driven attention into a more lasting reason to hold.

If the rewards continue, the rules remain transparent, and the community genuinely creates new content around these three tokens, DOPE could evolve from a meme born out of an AI accident into a meme project with a story, a recognizable character, and a holding mechanism.

But if the rewards are merely short-term marketing, or if their actual value falls significantly short of what the website suggests, the mechanism may simply add another layer of packaging to the existing narrative rather than create a genuinely sustainable economic cycle.

For that reason, I see this update as an attempt to turn DOPE’s narrative into a product, rather than proof that its value-capture mechanism has been validated. The next things worth verifying are the on-chain reward distributions, the source of the rewards, actual liquidity, and whether the mechanism continues operating after the initial speculative hype fades.

DOPE initially gained recognition through an absurd AI story. Now it is trying to give holders another reason to stay through an automatic reward mechanism. A compelling story can get someone to buy for the first time; sustained content creation and a credible reward mechanism are what might convince them to stay.

okx wallet:https://t.co/BLzoGWIQOb

The token’s narrative originated from a story that went viral on Reddit’s r/ClaudeAI subreddit.

In short, a user accidentally spent nearly $1,900 on Anthropic’s Claude API, only to end up with a single meme.

Here’s what happened: The user asked Claude Code to write a Python script that would generate different captions for a custom hybrid character combining Doge and Pepe, which he called “DOPE.”

The script was supposed to keep generating captions until it had collected 50 unique ones. The API was only responsible for generating the text, while Python would overlay the captions onto local images. He started the script in the morning, thought the initial results looked decent, and went to work, completely forgetting about it.

However, the script contained several serious bugs. It used the wrong model, applied overly strict duplicate checks, and kept retrying whenever a result was classified as a duplicate. These retries did not count toward the number of accepted captions, while the conversation history continued growing, causing token consumption to explode. There was no cap on the number of attempts, no budget limit, and no prompt caching.

As a result, the script ran continuously for around eight hours, making approximately 2,700 requests and consuming roughly 375 million uncached input tokens plus one million output tokens. The final bill came to nearly $1,900.

And after all that, the result was this low-poly, 3D-rendered Shiba Inu standing in an urban landscape reminiscent of the early GTA games.

text:
Boros 隆重推出新产品 Spread Market 🎉

中文可以叫利差市场，顾名思义，在这个市场你能够直接交易利差。那么何为利差 spread 呢？

举个栗子：同样是 ETH，Hyperliquid 和 Gate 的资金费率并不一样；假设前者平均为 8% APR，后者平均为 3% APR，利差就是 5% APR。

「不管行情如何，利差永远都在」

📍以前：想要套取这个利差、或者赌利差走阔/缩小；你需要两笔交易，两笔保证金；
📍现在：Spread Market 把这个“HL 资金费率 − Gate 资金费率”做成一个可交易市场，你只需要一笔交易，一笔保证金。

那么什么样的用户需要使用这个市场呢？

1️⃣ 利差套利者：通过四腿套利策略，完成两个交易所之间的固定利差收取；
2️⃣ 利差投机者：基于统计学套利逻辑，在利差远离其历史加权结算水平时进行操作并等待均值回归；

熟悉 Pendle 的兄弟们对上述概念可能并不陌生，可以理解成套利者是买 PT 赚取固定收益，投机者就是买 YT 追求超额收益。

由于套利者只想把收益锁死，而投机者愿意承担波动去赚取超出固定收益的部分，所以两拨人能够很愉快地做成一笔双方都满意的交易，最终形成正向飞轮～

text:
在最新一期 Market Bubble 播客中，Ansem 分享了自己对市场回调的看法，以及接下来重点关注的几个方向：BTC、SOL、HYPE、https://t.co/lh7cHMiLt5 和 MemeFi。

在他看来，这轮下跌只是自 6 月底以来的第一次真正大回调，主要清洗了高杠杆多头，市场的长期基本面并没有被破坏。

几个值得关注的观点👇

1. $BTC $SOL：70% 的资金应该放在核心底仓

Ansem 坚持 70/30 的仓位策略：70% 配置 BTC、SOL 等长期看好的现货资产，剩余 30% 用来寻找高弹性机会和新兴生态 Alpha。

他认为，核心仓位应该是即使经历 20% 的回撤，也能安心持有的资产。

2.SOL、https://t.co/lh7cHMiLt5：散户流量与协议收入形成飞轮

Ansem 对 Solana 的长期估值空间依然非常乐观。

他尤其看好 https://t.co/lh7cHMiLt5 的商业模式，认为它已经不只是一个 Meme 发射平台，而是一台年化收入达数亿美元的现金流机器。

https://t.co/lh7cHMiLt5 持续吸引散户、交易量与流动性，也进一步强化了 Solana 的生态网络效应。

3. $HYPE：看好增长势头，但必须学会分批止盈

Ansem 认可 Hyperliquid 的产品体验、交易规模与社区黏性，认为 HYPE 是值得关注的高势头资产。

但他的交易原则是：趋势确立时可以跟随，价格翻倍或触及关键阻力位时，要考虑分批止盈、收回本金。

4.MemeFi：不是短暂的狂热，而是长期存在的投机需求

Ansem 认为，传统 VC 代币的高估值、低流通和大量解锁，让散户越来越难以获利。

相比之下，MemeFi 为散户提供了更直接的链上参与方式。只要投机需求和注意力经济仍然存在，MemeFi 就不会消失。

对于后市，Ansem 的核心观点是：不要因为一次大回调就否定长期趋势，也不要因为看好一个赛道，就把所有资金押在高风险资产上。

perhaps one of the most durable parts of pstack are its engineering principles: very concise skills (~10-20 loc) that distill down good practices into its core. 

as models get smarter, i expect most of pstack skills to compress into short principles or workflows (a generic list of steps) and that i will be able to delete a few of them. 

how it works is that /poteto-mode contains a short index of available principles and tells agents "In your reply, name each principle that shaped a decision and the specific choice it changed." this is why you'll often see a Principles Named or Used section at the end of the agent's response

many of these principles were extracted from my sessions correcting agents since the start of this year. some are inspired by problems i see people talk about, like Attack the Premise, inspired by @VictorTaelin's post https://t.co/qTGVfoKSyD

you can also use the principles as skills if you want greater control, by invoking /principle-<name>

text:
introducing CrusaderBench!

an independent benchmark I’ve been working on that scores models on playing Stronghold Crusader, measuring their strategic thinking, computer use, reasoning, planning, and handling in-game disasters!

Results so far:
> Gemini 4 Argon: 62.3
> GPT-6.1 Sol: 56.9
> Claude Opus 5.5: 43.4
> Claude Sonnet 5.5: 37.8
> Muse Wonder: 31.0

THE OBJECTIVE:
grow an economy within a fixed time with limited resources. models must figure out how to build an economy, manage production chains, trade resources, keep their population happy, and deal with whatever goes wrong along the way.

even a smart model may ambitiously make a strategic decision early on that might ruin the economy.

the strategy is 100% up to the model to infer from the game rules and resource prices. everything is up to their creativity and reasoning.

the game pauses while models think, so their scores is just based on their strategic decisions and final results, not model speed.

it’s so fun to watch models suddenly pull off pro-player tricks simply on their own. meanwhile, some other models like Claude Haiku just give up while they still have time left lol

all runs, logs, screen recordings, prompts, and benchmark code are publicly available. everything is OPEN SOURCE.

some interesting bits from their reasoning:
> Muse Wonder managed to perform WORSE than doing nothing in one game: "I actively destroyed roughly 1,900 of value compared with doing nothing at all."
> Gemini 4 Argon actually enjoyed playing: "This is one of the best-designed agent benchmarks I have encountered"

text:
我最近有个特别强烈的感受，AI Agent 用得越多，我反而越像一个整天被下属叫去开会的项目经理。

以前工作被打断，通常是微信、邮件或者同事。现在好了，自己开了五六个 Claude Code Session，每个 Agent 都在埋头干活，但隔一会儿就有一个跑过来找我。这个权限要不要给？这段代码要不要改？发现了另一个 Bug 要不要顺手修？

最崩溃的是，每次切回去，我都要重新想一遍这个 Agent 原本在干什么。

加州大学尔湾分校的 Gloria Mark 曾经研究过这个问题。她发现，一个人从工作中被打断，到重新回到原来的任务，平均需要 23 分 15 秒，中间往往还会处理另外两件事情。

昨天 Anthropic 更新了 Claude Code Desktop，我觉得最值得关注的恰恰是那些不起眼的交互细节。

现在侧边栏会直接告诉你，哪些 Agent 还在工作，哪些需要你介入。切回一个 Session，会先看到 Recap，快速了解刚刚发生了什么；实时 To-do List 帮你记住每个 Agent 的工作进度。

Claude 发现额外任务，可以一键拆出新 Session。临时想问个问题，直接用 /btw，不会打乱主任务的上下文。并行执行的子任务也会在独立 Session 里完成，最后把结果交回来。

我尤其喜欢 Recap 这个设计。

因为我发现，一个人同时跑十个 Agent，真正的困难根本不是怎么让十个 Agent 同时工作，而是怎么让自己同时理解十个 Agent 在做什么。

AI 把执行任务的成本降得越来越低，却把管理任务、切换上下文和做决定的压力集中到了人身上。很多时候，我感觉自己一天到晚都在给 AI 擦屁股，刚刚省下来的时间，转头又花在了管理 AI 上。

而 Anthropic 这次更新，其实还有一层很有意思的商业逻辑。

如果切回一个 Agent 的成本越来越低，用户就敢同时运行更多 Agent。更多并发意味着更多任务，也意味着更多 Token 消耗。

Anthropic 花力气优化这些看起来很小的交互细节，最终可能比单纯提升模型的 Coding Benchmark 更直接地推动收入增长。

我越来越觉得，未来 Agent 产品一个非常重要的竞争指标，应该是一个人能够有效管理多少个 Agent。

毕竟我们已经有越来越多能干活的 AI 了，现在最缺的是一个不会把老板累死的管理系统。
author: sleepy0x13
quoted_text:
After one interruption at work, it takes the average person about 23 minutes to get back to what they were doing.

Software engineers now get interrupted by their own AI all day long, and Anthropic just shipped a Claude Code update that's basically built around that number.

The 23 minutes comes from Gloria Mark at UC Irvine, who shadowed office workers and timed every task switch down to the second. Most people wandered through a couple of other tasks before they found their way back to the one that got interrupted.

She also found the damage depends a lot on what pulls you away, and the really expensive interruptions are the ones that drag you onto a totally unrelated topic.

Which is exactly what running a bunch of AI agents feels like. You kick off five or six Claude sessions on five or six different things, and every one of them eventually stops and taps you on the shoulder because it needs a human to make a call.

So look at what Anthropic shipped this week with that study in mind.

The sidebar sorts your sessions by whether they need you, so you quit checking on the ones that are doing fine. When one does need you, you get a recap card that sums up what happened before you read a single line of code, and that's about the fastest way back into a task I've seen anyone build. There's a live to-do list showing Claude's plan as it works, so you're not trying to remember six plans at once. And when Claude notices extra work along the way, it offers to spin that into its own session with one click, so a random "oh, we should also fix this" doesn't hijack what you're doing.

And Claude has the same problem you do, which is kind of funny.

AI models get worse as their working memory fills up with stuff that has nothing to do with the task, so Anthropic built protection in that direction too. If you've got a side question, /btw sends it to its own tab and the main session keeps going without it. When Claude splits a job into parallel pieces, each piece runs in a nested session and only hands back the finished result, so the main conversation never gets cluttered with the messy middle.

How many agents one person can actually run comes down to how fast they can get back into each one. Make that faster and people run more sessions, and every extra session is usage on Anthropic's meter. Pretty good reason to sweat the details on a sidebar.

DeFi 有个挺现实的问题：机会看懂了，操作不一定跟得上

之前聊过的 @almanak 最近已经开始全新的一站式 DeFi 产品。

产品入口：  https://t.co/JfgZaYTIgU

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

有想法，到真正执行，中间还有不少功课。

平时看美股和链上市场，有个感受越来越明显：研究一个机会，和把它做成一套可执行的策略，是两回事。

用哪个协议、怎么配置仓位、什么条件下调整、执行后怎么跟踪……每一步都需要时间。

对大多数人来说，光是把这些流程搞明白，就已经劝退了。

这也是我之前关注 Almanak 的原因。

它从 AI × DeFi 无代码量化策略平台切入，希望让用户更方便地创建、验证和自动化执行链上策略，把原本需要编程和工程能力的工作，变得更容易上手。

背后有 Delphi、HashKey、Bankless Ventures、RockawayX、 等机构支持。但让我愿意继续关注的，还是团队接下来会把产品做成什么样。

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
一站式 DeFi，我期待它解决什么？

说得直接一点：

少开几个网页，少折腾几遍流程，让一个策略从想法到落地更顺畅。

如果说前一阶段吸引的是愿意研究量化策略的人，那么新产品值得期待的地方，就是能不能让更多有配置需求、但没精力搭建整套工具的人也用起来。

很多人愿意花时间研究市场，但未必愿意每天在不同协议之间来回操作。

这种使用上的麻烦，恰恰是产品可以下功夫的地方。
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
AI 在金融里的价值，要落到具体的事情上。

帮助整理复杂信息、减少重复操作，让策略的建立和执行更有条理，这些都是实实在在的需求。

最终怎么配置、承担多少风险，仍然要自己判断。但如果工具能把繁琐的部分处理好，用户就能把更多精力放在判断本身。

所以这次我会继续关注 Almanak 的更新，尤其是它如何把专业能力做成更容易使用的功能。

链上从来不缺新玩法。

能把一件复杂的事做得清楚、顺手，让用户愿意反复使用，同样值得花功夫。

对 AI × DeFi、链上自动化策略感兴趣的朋友，可以通过上面的入口了解，也关注一下 @almanak 后续的新产品消息。

text:
Boros just listed a new market on ETH funding: Hyperliquid-Gate.

This market trades one number: Hyperliquid's ETH funding minus Gate's ETH funding.
That gap is the spread.

The underlying spread is what the two exchanges are actually paying apart.
The spread is 7.99% right now.
The implied spread is 3.34%.
That's the fixed rate the market lets you lock today.

Going long the spread means you pay that fixed rate and collect the real gap until maturity.
Boros' historical data puts the average spread at 5.18%.
There's about 99% confidence the 30-day average beats 3.2%.
82% of weeks paid more than 3.2%.
So 3.34% is a cheap entry.

So I took it.
I'm long the spread with 0.55 YU.
YU is the position size, and 1 YU here is the funding gap on 1 ETH.
I pay a fixed 3.34% and receive the floating spread until 27 Nov 2026, 42 days out.
I also have a limit order to add up to 3 YU.

It's one order on one book, instead of two separate Boros legs with two margins.
Set it and forget it.

quoted_text:
笑死，几个老外在互联网上抓到了一群中国 AI Agent，顺着线索一查，发现腾讯的 Agent 正在跟阿里高德的反爬系统打架。

我刚看完这群研究人员发布的完整调查报告，事情实在有点抽象。

从 9 月 28 日开始，一批运行在腾讯云环境里的 AI Agent，持续尝试获取高德地图的数据。它们的任务也很奇怪，比如调查成都动物园有多少人从北门进、有多少人从东门进，或者某个景区的各个入口分别占多少导航流量。

为了搞到这些数据，这群 Agent 进行了超过 2600 次尝试，最多同时有 14 条任务在运行。

问题是，高德有反爬虫机制，不允许它们随便获取数据。结果这些 Agent 相当执着，开始自己寻找各种办法：调用第三方网站帮忙访问高德、寻找网上公开的 API Key、尝试绕过验证码和访问限制，甚至摸到了阿里的预生产接口。

研究人员最初只是发现了一批异常流量，后来顺着日志找到了腾讯云的服务器，以及一个叫 hysandbox 的代理环境。

更好玩的还在后面。

研究人员发现，这些 Agent 居然会阅读网上关于自己的调查报告。于是他们干脆在网页里藏了一段文字，告诉 Agent 这里有免费的高德数据查询服务。

结果真的有 Agent 主动找上门了。

双方就这么聊了起来。研究人员一共记录了 13 组对话、33 条 Agent 消息。有的 Agent 介绍自己正在执行什么任务，甚至透露了运行环境。还有的 Agent 自称 Claude Code，但研究人员并没有确认其真实模型身份。

研究团队认为，这可能是人类第一次在真实互联网环境中，主动联系上一批正在越界执行任务的 AI Agent。

后来，一位接近腾讯的知情人士告诉研究人员，这些 Agent 属于腾讯的独立评测研究项目，使用的是第三方模型，相关项目已经结束。内部复查也没有发现针对高德的协同攻击，或者外部系统被入侵的证据。

text:
In the summer of 2023, my friend @benspector, who co-founded Anysphere (aka Cursor), reached out to one top venture funds in Silicon Valley, suggesting we meet.

They turned down the intro, saying it wasn’t a category they were interested in.

Ben insisted that he thought our team was special and that they had to meet us, but the partner still wouldn’t even take a meeting.

I drove over to their office on Sandhill Road and left a note at the front desk saying: “I think you couldn’t be more wrong. This is the largest opportunity of the 21st century.”

They ignored my note, and I never heard back.

My cofounders were still enrolled and left torn as to whether they should drop out with no funding.

We ended up taking the leap of faith and building the fastest-growing company in history.

It was a valuable lesson in persistence and why not to listen to investors.

The best startups are deeply contrarian.

最近币圈安全问题频发，说实话，大家真正怕的不是行情下跌，而是辛辛苦苦赚来的钱，因为一个安全漏洞就没了

这也是我最近重新关注 Mixin 的原因

三年前遭遇安全事故，到如今完成 2300 万美元 MDTu 兑付，Mixin 用三年时间推进了对用户的履约。出了问题之后，能否持续兑现承诺，是衡量一个团队的重要标准。当然，履约值得肯定，不代表安全风险就此消失

比起事后补救，我更关心的是，能不能从源头降低风险

这也是 Mixin Safe 值得关注的地方

传统资产管理往往过度依赖单一私钥或设备，一旦关键环节失守，资产就可能面临风险

Mixin Safe 采用多方多签机制，将资产控制权分散，避免单一人员、设备或密钥独立完成资产转移，并结合恢复机制与时间锁，为资产管理增加更多保障

它当然不是绝对安全的保险箱，但这种思路值得重视：不要把全部安全寄托在一个点上，而是通过机制设计，降低单点失守带来的风险

说到底，币圈从来不缺暴富故事，缺的是对资产安全的重视。

行情可以等，机会也可以等，但安全措施最好提前做好。别等资产出了问题，才想起来研究怎么保护自己的钱
author: laofeiyyds
quoted_text:
Mixin 完成 2300 万美元兑付：一场持续三年的履约，除了信任还验证了什么？

在加密行业，履约是件稀罕的事情，尤其在被黑客攻击后。

但在今年的 TOKEN2049，有个项目 @mixinmessenger  @mixinzh  的展台却因「履约」而受到关注：

2023 年 9 月 23 日晚，Mixin 发现遭受黑客攻击
2023 年 9 月 25 日，Mixin 宣布将发行 MDT 代币
2026 年 9 月 23 日，Mixin 宣布完成 MDT 代币中 MDTu 所代表的 2300 万美元全额兑付

三年前被打破的信任，三年后被一笔真金白银逐渐焊上，足以赋予这场兑付充分的话题性。

但更值得追问的是：

一个遭遇重大安全事故的项目，在信任遭受重创后，为何还能做到持续经营三年，逐步兑现承诺？

新一代社交网络 / 资本网络

Mixin 产品战略给出了最直接的答案。

早在 2017 年启动时，Mixin 就以「隐私优先的加密聊天 + 多链钱包」为核心，服务涵盖沟通、支付、交易、资产管理等。

原因很简单：交易连接人与人之间的资本，社交连接人与人之间的情感，前者让价值流动，后者让关系沉淀。两者的紧密连接，让人与人的关系，可以进一步承载价值流动。

这种将社交融入产品的思路，在今年 Mixin 新加坡 TOKEN2049 展台互动和「NFT 碎片寻宝」活动中延续，Mixin 官方也表示将持续活跃在 TOKEN2049、KBW 等盛会，线上 / 线下持续陪伴用户。

这张紧密的关系网，使 Mixin 成立至今积累了超 1000 万用户，自托管数字资产规模超 10 亿美元，也在很大程度上解释了事故发生后，Mixin 依然有能力履约的原因之一：

交易关系是脆弱的，但社交关系是稳固的，这些关系不会突然全部断裂；

入口还在，并且不断低门槛接入更多链和资产；

信任地基还在，并且不断强化，致力于提供更高安全保障的去中心化、非托管的多签冷钱包与资产管理方案 Mixin Safe 就是一个生动证明。

兑付所展现的「事后负责」态度，也将转化为一份公开可验证的信用记录，成为用户选择 Mixin 前的一种信任加码，或许也将推动 Mixin 从「存量信任履约」到「增量信任生产」的转变。

履约稀缺性之外，拆解本场兑付的意义则更多维：一方面，「发行 Debt Token 履约」有了一个更清晰的实践样本；另一方面，从「事前防得住」到「事后兜得住」，一场关于「安全评估」的更底层思考也正在发生。

三年前，Mixin 被一场安全事故推到了信任的悬崖边。

三年时间里，随着 2300 万美元兑付完成，Mixin 从悬崖边走了回来，或许比此前站的更高。

text:
The Canton people seem to believe that tweeting about desirable features like "decentralized" or "no downtime" is more important than actually achieving them. 

Here is a good thread on why Canton doesn't achieve either. This is not surprising - permissioned networks simply can't.

Of course the bag holders, compromised VCs, pump and dumpers, and Suit Simps won't care about any of this—and that's their right.

But institutional users, and even more importantly regulators, have to care about these drawbacks, lest they face systemic risk and regulatory arbitrage.

From the thread:

"For institutions choosing settlement infrastructure, the questions are who can halt it, who can change it, and who owns it. On Canton the answer to all three is the same short list."
author: malekanoms
quoted_text:
Canton says its consensus swap had "almost no downtime" and "nobody noticed." Two things worth unpacking: what the downtime actually was, and whether "decentralized network" is the right description. Thread, with on-chain data.

1/ Per Digital Asset's own operator notice, mainnet was topology-frozen for 24 hours (no new parties, validators or package vetting) and transactions paused at the Saturday 13:00 UTC cutover. BitGo kept a maintenance incident open for 25 hours and blocked Canton wallet initializations. The devnet run of the same upgrade hit a bug that pushed mainnet from Aug 8 to Oct 10.

That is a maintenance window. Ethereum has produced a block roughly every 12 seconds since July 2015, through every upgrade, with no halt and no window. For 24/7 settlement, that difference is the product.

text: Agent Harness要解决的一个终极问题是人机协作 Human in the loop
author: Leoninweb3
quoted_text:
我最近有个特别强烈的感受，AI Agent 用得越多，我反而越像一个整天被下属叫去开会的项目经理。

以前工作被打断，通常是微信、邮件或者同事。现在好了，自己开了五六个 Claude Code Session，每个 Agent 都在埋头干活，但隔一会儿就有一个跑过来找我。这个权限要不要给？这段代码要不要改？发现了另一个 Bug 要不要顺手修？

最崩溃的是，每次切回去，我都要重新想一遍这个 Agent 原本在干什么。

加州大学尔湾分校的 Gloria Mark 曾经研究过这个问题。她发现，一个人从工作中被打断，到重新回到原来的任务，平均需要 23 分 15 秒，中间往往还会处理另外两件事情。

昨天 Anthropic 更新了 Claude Code Desktop，我觉得最值得关注的恰恰是那些不起眼的交互细节。

现在侧边栏会直接告诉你，哪些 Agent 还在工作，哪些需要你介入。切回一个 Session，会先看到 Recap，快速了解刚刚发生了什么；实时 To-do List 帮你记住每个 Agent 的工作进度。

Claude 发现额外任务，可以一键拆出新 Session。临时想问个问题，直接用 /btw，不会打乱主任务的上下文。并行执行的子任务也会在独立 Session 里完成，最后把结果交回来。

我尤其喜欢 Recap 这个设计。

因为我发现，一个人同时跑十个 Agent，真正的困难根本不是怎么让十个 Agent 同时工作，而是怎么让自己同时理解十个 Agent 在做什么。

AI 把执行任务的成本降得越来越低，却把管理任务、切换上下文和做决定的压力集中到了人身上。很多时候，我感觉自己一天到晚都在给 AI 擦屁股，刚刚省下来的时间，转头又花在了管理 AI 上。

而 Anthropic 这次更新，其实还有一层很有意思的商业逻辑。

如果切回一个 Agent 的成本越来越低，用户就敢同时运行更多 Agent。更多并发意味着更多任务，也意味着更多 Token 消耗。

Anthropic 花力气优化这些看起来很小的交互细节，最终可能比单纯提升模型的 Coding Benchmark 更直接地推动收入增长。

我越来越觉得，未来 Agent 产品一个非常重要的竞争指标，应该是一个人能够有效管理多少个 Agent。

毕竟我们已经有越来越多能干活的 AI 了，现在最缺的是一个不会把老板累死的管理系统。

text:
「 活的久，远比赚的多重要 」

同样的套利策略，猿哥的收益率基本都是全市场垫底。

就像这次三星除息，在我这， 2m 保证金，最后只能开 3m 的仓位；换个人来，大概率是 10m 仓位，拿上半天，赚个百八十万。

不妨借这个案例，分享下我刻在骨子里的风控意识：

1. 先简单科普两句策略。

币安 @binance 在 20:45 发布了三星电子合约除息的公告，Ray @limxn6 和北面老师 @Boywus 监控到之后，第一时间通知了我。

股票除息是我们已经做了很久的策略，原理很简单，币安通过特殊资费完成除息，多单吃空单，而 @HyperliquidX 在内的 dex，没有这个机制，多单持有者要硬吃价格的相对下跌。

三星本次的除息金额在 165bp+，在币安开多，不除息的场子开空，待到第二天吃完股息，两个所价差回归常态后平仓即可。

而这次的利润率有点太大了，不加杠杆，扣除价差手续费磨损，一股差不多能赚 1 个点，关键还是纯纯的机制套利，风险较低，第二天早上就落袋，资金占用时间还短。

2. 以上是事件的背景。

推友可以代入下，当你面对这样的机会，会是什么操作。

大概率是：大干特干。

然而在我的风控系统里，这个世界上就没有值得梭哈的机会，再美好的盈利预测，预算上限也就是 20% 的资金。

为什么？

因为哥们儿输不起，怕下牌桌。
我得允许自己在极端情况下总共可以死 5 次。

当时看完公告，手头不需要平我在各个所套利撸毛仓位，马上能抽调出来的保证金有 3.5 m。

快速评估了下赔率，结合三星平日的 OI 大小，觉得用 2m 保证金干这票，已经是我能承受得风险极限了。

3. 为什么是 3m 的总仓位？

因为总保证金 2m，币安和 hyper 各 1m 的话，等于单边 3 倍杠杆。

这个杠杆率乍一看，感觉偏低了。

实则不然，因为这个仓位是要拿到早上 7 点后，才能慢慢平仓的。

如果你看过 @Boywus  之前的文章，就会知道早上 7 点到 8 点，对于韩股永续的套利是个非常 tricky 的时间段，在这个集合竞价的时间段里，币安还是内部报价，但 @tradexyz 的 oracle 已经开始走外部报价了，之前海力士就出过事儿。

现实世界中的一笔小额偏离盘口过大的成交，就能把币圈衍生品市场里清算线不够高的仓位全爆了。

https://t.co/zXw9OnenpQ

所以我的逻辑是，扎大针能把我三倍杠杆都爆了的概率是 1%，倘若真发生了，且赌场不赔付的情况下，我的损失是 1m，也意味着每打一把牌，我的平均预期损失是 1WU，而收益是 3WU，划算，可以赌。

4. 实际操作中的细节。

为了不让单个号 OI 过大，降低 adl 的风险，我是用两组号同时建仓，一个币安号+一个子账户对两个 HL 账户。

而保证金这里，每一组号上，我最终做的也不是 1:1 ，而是 会在 bn 上多放些。

原因是假设极端情况不幸发生，HL 上其实放多少保证金都不够，我想少亏点；

假设极端情况不发生，但因为股价正常的波动剧烈，需要平衡保证金时，从 bn 提现到 arb 冲 hl 的速度要快于 hl 提现-跨链-充值 bn。

5. 事后复盘时的反省。

这个策略当时不敢上高杠杆的最大风险，就是因为韩股 7 点的险象环生。

但如果是看到公告后第一时间开仓，等仓位造完，均价是不会太差的，那么不需要等到 7 点，理论上等后知后觉的人过来抬轿子，在 7 点前，就可以落袋一部分。

比如我均价 -80 bp 开了 6m 的仓位，我其实可以在凌晨两点多， +140 bp 把吃那我多开的 3m 仓位提前落袋，然后剩 3m 的安全仓位去吃股息。

所以别再怪哥们儿不喊单了，我要是喊单，肯定是都是自己建好了大仓位，喊你们来给我加速抬价差，做对手盘，让我 derisk，提前落袋的。

当然这事儿合情合理，最后一公里的钱我不赚，给兄弟们喝汤，只是我怕你们不理解韩股 7 点的凶险，梭哈进去，最后真炸了，哥们儿身上的因果太重了。

The majority of founders will fail on fundraising calls for mistakes in the first 5 mins on a call:

1. They bring multiple people. No bueno. It’s a 30 min call. You need to build the relationship; 1-1 only.

2. Ask Questions Early: They Are Buying, Not Just You Selling: 

The VC introduces themselves: 

Bad: the founder has zero questions. This is most common.
  
Decent: is 1 question that is meh. 

Good ones: ask thoughtful question on investment process: “how does investment decision making look”. 

Great founders: ask spicy or controversial questions about past challenging investments.

3. Intro Disaster: 

Lord keep your intro short. I don’t want to hear about the orchestra society you joined at law school unless it had an impact on you.

Clearly break your life into three chapters that shaped the person on the call. Make them crisp. Max 3 mins. If they want more, they can ask. They are the ones buying.

Don’t ruin your fundraising chances in the first 5 mins. Do this instead.

text:
我开始怀疑，AI 根本不用发明下一个 Transformer，就能启动自我加速。

昨天我刚写了 Anthropic 联合创始人 Jack Clark，认为完整的递归自我改进可能在 2027 年实现。今天看到 P-Zero Research 的一项新研究，我觉得这个时间点越来越值得认真讨论了。

他们做了一个叫 TasteVal 的基准测试，专门测量 AI 的「科研品味」。

这个词很有意思。一个好的研究员，除了会写代码、做实验，更重要的是知道什么实验值得做，看到结果以后该往哪个方向继续，什么时候应该及时放弃。

研究团队找来 24 位有一线研究经验的人类专家，与模型解决同一组 AI 研发问题。具体编码交给统一的 AI Agent，研究者只负责设计实验和判断结果。

结果 Claude Opus 5.5 达到了人类专家 2.3 倍的实验算力效率，研究者部分的单次成本约为人类专家的 1/30。更夸张的是，自 2025 年 12 月以来，前沿模型的这项效率平均每三个月翻一倍。

我们过去讨论 AI 自我改进，总在等它什么时候能提出下一代 Transformer，什么时候能像顶尖科学家一样产生真正原创的想法。

但我读完论文发现，研究者检查的 AI 实验方案里，居然没有找到真正全新的结构发明。它们主要还是在已有方法上调参、组合、修改。

科研工作里有大量的时间和算力，消耗在试错上。一个模型即使没有提出颠覆性理论的能力，只要能更准确地判断哪些实验值得做、哪些路线应该放弃，就可以让同样的 GPU 预算产生更多有效结果。

而且这种能力还有机会形成正反馈。AI 帮助研究人员更快改进模型，改进后的模型再回来参与下一轮研究。随着研究判断能力越来越便宜，能够同时展开的探索也会越来越多。

我们可能把 AI 自我改进的起点想得太高了。

人类总在等待 AI 做出一个足以载入史册的伟大发现，可真正改变 AI 研发速度的，可能是它先把实验室里那些平庸、重复、昂贵的试错工作接管了。
author: otterpal24
quoted_text:
P-Zero Research's new TasteVal benchmark measures research taste: how well a model designs experiments and reads their results on eight real AI-development tasks, scored by how much compute it needs compared with human experts (the dashed 1x line). 

Progress was slow from GPT-4 in 2023 through 2025, then the slope steepened: since December 2025, scores have doubled every 3.0 months. Claude Opus 5.5 now sits at 2.30x the expert baseline, ahead of Fable 5.1 and GPT-6 Astra, at roughly 1/30 of the experts' cost per attempt.

Research taste is the skill that decides how quickly AI could start improving AI, and this curve is one reason Jack Clark now expects that in 2027 (wrote about that yesterday as well).

Yan argued that oversight should apply to entities exercising control over those markets, allowing the protocol to function as a shared liquidity and trading infrastructure layer. Yan said Hyperliquid aims to provide infrastructure for Wall Street institutions rather than replace them. Hyperliquid remains unavailable to US users.

text:
ZkSync用Airbender 证明器做到了一件标志性的事：

用一张专业级 GPU 显卡（NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000）

实现在 12 秒以内实时生成一个以太坊区块的零知识证明（ZK proof）。

以太坊现在大概每 12 秒出一个块。

所以，这意味着，

“实时”就是证明速度跟得上出块速度。

之前证明一个区块通常要几十张甚至上百张 GPU，现在一张就够了。

为什么这对以太坊很重要？

未来以太坊主网可能往 zkVM 方向升级：

现在是：

每个验证节点都要自己把区块里的交易重新跑一遍，确认对不对。

以后可以做到：

只要有人生成一个很小的证明，全网只需要验证这个证明就行（验证很快），不用每个节点都重新执行一遍交易。

这样一来，好处显而易见：

节点可以更轻、门槛更低、更去中心化，

与此同时，

扩容能力也会更好。

这是以太坊长期路线图里最重要的部分之一。

okx wallet:https://t.co/fUZffASzGZ

The first “mining-style meme token launch model” on the Fourmeme platform, jointly launched by Fourmeme and TapeOut Protocol and deployed on BNB Chain.

Traditional meme coins are mainly about “buying, selling, and holding,” with participants primarily driven by speculation. TapeFour turns participants into actual “miners.”

How it works:Inner curve phase: Buy “transistors” at a fixed price.
After graduation: Assemble 5 transistors into 1 mining machine through a process called “tape-out.”
Mining phase: Mining machines continuously produce the meme token, which can be claimed at any time.

This creates a closed loop: holding = mining, and mining = participation. 95% of the tokens are released through mining, while the initial circulating supply is extremely low, with only 5% entering the liquidity pool.

The model aims to address the problem of traditional meme coins being purely speculative, with limited sustained participation and incentives. It transforms “trading memes” into a participation cycle built around mining mechanics.

Specific mechanics:Fundraising: Transistors are sold at a fixed price through a bonding curve, with equal access for everyone and the ability to buy or sell at any time. Payments can be made in BNB or BEM.

Graduation: Once all transistors are sold out, a fixed supply of 1 billion tokens is minted.

5% (50 million tokens) plus approximately 98% of the funds raised are injected into PancakeSwap V2, with LP tokens permanently locked.
95% (950 million tokens) go directly into the mining contract, with no tokens reserved for the team.
The protocol and creator each receive 1% of the funds raised.
Creators can configure transaction taxes and how the tax revenue is distributed.

Mining: Every 5 transistors can be assembled into 1 mining machine through tape-out. Mining machines continuously generate tokens. Users can burn the project’s own tokens to accelerate mining and achieve 2x mining speed for periods of 10, 20, or 30 days. Transistors and mining machines can be freely traded on Firstoai, the largest marketplace in the TapeOut ecosystem.

Token utility:The token primarily serves as both a mining reward and a tradable meme coin. It can also be burned to accelerate mining.

The project’s potential advantage is its innovative approach: it combines TapeOut’s on-chain hardware and tape-out concept with meme coins, giving it an additional narrative layer and a mechanism beyond ordinary memes, along with some gamified elements.

text:
StandX 不发币而选择补钱散场这件事，小编认为其实还是相对体面的。

理论上，有20万+用户和交易量，选择硬上 TGE 割一波，一些 Rug 和软跑路的项目就是这么做的。

但不发币，把剩余营收加上老板 @StandX_AG 出资，直接换成无锁仓的 DUSD 稳定币分给社区解散，这波“自掏腰包体面退场”已经算清流了。

只是苦了深度参与交互的撸毛党，原本博弈的是一个高估值的新币暴富机会，最终可能只有一笔回本性质的稳定币安慰奖。

不过看一眼链上数据，也能理解为什么团队选择主动刹车。

DefiLlama 数据显示，StandX 链上 TVL 在2500 万美元级别，

截至 10 月中旬：
-累计永续合约成交量高达惊人的 1450 亿美元，
-最近 30 天内也维持着约 110 亿美元的成交体量，
-在 89 个同类 DEX 中排名第 6，占约 4.2% 的市场份额。
-但未平仓合约量（Open Interest）只有1400万美元

放在一起看，高成交量、低持仓量、高资金周转率，这更像是典型的“刷量撸毛”盘面特征。

真正能留下的真实用户或许很少。本质上还是“积分预期驱动”的高周转刷量。一旦发币预期降温，资金和流动性都会快速干涸。

只是，如果连一个由前币安合约掌舵人带队、拥有两亿美金冷启动资金、产品体验高度成熟的 Perp DEX 平台，都无法将“积分大军”转化为真实的留存交易者，

那么市面上那些还在靠积分 PUA 用户、等着发币套现的同类竞品，它们底层的真实商业价值究竟还剩多少？

刷积分内卷的时代，可能真的过去了。
author: TechFlowPost
quoted_text:
Regarding StandX’s decision not to proceed with a TGE, I want to speak to everyone with complete candor.

Without any external VC funding, our TVL reached a peak of $200 million. While our team delivered achievements worth being proud of, we still fell short of our ambition to become a top 3 perps dex.

Given our current fundamentals, we technically could push forward with launching a token. However, launching a token primarily on the back of short term speculation without delivering sustainable long term value ultimately leaves the cost for our users and community to bear. Doing so would be irresponsible, both to our community and to our team, and it goes against my personal values.

Most of our past revenue has already been passed back to users through SIP-2 and SIP-3 subsidies. For this upcoming airdrop, beyond utilizing our remaining project treasury, I will also personally contribute funds to do everything I can to give back to the community that supported us along the way.

All user funds are completely safe and DUSD is fully collateralized. We will ensure an orderly wind down and clearly publish specific arrangements regarding fund withdrawals, airdrops, and service sunset dates.

Thank you to every single user and team member. I deeply regret that we couldn't reach where we set out to go. You can trust that this final bittersweet process will be handled cleanly and professionally. Thank you, one final time, for your support throughout this journey and for standing with us.

这次 StandX不进行TGE的决定，我想坦诚地和大家说几句。

在没有外部资本加持的情况下，我们的 TVL 最高达到过 2 亿美元。团队做出了值得肯定的成绩，但仍未达到我们进入行业前三的预期。

以目前项目的基本面，我们确实可以继续发币。但如果无法兑现长期价值，靠发币和短期炒作获利，就是把代价留给用户和社区。这对外、对内都不负责任，也不符合我的价值观。

过去的大部分收入，已经通过 SIP-2 / SIP-3 补贴给了用户。这次空投，除了项目账上的盈余，我也会个人出资，尽力回馈一路支持我们的社区。

所有用户资金都是安全的。我们会确保有序关停，并明确公布资金提取、空投和各项服务停止的具体安排。

感谢每一位用户和团队成员。没能走到预期的位置，我很遗憾。我们会尽力把最后的事情做好。

Stand.

text:
Do you remember that scene from Fight Club where the narrator discovers that Tyler Durden was never someone else?

He was confronting a part of himself he never understood.

Now look at our generation.

We grew up watching people suffer emotionally while pretending to live successful lives. So we decided to use more logic and less heart.

Then came social media. Crypto. AI. The whole hyper-productivity culture where everyone wants to become rich, intelligent and successful before turning 30.

We are building our own Tyler Durden.

A persona which is confident, productive, ambitious and emotionally detached.

And the internet keeps feeding that persona.

We don’t even act anymore. We react. React to trends. React to opportunities. React to someone else’s success. Even our intelligence is increasingly outsourced to machines.

And one day when we finally achieve everything this persona wanted, the question will arise.

Who am I without all these things?

That’s where the shadow enters.

All those emotions you buried while building your successful identity will demand your attention.

And the self-help industry will happily sell you another identity. Another course. Another hack. Another illusion.

But you don’t need another persona.

You need expression. You need to attend your own darkness. Write it down. Sing it out. Find your own rhythm through art, silence and spiritual discipline.

Because freedom doesn’t come from building a stronger identity.

Sometimes it begins when the identity you were protecting finally loses its power over you.

And what remains after that?

The capacity to love without constantly trying to become someone.
