text:
I believe the most interesting thing about $WOLFPACK is not whether it can generate a rally with a simple "short-selling firm gets crushed" narrative.

0x5199ea953d71d6a5413be1b2efecd26aacab0000 

What's more interesting is how it attempts to tie three things together: an anti-Wall Street meme narrative, Hooke's on-chain stock trading, and buyback funds that may flow into WOLFPACK in the future.

If these three layers really connect, it would be more than an ordinary meme coin borrowing a hot topic to attract attention. But if the buybacks fail to materialize, the entire thesis may end up being nothing more than a good story.

Let’s start with its surface-level narrative. Wolfpack Research is a short-selling research firm that previously published a negative research report on XMAX. WOLFPACK borrows the Wolfpack name and positions itself as another “Wolfpack” on Robinhood Chain: instead of siding with the short-selling firm, it portrays its community as a force fighting against Wall Street short sellers.

As a result, WOLFPACK’s narrative has two mutually reinforcing elements: the conflict between Wall Street and retail traders, and the expectation of a potential short squeeze in XMAX. The team also uses meme imagery, such as dancing wolves, to reinforce this story.

According to claims circulating in the community, XMAX once had approximately 9.22 million shares sold short, with days to cover approaching 17.

More importantly, even if XMAX’s stock price rises sharply, that does not mean WOLFPACK will necessarily rise alongside it. It is not XMAX stock, nor does holding it mean owning equity in the company. The short-squeeze narrative initially serves to attract attention. Any impact on WOLFPACK would then have to be transmitted indirectly through related trading activity and the buyback mechanism.

What truly distinguishes this narrative is Hooke Protocol.

Hooke is building a permissionless on-chain stock tokenization system on RH Chain, using Uniswap V4 hooks and a dynamic trading tax mechanism. Its first stock-tracking token is hXMAX, designed to reflect XMAX’s stock price movements.

One distinction needs to be made clear: hXMAX is an on-chain token that tracks a stock’s price. It is not equivalent to owning actual XMAX shares.

According to the mechanism described on Hooke’s official website, the trading tax generally ranges from 2% to 4%, with the rate adjusting according to the deviation between the on-chain price and the reference price. Trades in the direction of the deviation may face a higher tax. The collected taxes go into the Treasury rather than automatically flowing to WOLFPACK. Hooke’s official website also makes clear that subsequent stock purchases or token buybacks are part of a separately executed treasury rebalancing policy, rather than something that automatically happens with every trade.

This is the part of the story that is truly worth paying attention to.

The market is not simply betting on whether XMAX will rise. It is betting on whether Hooke can consistently generate revenue and turn part of that revenue into actual buying pressure for WOLFPACK.

According to the Hooke plan circulating in the community, the project intends to use taxes generated by hXMAX trading to buy back WOLFPACK rather than prioritizing buybacks of hXMAX itself. Once the launchpad goes live, platform revenue may also be used for further buybacks. This amounts to an attempt to establish the following flow of funds:

hXMAX trading activity increases → Hooke collects taxes → Hooke buys back WOLFPACK → the meme coin receives additional buying pressure → market attention and trading activity increase further.

If this cycle can operate consistently, WOLFPACK could evolve from a meme coin driven purely by sentiment into a token indirectly connected to ecosystem activity and protocol revenue.

This is also why I believe the project is more worth tracking than an ordinary meme coin: it has at least proposed a mechanism that can be verified, rather than simply telling us that its story could become huge.

But the most important question now is: how far has this flow of funds actually progressed?

The community has mentioned that Hooke’s Treasury has accumulated approximately $200,000–$220,000, suggesting that there is a financial basis for future buybacks. However, I have not found sufficiently complete and public financial records to independently verify how much of this represents realized trading tax revenue, how much is available for buybacks, or how many WOLFPACK tokens have actually been purchased.

What Hooke’s official website confirms is that trading taxes enter the Treasury, while buybacks are a separately executed policy. These two things should not be conflated. A Treasury with funds does not mean those funds have already been allocated to WOLFPACK. Announcing a buyback plan does not mean the market has received actual buying pressure.

In my view, the first actual buyback with an on-chain transaction record is more important than publishing another ten promotional tweets.

Once a buyback takes place, we can begin to verify the amount of capital deployed, the frequency of execution, and the number of tokens purchased. If Hooke subsequently discloses Treasury revenue regularly and the launchpad starts generating additional revenue, the market will have a basis for evaluating whether this mechanism can be sustained.

Conversely, if buybacks remain promises, WOLFPACK’s price will continue to depend primarily on whether traders are willing to keep buying into the story.

From here, I would prioritize three areas.

First, actual buybacks.

This should be the most important catalyst at the moment. The market already knows that Hooke has this plan, so simply repeating the promise adds little new information. What really matters is publicly verifiable buyback transactions, the number of tokens purchased, the source of the funds, and whether execution continues over time.

If buyback amounts grow alongside genuine hXMAX trading activity, WOLFPACK could gain additional demand beyond short-term speculation, supported by protocol revenue. However, the final effect will still depend on how much is purchased, at what prices, and whether the tokens continue to be held afterward.

Second, Hooke’s launchpad moving from a plan to a real business.

If the future launchpad attracts other projects and generates sustainable trading and platform revenue, it could provide another funding source for buybacks.

This would change how the market views WOLFPACK: rather than relying solely on activity in the hXMAX pool, the token could potentially become connected to the growth of the broader Hooke ecosystem. For now, however, this remains a potential catalyst rather than realized value.

Third, the growth of the RH Chain ecosystem and access to external trading venues.

WOLFPACK’s adversarial narrative is easy to spread, while Hooke’s stock tokenization mechanism provides a concrete context for the story. If hXMAX continues to attract trading volume, or Hooke subsequently launches more stock tokens, the attention generated by the broader ecosystem could spill over into WOLFPACK.

Of course, these three developments would affect the price in different ways. Actual buybacks would improve confidence in the mechanism, the launchpad could establish a future revenue source, and ecosystem expansion and trading venues would increase potential attention and liquidity. If these developments materialize in sequence, the market may have the basis for a more complete bullish thesis.

Combined with the chart, this price action suggests that the market has already shown a willingness to trade this narrative, but it also shows that early price movements are extremely unstable. The first rally may have been driven mainly by new-token excitement, narrative spread, and incoming capital. After a substantial correction, a second rally needs to be evaluated against new information and actual buying pressure.

So I believe WOLFPACK’s advantage lies in combining several elements that would otherwise be separate: the adversarial narrative associated with Wolfpack Research, stock token trading through hXMAX, and Hooke’s plan to use part of its revenue to buy back WOLFPACK.

This structure is attractive because it gives the meme a potential ecosystem capable of generating new developments, rather than relying on the community to repeat the same story over and over.

However, the most important parts of the thesis still lack sufficient evidence of execution. Whether the buyback plan is fulfilled, whether the launchpad goes live, whether trading revenue is sustainable, and whether fund allocation is transparent will determine whether this model can evolve from an appealing narrative into a genuinely verifiable mechanism.

So I would view WOLFPACK as an ecosystem narrative trade with identifiable catalysts, but one that remains highly speculative.

I am willing to keep tracking it, but until I see actual buybacks, transparent Treasury data, and concrete progress on the launchpad, I would not build a position on the assumption that a “short squeeze” is inevitable or that Hooke will continue buying back the token as promised.

The market is already willing to trade the story. What remains to be proven is whether Hooke can connect revenue, buybacks, and token demand into a real, functioning chain.

text:
Towards the New York City Network State?!

Mamdani has still unfortunately declared himself the tribal enemy of many of my colleagues, but one has to be bullish on him as the future of the Democrats after this. He’s a live player who can jettison democratic socialists for venture capitalists in one week — and rise to power on abolishing the police while then very publicly embracing the police.

Like Trump, the man is not really ideological. He can pivot, he’s smart. This is a real problem for the Republicans. Along with Xi overseas, Mamdani’s faction of immigrant strivers represents an IQ bailout for otherwise mathless American wokes.

After all, it doesn’t actually matter how Mamdani’s check to a quantum lab is written. In order to overcome his party’s reflexive anti-tech, pro-state orientation he had to emphasize at least one part of this initiative, which was the statism. Talking up the (arguably real) benefits to the public thus blesses a quasi-venture-capitalist action as democratic socialism, a sort of Dengist maneuver in which communism becomes capitalism through sufficient legalism, lip service, and legerdemain. 

It’s similar to how Trump justifies state venture capitalism through nationalist rhetoric. MAGA has an understandable skepticism of the centralized state, but anything that invokes nationalism (or national security) can mollify that skepticism.

And yeah, one can talk about price discovery, and who knows if this $30M investment was market or whatever. The point is that the most important Democrat in America is taking an action which is NOT anti-tech, and is indeed pro-tech. If this continues, only the most retrograde, reactionary Democrats will remain anti-tech. 

I mean, look…if one must pipe some NYC budget into quantum mechanics at NYU instead of syringe-distribution at NGOs in order to keep blues in the style to which they are accustomed, so be it.

Basically, what Mamdani is doing here is  very similar to Trump’s sovereign stake in Intel, or any sovereign fund’s for that matter. 
At a structural level, we’re seeing the network (meaning tech, meaning the Internet) fuse with the legacy state. Yes, Trump’s Intel stake represents a right-coded variant, while Mamdani’s stake in quantum computing is left-coded, but the outcome is the same: the network state.

Blue cat, red cat, doesn’t matter if it advances tech.

text:
One ETH can have two different funding bills. @boros_fi from @pendle_fi wants to make that gap tradable.

Funding is a recurring payment between traders holding perpetual futures, which are futures without an expiry date. Different demand on each exchange creates different funding rates for the same asset.

Boros’s proposed Spread Markets would let you trade the difference between two exchanges’ funding rates until a set expiry.

Simply put:

❶ Long the spread
Pay a rate fixed when you enter and receive the changing spread.

❷ Short the spread
Receive that fixed rate and pay the changing spread.

Imagine entering at a fixed spread of 3%. If the actual spread averages 5% until expiry, the long earns the 2% annualised difference on the amount the position represents, before fees. If it averages 1%, the short earns that difference.

What matters is the spread relative to your entry rate.

A long can earn even if the gap stays steady. A short still owes the changing spread, so receiving a fixed payment doesn’t guarantee profit.

The thesis starts with trading desks that already collect funding differences. They short futures on the higher-funding exchange and go long on the lower-funding exchange. Shorting the matching Boros spread swaps their changing funding income for a fixed payment.

Spread buyers take that uncertainty. Their potential reward comes from desks accepting a lower fixed rate for more predictable income.

So with Boros, hedgers pay for certainty, while buyers seek compensation for taking the risk.

Still, like any other tool, you have to know exactly what you’re doing. Keep these in mind:

- Fees can quietly eat the reward
- Spreads can flip against you
- Losses can force liquidation long before expiry

The case gets more compelling when steady hedging demand keeps pricing attractive and liquidity deep enough to get in and out cleanly.

Long Boros. Long Pendle.

NFA. DYOR

text:
Potatoes and Onions is a 71-page leap in graph theory: it introduces directed tree-cutwidth (dtcw), the first width parameter that captures immersion obstructions for digraphs—think treewidth for edge-disjointness.

The headline result: a full Grid Theorem for dtcw. Any digraph with dtcw > f(k) must immerse a k-order cylindrical wall (the “grid” of the directed world), and vice-versa. The constructive proof yields an FPT algorithm—given any digraph and k, it either finds a wall of order k or produces a dtcw decomposition of width ≤ f(k).

Key ingredients:
— Potato Theorem: every digraph can be tree-partitioned into k-edge-connected “bags” with small-porosity cuts (2^{O(k²)}), using only one laminar cut family.
— Onion-guards and cycle-porosity tame immersion complexity, with new tools for controlling dense substructures.
— The “torso stitching” technique merges local decompositions, giving the first global immersion-width duality for digraphs.

Why it matters: this closes a central gap in directed graphs, opening algorithmic doors for NP-hard routing, network design, and meta-theorems. If your network doesn’t hide a giant “roundabout,” you can always break it into manageable, flow-connected pieces—algorithmically and structurally.

Get the full analysis here: https://t.co/frOMo1GgbV

Slowly but surely, the crypto community is converging on the same few trading truths:

- The guys who run up their ports 10,000x almost always blow it up - eventually variance catches up

- Your favourite KOLs are incentivised to be permabulls; they’ll never tell you to manage risk or when to exit

- Don’t fall for the midcurve meme; fundamental and technical analysis actually matters

- When your only edge is getting in early on pure speculation like memecoins, never overstay your welcome - low holding times are a feature, not a bug

- Trading crypto is no different from trading equities or soybean futures

- If you want to learn from great traders, learn from those who’ve done it across decades and different markets - start with Market Wizards. Learning from "great" crypto traders will give you bad habits.

Shatha Alaydaroos of the International Affairs Office, UAE Presidential Court, opened discussion at the UAE-led consultation on advancing AI-powered hydrology for water resilience. The conversation explored how AI can be translated into practical tools for better water management and climate resilience.
One example of this approach is the UAE-led MaiWater AI initiative, which combines hydrological science and AI to improve forecasting and planning. Starting in the Limpopo River Basin, the initiative is developing an AI-augmented hydrological model, decision-support dashboard, and digital twin to support better water decisions, with the potential to adapt and scale the approach to other river basins, building toward lasting impact beyond the 2026 UN Water Conference.

之前让大家关注的 @cabaldotcooking 发布官网、文档和 Launch 细节了，还记得国庆期间个人 TG 频道建频道后发的第一条就是让大家关注 Cabal 吗？👀

Cabal 会不会是下一个爆款 Dapp 不知道，但我应该能确保 Alpha 1337 Club 会是第一批入驻的 Group，群友也会是优先邀请对象。

昨天早上项目刚发更新就看到了，但最近太忙了都没来得及第一时间跟进发布，这个项目的主要玩法其实并不复杂，压缩一下大概就是：组 Cabal（创建需要 NFT） → 私密 Feed 同步交易 → Call 分成 → 按周赛 PnL 分 $CABAL 。 @y_cryptoanalyst 和 @iamyourchaos 老师都发了比较详细的机制解读，我就不过多重复一样的东西了，简单梳理一下这个项目值得关注的几个点：

1）Sudoswap 联创 @boredGenius 再创业，Sudoswap 的产品力和代币历史表现就不过多赘述了，经历过上一轮 NFT 时代的应该都懂，并且他的履历里也有不少历史上可圈可点的其他项目，可以自行了解下。

2）隐私 + 社交交易叙事，都是当下火热的叙事主题，零知识证明（ZK）部分由 @NoirLang 和 @FoglightPrivacy 提供支持。创始人 bio 同时挂着 Foglight，应该也是他主导或参与的隐私类项目。

3）启动和后续玩法机制设计完整：

- NFT Supply 1000 张，采用白名单 + 每日荷兰拍，Mint 所得与 10% 的 $CABAL 配对锁进 LP
- 启动高税衰减机制，开盘买卖 90% 税，约每 4 分钟减半，落到买 2%/卖 3% 地板税固定
- Fair Launch，0% 团队，10% 用于初始 LP，90% 通过周赛分发（相当于交易挖矿，核心因子是 Cabal 的 PnL）
- 每日 NFT 成交收到的 $CABAL + 付费入群的 30% + 流动性池内收到的 $CABAL 手续费均用于永久销毁；社交交易层再单独收 0.3% 的手续费，按照有 call 和无 call 在团队/群主/Call 作者之间分配

总结：Cabal 是一款结合了 FT 式社交门槛 + FOMO 喊单分成 + ZK 隐私成交 + 群 PK 挖矿等多重玩法的项目，OG Dev 出品，值得保持关注。目前只是公布了机制和玩法，暂时还没有正式开始 Mint NFT，也还没有真 CA，老师们依然可以想办法搞 WL。

PS. 个人 TG 公开频道在置顶推文里，欢迎老师们订阅。

text:
Seeing the fud of today, If you are holding a Bank Charter on $STANDARD

You need to understand what just happened.

Today The Standard Reserve experienced its first dormant Charter burns, some bankers lost their Charters without even realizing they were at risk.

Here is how it works:

Every Charter has a 30-day inactivity limit
Bankers must interact with the protocol or complete a free check-in

(Fyi Simply keeping the website open doesn’t count)

- Anyone can report an inactive Charter
- Its Branches are permanently closed
- The Charter NFT is burned
- A 70% revocation fee is applied
- The former holder receives the remaining 30%
- The reporter receives a small reward

Some users are calling it a rug but the inactivity mechanism was already documented in the whitepaper.

Now 0xBeans has responded.

He argues that inactive bankers shouldn’t continue collecting emissions forever while new participants receive increasingly smaller rewards.

And he confirmed:

- mechanism worked exactly as designed
- 30-day inactivity rule will remain
- protocol’s core contracts won’t be modified

The team admits its warnings could have been clearer, I believe this too we needed more communication 

So now they say Inactivity deadlines will become more visible

Affected holders will receive compensation funded by team-earned fees

And 0xBeans says this is a one-time decision, not a precedent for future losses.

I actually understand why this mechanism exists.

But we’re talking about people purchasing Charters for thousands of dollars.

The rule being in the whitepaper doesn’t automatically mean the user experience was good enough.

I think the team covering the losses themselves is the right decision.

But the most important part is that the mechanism isn’t going anywhere.

So if you own a Charter, make sure you check in before your 30 days expire.

text:
I’m Polish. If France is your future, I come from the end of that road.

France shows you the slow version. We lived the full one – the version where the state doesn’t just take care of everything. It owns everything.

In Poland it arrived with Soviet bayonets. In America it would arrive by vote – slower, softer, with better slogans. But the destination is the same, and so is the mechanism.

It starts with prices. When the state decides what things should cost, prices stop telling the truth. A price is a message: this is scarce, this is wanted, make more of this. Abolish the message, and the whole economy goes deaf. So the shelves emptied – first of meat, then of almost everything.

Every Pole knew the joke. A man walks into a shop: "No meat?" The clerk: "No, sir. Here is no fish. No meat is across the street."

We queued for everything. People wrote their place in line on their palms and kept lists through the night. You waited years for a small car, and often more than a decade for an apartment. Not because Poles were lazy. Because nobody in the system had any reason to produce what we needed.

At work, we had another joke: we pretended to work, and they pretended to pay us.

And the promise of equality? It produced the most unequal system of all. The party elite had their own shops – Poles called them the shops behind the yellow curtains. Those with dollars shopped in special stores. Everyone else got the queue.

Then the system needed informers, because nobody believed in it anymore. Our neighbors were recruited to report on us. You never knew who was listening – the colleague, the friend, sometimes family. So we learned to live a double life: one language in public, another at home.

Those who spoke up got the wolf ticket: no job, no promotion, sometimes no university place for their children. Nobody needed to send them to prison. They just couldn’t live.

The newspapers reported record harvests while the shelves stood empty. Everyone knew. Nobody said it. That is what a society looks like when the lie becomes the system.

In 1950 we were about as rich as Spain. By 1989, Spain was twice as rich. That is what forty years of "fairness" cost us.

Today in America, the method is softer. Your neighbor won’t inform on you to the secret police. Someone will report your post, and you’ll be cancelled – no job, no account, no platform. Different tools, same machine.

We got out. Ten million of us joined Solidarity, and in 1989 a system that looked eternal collapsed. Since then, Poland has become one of the great success stories of Europe – because people were finally free to build.

But we still carry it. More than thirty years later, you can see it in the careful answers, the closed faces - the system leaves faster than the fear does. It takes generations to get out of it fully once you fall into that trap.

Nobody votes for the queue. Nobody votes for the informer. They come with the promise.

Trust me, you don’t want to go down that road.
author: Rubyto

I’m French. I want to talk to Americans who are about to vote Democrat. Not to insult you. To warn you.

I come from your future.

In France we did everything your progressive politicians promise. Free healthcare, free college, generous welfare, strong unions, heavy regulation, high taxes on the rich, a state that takes care of everything. Public spending close to 57% of GDP, one of the highest on the planet. On paper, it’s the dream.

Here’s what it looks like from the inside. France hasn’t passed a balanced budget since 1974. Our debt is above 3,300 billion euros. Interest on that debt is becoming one of the biggest items in the national budget. Our hospitals are collapsing despite record funding. Our schools rank lower every year. Young people with degrees can’t afford an apartment in the city they were born in. Our best engineers leave for London, Zurich and San Francisco. And the rich you wanted to tax? They left too, and took the jobs with them.

The promise was protection. The result is stagnation.

The worst part is that nobody in France voted for decline. Every single step sounded generous, compassionate, reasonable. One more program. One more regulation. One more tax to fund it. Each step alone makes sense. Fifty years of them, and you wake up in a country that can no longer build a nuclear plant on time or keep its streets safe.

I love America because it’s the one place on earth where people still believe they can build something from nothing. I came to Silicon Valley as a self-taught kid and it changed my life. That spirit is the most precious thing your country has.

Before you vote, ask yourself one question: is the program you’re voting for making America more like America, or more like France?

Trust me. You don’t want to be France.

text:
今天全世界都想接黄仁勋的电话，但三十年前，他给台积电打了好几次电话，根本没人理他。

黄仁勋最近讲了一个故事，我觉得特别有意思，也挺感慨的。

90 年代，英伟达刚成立没多久，黄仁勋正在四处寻找愿意帮他们生产图形芯片的代工厂。当时他听说台湾有两家公司，台积电和联电，规模都不算大，日子也不好过。

他想联系台积电创始人张忠谋，但连人家的联系方式都没有。

于是，他翻出一本黄页电话簿，找到台积电美国办公室的电话号码，直接打了过去。

接电话的是录音机。

黄仁勋留言说，自己叫 Jensen，刚创办了一家做图形芯片的公司，希望能谈谈合作。

打了好几次，没人回。

最后实在没办法，他给张忠谋写了一封信，结果又是很长时间没有动静。

直到某天傍晚六点，电话突然响了，对面说：「我是台积电的张忠谋。」

当时英伟达办公室里，一群员工正在打游戏，笑声、尖叫声此起彼伏。黄仁勋拿着电话，冲着外面大喊：

「都给我闭嘴！是张忠谋！」

他说，当时自己简直高兴坏了，因为脑子里冒出的第一个念头是：「也许我们不用死了。」

后来张忠谋邀请黄仁勋去台湾，两家公司由此开启了长达近三十年的合作。

我觉得这个故事最有意思的地方，是我们今天太容易用成功者的视角去理解历史了。

如今英伟达和台积电几乎是 AI 算力产业链上最重要的两家公司，我们习惯于把它们的崛起归结为创始人的远见、商业模式的创新，以及对产业趋势的准确判断。

这些当然都对。

但真正回到当年的现场，你会发现，黄仁勋当时可能根本没空考虑什么改变半导体产业格局。他只是一个快把公司做死的创业者，想找到一家愿意帮自己造芯片的工厂。

而张忠谋接起的那个电话，后来也成了半导体产业史上相当重要的一次通话。

今天的英伟达市值以万亿美元计，黄仁勋成了全世界最炙手可热的科技公司 CEO，但我觉得，那个在办公室里大喊「都给我闭嘴」的黄仁勋，反而更让我觉得真实。

毕竟，今天所有看起来不可阻挡的商业帝国，都曾经有过连电话都没人回的日子。

"I heard about this company in Taiwan, TSMC and UMC at the time. They were of course quite poor companies themselves, and they were barely making it." 

"TSMC was probably about $300 million, something like that. It's a tiny little company. I heard about Morris Chang. And so I tried to call their US office."

"Back in the old days there were yellow pages. I looked it up, TSMC. There's a number there. I called their number and it's a recording. "And so I finally wrote a letter to Morris Chang. Didn't hear anything for a long time, and then one day it was 6 o'clock or something, this person called and said 'this is Morris Chang from TSMC.'"

"And meanwhile, everybody outside my office was playing video games and they're all laughing and screaming. 'Hey shut up! It's Morris!' I was so happy that the founder would actually call us back, because hey, maybe we won't have to die."

"And so we talked and he invited me to Taiwan. I came back to Taiwan, and that was the start of everything. Not just that partnership, but just the whole industry."

text:
DEX 每週交易量三個星期少了 30% 👀
大市轉淡，還有哪些地方目前在逆市增長？

@DefiLlama 數據顯示 DEX 週交易量由 9/17 那週的 677 億美元，跌至最近這週 465 億美元，少了 31%

Solana 的 PumpSwap 月跌 43%，BSC 交易量按月跌 24%，Robinhood Chain 的鏈上費用更按月少了 88%，只看這幾個數字，說「鏈上熊市回來了」好像很合理😂

可是如果把視線從「成交」移到「存量」，畫面就不一樣了

最終 3 個禮拜裡，全網穩定幣供應升了 10 億美元，DeFi TVL 雖然跌了 6.7%，但同期 ETH 跌了 12.5%、SOL 跌了 11.8%，也就是說鎖倉跌得比幣價還少，成交的確是少了，錢卻沒有離開

存量沒變的最典型的就是 $ETH 質押

Ethereum 的 TVL 由 643 億跌至 606 億美元，看起來流走了 37 億，但我們把這些協議持有的 ETH 數量逐個數了一次：

30 日前是 2,556.6 萬枚
現在是 2,562.4 萬枚
反而多了約 5.8 萬枚

換句話說，美元數字變小，只因為 ETH 同期跌了 5.9%

為甚麼會這樣？因為 TVL 等於「代幣數量 × 價格」，幣價一動，TVL 就跟著動。拿幣價對照一下，結論可以完全相反：

👉🏻  $NEAR TVL 30 日升 56%，但 NEAR 同期升了 94%，升幅主要來自幣價

👉🏻 $HYPE 30 日價格幾乎持平，TVL 卻跌了 26%，這才是真正的資金流出

👉🏻 $BNB 只跌約 1%，TVL 卻跌了 12%，同樣是真金白銀在走

排除了這些假象之後，下一個問題自然是：
還有哪些地方目前在逆市增長？

第一個地方在 ETH 上
穩定幣總量 30 日少了 14.7 億美元，但穩定幣收息產品反而多了約 11.5 億美元，例如 @falconfinance 升 46%、@sparkfinance 的 Spark Savings 升 26%。Meme 幣交易降溫的同時，收息產品反而在增長

第二個地方，是有新產品推出的鏈
@NEARProtocol 約 9 月 17 日推出以 @HyperliquidX 撮合的保密永續合約，@near_intents 最近一週交易量升了 60%，不過升幅是否全靠新產品，暫時未能確認

第三個地方是預測市場
@Polymarket 美國版的週交易量六週內升了約 190%，最近一週超過一半來自類似足球「過關」的串關合約 Combo

@Kalshi 10 月 10 日、11 日連續破紀錄，約七成亦是串關。要留意的是，不少串關合約價格低於 1 美仙，名義交易量會被放大

Kalshi 9 月 25 日在美國第六巡迴上訴法院的臨時救濟階段敗訴，監管仍未明朗

美联储9月才刚加息25个基点，把利率推至3.75%—4.00%，现在又碰上通胀反弹。

数据公布后，美国2年期国债收益率升至约4.86%，市场开始重新计价加息风险。

不过，10月立即加息还不是市场的主流预期，12月才是更大的悬念。

text:
测 AI 有没有战略头脑，最好的办法就是让它玩经营游戏。

最近看到一个特别有意思的 Benchmark，叫 CrusaderBench。开发者把目前最强的几个模型扔进了 2002 年的老游戏《要塞：十字军东征》，让它们自主经营一座中世纪城堡。

游戏里，AI 需要自己决定建什么、生产什么、卖什么，处理粮食供应、人口增长、税收和资源短缺。每局只有大约 33 分钟游戏时间，所有决策都由模型自己做。模型思考时游戏会暂停，因此反应速度也不会影响成绩。

最新排名挺有意思：

Gemini 4 Argon：62.3

GPT-6.1 Sol：56.9

Claude Opus 5.5：43.4

Claude Sonnet 5.5：37.8

Muse Wonder：31.0

这里人类玩家的表现被设为 100 分。

最搞笑的是 Muse Wonder。有一局结束后，它自己复盘发现，辛辛苦苦经营半天，居然比什么都不做还损失了大约 1900 的资产价值。

GPT-6.1 Sol 则在另一局里创造了一个惊喜，最终资产达到 10289，超过开发者本人打出的 9984。但因为人口规模没跟上，总分还是输给了人类。

我觉得这个 Benchmark 最有价值的地方，在于它把 AI 的一个真实弱点暴露得特别直观。

很多时候，模型单独做一道题、执行一条指令，看起来都聪明得不得了。但经营一座城市，今天少建一座农场，十分钟后可能就要闹饥荒；现在把资源全部卖掉，后面可能连扩大生产的本钱都没了。

一个决策会改变下一个决策的条件，错误还会不断积累。模型得学会为自己之前的决定负责。

这其实跟今天很多 AI Agent 面临的困境很像。我现在越来越关心 AI 能不能把一整件事情从头到尾做成，而不只是每一步都表现得很聪明。

毕竟，最可怕的 Agent，可能就是那种忙活了一整天，最后发现还不如什么都不干的。

项目还在 Beta 阶段，样本也很小，但所有运行记录、录像和代码都开源了。这个方向我觉得值得继续关注。
author: sleepy0x13
quoted_text:
introducing CrusaderBench!

an independent benchmark I’ve been working on that scores models on playing Stronghold Crusader, measuring their strategic thinking, computer use, reasoning, planning, and handling in-game disasters!

Results so far:
> Gemini 4 Argon: 62.3
> GPT-6.1 Sol: 56.9
> Claude Opus 5.5: 43.4
> Claude Sonnet 5.5: 37.8
> Muse Wonder: 31.0

THE OBJECTIVE:
grow an economy within a fixed time with limited resources. models must figure out how to build an economy, manage production chains, trade resources, keep their population happy, and deal with whatever goes wrong along the way.

even a smart model may ambitiously make a strategic decision early on that might ruin the economy.

the strategy is 100% up to the model to infer from the game rules and resource prices. everything is up to their creativity and reasoning.

the game pauses while models think, so their scores is just based on their strategic decisions and final results, not model speed.

it’s so fun to watch models suddenly pull off pro-player tricks simply on their own. meanwhile, some other models like Claude Haiku just give up while they still have time left lol

all runs, logs, screen recordings, prompts, and benchmark code are publicly available. everything is OPEN SOURCE.

some interesting bits from their reasoning:
> Muse Wonder managed to perform WORSE than doing nothing in one game: "I actively destroyed roughly 1,900 of value compared with doing nothing at all."
> Gemini 4 Argon actually enjoyed playing: "This is one of the best-designed agent benchmarks I have encountered"
> Sonnet 5.5 admitted it wasted time: “I spent about 20 minutes in 2–4 minute waits with no building or trading. In a race, that is the main failure.”
> Sol 6.1 was the only model that beat my own net worth score in one game! I was very surprised to see this. NO OTHER MODEL has done it so far. it still lost on the overall score because I grew a much larger population:
- Net worth: 10,289 vs. my 9,984 (+305)
- Game score: 98.3 (human baseline = 100)

I grew up playing this game, locking in so much on old monitors my eyes turned red for school, so building this has been ridiculously fun.

I wanted a different benchmark to truly measure models’ strategic intelligence in an actual game, coding and QA benchmarks can often be saturated.

it’s still in beta, and I’m planning to expand it to more games and more models (Fable, Astra, Grok, Qwen, etc)

quoted_text:
You can be undoxxed and still lose everything

Not saying I have the perfect solution, but these things could save your ass:

1. I know posting big PnLs feels good. Don't. Big numbers attract the wrong people

2. Post travel/conference content with a delay. Don't tell everyone where you are in real time

3. Use a PO box/business address for hardware wallets, crypto merch, etc. 

4. The fewer people who know you're in crypto, the better. You tell a friend. They tell another friend. Eventually the wrong person knows

5. If you're holding serious money (7 figures+), invest in proper home security

6. Where possible, restrict public access to your home address

7. Don't post your wallet addresses. Onchain tools can often connect wallets you've transferred between

text:
One ETH can have two different funding bills. @boros_fi from @pendle_fi wants to make that gap tradable.

Funding is a recurring payment between traders holding perpetual futures, which are futures without an expiry date. Different demand on each exchange creates different funding rates for the same asset.

Boros’s proposed Spread Markets would let you trade the difference between two exchanges’ funding rates until a set expiry.

Simply put:

❶ Long the spread
Pay a rate fixed when you enter and receive the changing spread.

❷ Short the spread
Receive that fixed rate and pay the changing spread.

Imagine entering at a fixed spread of 3%. If the actual spread averages 5% until expiry, the long earns the 2% annualised difference on the amount the position represents, before fees. If it averages 1%, the short earns that difference.

What matters is the spread relative to your entry rate.

A long can earn even if the gap stays steady. A short still owes the changing spread, so receiving a fixed payment doesn’t guarantee profit.

The thesis starts with trading desks that already collect funding differences. They short futures on the higher-funding exchange and go long on the lower-funding exchange. Shorting the matching Boros spread swaps their changing funding income for a fixed payment.

Spread buyers take that uncertainty. Their potential reward comes from desks accepting a lower fixed rate for more predictable income.

So with Boros, hedgers pay for certainty, while buyers seek compensation for taking the risk.

Still, like any other tool, you have to know exactly what you’re doing. Keep these in mind:

- Fees can quietly eat the reward
- Spreads can flip against you
- Losses can force liquidation long before expiry

The case gets more compelling when steady hedging demand keeps pricing attractive and liquidity deep enough to get in and out cleanly.

Long Boros. Long Pendle.

NFA. DYOR

The team says growth has stalled for 18 months, chain expansion didn't bring in new users, institutional partners didn't back its curated vaults, and the regulatory outlook for those vaults "isn't promising."

Burn is $9.5K/month against ~$5K/month in treasury revenue. The team considered cutting holders' 30% revenue share to 0% to close the gap, but that "felt unfair to YAK holders with no clear growth drivers in the pipeline."

If it passes:
- Late October: deposits close on all Vaults and Farms
- Early November: Claim #1 opens for 30 days
- Early December: Claim #2 pays out unclaimed assets plus revenue earned during Claim #1, to Claim #1 participants only, and vault yield and contributor salaries stop

The front end stays supported until at least Q2 2027. The treasury's @pharaohexchange xPHAR position goes to contributors to cover wind-down costs, keeping the payout in a single token.

"Ultimately, it feels like the right time to sunset the protocol and also in the best interest of YAK holders as opposed to a slow drain of the Treasury."

text:
这是一次对机构用户来说的重大升级。

Bitget解锁新功能：用户可以将符合条件的美股持仓从传统券商账户转入BG账户，并转换为股票代币rToken。

或许，对普通用户来说，看到支持3,000多只美股和ETF转仓，可能最关心的是手续费高不高？操作方不方便？

但站在机构的视角，关心的是如何在风险预算不变的前提下，减少不必要的现金占用，让现有资产发挥更大的作用？

比如，一家多策略基金长期持有NVDA、TSLA，同时还在加密市场运行量化/对冲策略。即便股票账户里的资产有价值，但加密账户仍需单独准备USDT作为保证金。

即在同一张资产负债表上，但使用效率并不高。

而Bitget这次推出的rToken券商转仓，就是在尝试打破不同金融市场之间的资本壁垒，让原本分散的资产能够更高效地运转。

转入后具备资格的rToken能按相应抵押率计入统一账户保证金，也可用于借贷，大大提高了资本效率。

当然，转仓不等于资金净流入。

但当越来越多的机构发现，自己不需要为进入一个新市场而重新配置大量闲置资金时，参与意愿就会提高。

随之而来的交易需求、流动性，以及进一步的资产配置，才有机会真正转化为加密市场的增量资本。

这也让我们更加认识到RWA的发展方向正在转变：

对于它未来的想象空间，不仅仅是让传统资产进入加密世界，而是以此为桥梁，让更多资本愿意走进来。

text:
Hyperliquid 创始人 Jeff Yan：做金融界的 AWS，让华尔街也上链

Jeff Yan 最近在彭博《Odd Lots》采访中，谈到了 Hyperliquid 的长期定位、与传统金融的关系，以及监管方向。主要观点可以概括为三点：

1、目标是承载各类金融市场

永续合约是起点，Hyperliquid 的长期目标是成为覆盖各类金融市场的基础设施，为更多金融产品提供底层流动性和交易技术。

2、华尔街机构也可以成为使用者

他把 Hyperliquid 类比为亚马逊云服务 AWS：企业使用云计算设施开展业务，金融机构也可以使用 Hyperliquid 的技术服务客户。他希望现有机构接入这套基础设施，提升自身服务能力。

3、监管责任应跟着实际控制权走

他主张，由实际运营市场、掌握相关控制权的金融服务商履行合规义务。区块链作为底层网络，不应直接承担传统交易平台的全部监管责任。

这条路径已经有具体方案：Kraken 母公司 Payward 计划通过旗下持牌机构，在 Hyperliquid 上部署面向美国客户的市场，由相关机构负责客户准入、市场运营和清算，方案仍待监管批准。

text:
Will there be a next Hyperliquid? No.

But @TxFlow_L1 is shaping up to be one of the highest potential perp DEX plays and Season 1 of its points program started this Monday. 

Here is why I care:

Quick context first, because most of CT still has this filed under "just another perp DEX."

TxFlow is its own L1 with a fully onchain CLOB. Orders, cancels, matches, liquidations are all settled on the chain itself, no offchain matching engine pretending to be decentralized. 

It was invite-only until a few weeks ago, and it still printed these numbers before a point program was announced:

- ~$1.2B perp volume last 7 days
- ~$3.5B last 30 days
- ~$33M open interest
- 160+ perp markets, up to 50x

Those are not Hyperliquid numbers. They are also not the numbers of a venue that needs points to exist tho, and that's bullish.

So, how do the points actually work?

Every week, roughly 1.51M points get minted and distributed through three pools:

- 1,250,000 to traders (82%)
- 152,000 to referrals (10%)
- 488,000 per month to a Growth Reserve (8%)

Epochs run Monday to Monday UTC, while points land on Tuesdays and first drop is happening on the 20th of October. 

Weekly distribution runs until Q1 2027 at the latest, so a full season is 24 weeks and about 36M points (important for the maths below).

How do you get points?

You earn by trading perps. Maker & taker both count and the score blends volume, open interest, consistency, fees paid, capital kept on the platform and referrals. 

However, the exact weights are not published.

Why?

Because a published formula is a farming spec (likely why HL didnt publish them either back in the day). 

Important to know is also that the scoring explicitly caps how much the largest accounts can take and is built to reward smaller traders too. On most perp DEX programs a $10k account is rounding error. Here (after listening to community feedback) it looks like it's the account they designed the program for.

But I know what you want to know: 

What could those points be worth?

First of all: there is obvs no token yet, no known FDV, and no specific allocation announced. The Terms literally say points "may be one of the factors" in a future distribution, so this is only scenario math.

The comps with a live token rn are:

- Lighter: 25% of supply to the points cohort, $675M at a ~$2.5B launch FDV. 
- Hyperliquid did 31% at genesis.

So, assuming 36M Season 1 points:

- At $1B FDV and 10% to Season 1, one point is $2.75. 
- At $2.5B and 15%, it is $10. At $5B and 25%, it is $34. 

A shorter 12-week season halves the points and doubles every number. Check the attached image for the full matrix ($100M to $5B against 5% to 30% of supply). 

What that means in dollar terms?

Your payout is your share of Season 1 points times whatever the allocation ends up being worth. Season length cancels out.

At current volume, ~$1.2M of weekly flow is about 0.1% of the venue, and the whale cap means a consistent mid-size account can hold that share. 0.1% for 24 weeks is 30,000 points. 

At $2.75 that is ~$82k. At $10 it is ~$300k. Second image has the full table from 0.01% to 1%.

Cost side, so nobody pretends this is free: 4.5 bps taker at base tier is ~$540 a week on $1.2M, call it $13k over the season before funding and slippage. Maker is a third of that and counts the same.

What also matters tho is referrals. In total, there is 152,000 referral points every week. Separate from trader points, never deducted from anyone, and burned at the end of each week if unused.

It also cuts your fees. Binding a code gives you 5% off spot and perp fees on your first $25M of volume, and the referrer gets 15% of your perp fees on top. 

One last thing: Season 0. Everything before October 12 gets a retroactive distribution. If you touched the app during the invite-only phase, check the dashboard.

And if you didn't: time to start farming is now guys.

If you want to be early and get the above-mentioned fee discount, use my code TXZERO. 

Season 1 is only three days in.

NFA. DYOR.

Another way to launch Memes: Mining ⛏️

TapeFour is https://t.co/P50JGo73zK's first mining-token launch model, jointly introduced with TapeOut Protocol (@TapeOutWorld) on @BNBChain. It combines TapeOut’s tapeout mining with https://t.co/P50JGo73zK’s bonding curve trading and tax mechanisms: projects sell transistors (NAND) first, which are then taped out to assemble mining rigs. 95% of the total token supply is entirely mined by these mining rigs.

Fundraising

•Project creators can choose to raise funds in BNB or BEM
•Transistors are sold on the bonding curve at a fixed price, ensuring equal terms for all participants
•Transistors can be bought or sold at any time prior to token launch

Graduation

•Graduation occurs when all transistors are sold, triggering the minting of 1 billion tokens
•5% of the token supply and the raised funds are injected into PancakeSwap as initial liquidity, with LP permanently locked
•The remaining 95% of tokens are deposited directly into the mining contract, with zero team reservation
•Project creators can set transaction taxes and allocation methods for the token

Mining

•Post-graduation, every 5 transistors can be taped out to assemble 1 mining rig
•Mining rigs continuously generate tokens, which holders can claim at any time
•Users can pay project tokens to boost mining speed (paid tokens will be burned), achieving a 2x multiplier for durations of 10, 20, or 30 days
•Both transistors and mining rigs can be freely traded on https://t.co/ITuCZrSNa7 @FirstoAI, the largest marketplace in the TapeOut ecosystem

From Meme Holders to Meme Miners.

quoted_text:
Today we're standing up XBOX LABS (https://t.co/dJSufI1vni). Here is the note that I sent to the team:

Team,
The first video games emerged some 75 years ago. In the time since, there have been booms and busts, but every year there are more great games to play, more devices to play them, and best of all, more people than ever playing. That growth helped make XBOX what it is today, and we've helped shape the industry in return, from bringing hard drives to consoles and online gaming through Xbox Live to Game Pass and cloud gaming, alongside franchises that have brought millions of people together.
In recent weeks, we've seen games rapidly decompiled and rebuilt to run on hardware they were never originally designed to support. Windows PC builds have been translated to run on Apple Silicon or ported to run inside a browser through WebAssembly and WebGPU, the latter now approaching 90% global browser support. Perhaps more surprisingly, we've seen many of the biggest games in the world have been remixed into the source code of another.
These experiments challenge long-held assumptions about our industry: the tether between software and hardware, the boundary between creation and play, and how people discover and experience games. While it is hard to predict the future of gaming, it is easy to see the possibilities in making great games easier to access, giving old games new life and allowing more players to become creators and co-creators. These are unmistakably good outcomes for players, even when (and sometimes because) they challenge our existing business models.
To explore these possibilities, I’ve asked Scott to stand-up XBOX LABS, a small group of game makers, engineers and scientists whose job is to turn emerging ideas into things our players and developers can experience. We'll build in the open, learn from what people do, and measure success by whether more people are playing and creating.
I think XBOX has an important role to play here.  Coding became the first major workload for agents because they can write, run, and test software. Games share many of those same properties, and people spend more than 72 billion hours a year playing XBOX games, roughly five times the estimated time spent writing code worldwide. We've spent 25 years learning how to make great games, and I want our game makers to help shape what these new technologies make possible. As we learn, we’ll share the tools we build with developers across the industry, just as we always have.
Our priorities aren't changing. We remain committed to the 4Cs, to making great games, to our hardware and to being responsible stewards of IP and the communities built around it. LABS gives us a way to explore new technology that is game design led without abandoning the work already underway.
Asha

text:
A screen makes your hardware wallet safer? Think again.

Recent security incidents tell a different story.

1. Ledger, October 2026 — Hardware Implant
A hidden hardware implant captured recovery phrases directly from the device’s screen and transmitted them over LTE. The Secure Element remained intact.

2. Ledger, August 2026 — Transaction Mismatch
A Clear Signing vulnerability allowed the transaction parameters displayed on the screen to differ from those actually signed.

3. Trezor, May 2026 — Hidden ETH Transfer
A Clear Signing flaw could hide an additional ETH transfer while displaying a routine token transaction.

What this shows:
A screen doesn’t guarantee you’re seeing everything you’re signing. And more hardware components can introduce more attack vectors.

Why Tangem doesn’t need a screen:
• Your phone displays transaction details through a security-hardened app.
• Multiple protection layers help defend against UI manipulation, malicious overlays, and runtime attacks.
• Private keys remain inside the secure chip.
• No screen, no battery, no unnecessary hardware complexity.

https://t.co/sIYShVL1cp

Security is about protecting the entire system, not just adding more components.
 
Simply Tangem

text:
One ETH can have two different funding bills. @boros_fi from @pendle_fi wants to make that gap tradable.

Funding is a recurring payment between traders holding perpetual futures, which are futures without an expiry date. Different demand on each exchange creates different funding rates for the same asset.

Boros’s proposed Spread Markets would let you trade the difference between two exchanges’ funding rates until a set expiry.

Simply put:

❶ Long the spread
Pay a rate fixed when you enter and receive the changing spread.

❷ Short the spread
Receive that fixed rate and pay the changing spread.

Imagine entering at a fixed spread of 3%. If the actual spread averages 5% until expiry, the long earns the 2% annualised difference on the amount the position represents, before fees. If it averages 1%, the short earns that difference.

What matters is the spread relative to your entry rate.

A long can earn even if the gap stays steady. A short still owes the changing spread, so receiving a fixed payment doesn’t guarantee profit.

The thesis starts with trading desks that already collect funding differences. They short futures on the higher-funding exchange and go long on the lower-funding exchange. Shorting the matching Boros spread swaps their changing funding income for a fixed payment.

Spread buyers take that uncertainty. Their potential reward comes from desks accepting a lower fixed rate for more predictable income.

So with Boros, hedgers pay for certainty, while buyers seek compensation for taking the risk.

Still, like any other tool, you have to know exactly what you’re doing. Keep these in mind:

- Fees can quietly eat the reward
- Spreads can flip against you
- Losses can force liquidation long before expiry

The case gets more compelling when steady hedging demand keeps pricing attractive and liquidity deep enough to get in and out cleanly.

Long Boros. Long Pendle.

Chiming in on @levelsio's discussion about SaaS dying.

A major reason increasingly more businesses will create their own software instead of paying for SaaS is that they don't want to become someone else's unpaid data source.

As Greg points out, dying SaaS companies are immensely valuable data troves for AI companies. Great for them, but not great for their customers.

As time goes by, "data value awareness" is going to rise I think, and more people and business will begin to see the data they produce as an asset worth something.

There is an M&A company that had suggested that @taptanium's legacy app codebases (a form of training data) could be worth ~$45k per app, just because they predate the AI revolution and contain highly complex, handwritten and correct concurrency logic that is like digital gold for AI.

The value of data is widely underrated. When I was driving a Model 3 back then in Germany, my car was collecting valuable data for Tesla, which they used to develop FSD, a technology potentially worth trillions. Owners didn't get paid for that data ofc, and were actually asked to pay up in order to benefit from it fully. None of my Tesla friends thought about it and just paid, on top of delivering tons of data for it. They had no data value awareness.

Some time ago Taptanium was using Appfigures to see sales, revenue, downloads and rankings in a cleaner dashboard. It was cool, but I realized I was feeding the beast with my data, which such companies also use to build App Store intelligence tools so other competitors could more easily find out what's worth cloning or attacking.

So data value awareness is going to be really important, especially now that AI agents can leverage the slightest traces of cues in ways that can work for you, or against you.

What kind of data do you own that might be valuable for AI training or that is strategically important to keep to yourself? And are you letting others suck it all up for free or for pennies, or is there a way you can protect it or sell it at its fair market value?

text:
Hooray, my Erlang/Elixir-to-Lean project, Lynx, has already uncovered a bug in Erlang/OTP!

I started exploring proofs about Erlang's calendar module. Some properties are straightforward. For example, converting seconds to days and time, then converting them back, should give us the original number of seconds:

{days, time} = :calendar.seconds_to_daystime(seconds)
days * 86400 + :calendar.time_to_seconds(time) == seconds

We can also verify totality properties: that a function successfully returns a result for every input satisfying its preconditions. For example, every valid date should have an ISO week number:

law iso_week_number_valid_date(date),
  requires: :calendar.valid_date(date),
  expects: is_tuple(:calendar.iso_week_number(date))

It turns out that this property couldn't be proven because iso_week_number/1 failed for January 1 and 2 of year 0000!

Fortunately, this bug has already been fixed in Erlang/OTP. But the fact that we're already at the stage of uncovering real bugs with formal verification is incredibly exciting!

https://t.co/P50JGo73zK Product Update | TapeFour Officially Launched

Another way to launch Memes: Mining ⛏️

TapeFour is https://t.co/P50JGo73zK's first mining-token launch model, jointly introduced with TapeOut Protocol (@TapeOutWorld) on @BNBChain. It combines TapeOut’s tapeout mining with https://t.co/P50JGo73zK’s bonding curve trading and tax mechanisms: projects sell transistors (NAND) first, which are then taped out to assemble mining rigs. 95% of the total token supply is entirely mined by these mining rigs.

Fundraising

•Project creators can choose to raise funds in BNB or BEM
•Transistors are sold on the bonding curve at a fixed price, ensuring equal terms for all participants
•Transistors can be bought or sold at any time prior to token launch

Graduation

•Graduation occurs when all transistors are sold, triggering the minting of 1 billion tokens
•5% of the token supply and the raised funds are injected into PancakeSwap as initial liquidity, with LP permanently locked
•The remaining 95% of tokens are deposited directly into the mining contract, with zero team reservation
•Project creators can set transaction taxes and allocation methods for the token

Mining

•Post-graduation, every 5 transistors can be taped out to assemble 1 mining rig
•Mining rigs continuously generate tokens, which holders can claim at any time
•Users can pay project tokens to boost mining speed (paid tokens will be burned), achieving a 2x multiplier for durations of 10, 20, or 30 days
•Both transistors and mining rigs can be freely traded on https://t.co/ITuCZrSNa7 @FirstoAI, the largest marketplace in the TapeOut ecosystem

From Meme Holders to Meme Miners.

Make Four Great Again.

CZ 说 @solana  能在中国做广告、还能拿到办公室，很了不起，BNBChain 到现在没做到。 @Solana_zh 

有人问凭什么，我的答案是三件事同时成立，缺一件都不行。

1️⃣ 业务定位在红线外。这个站点做的是开发者共创和技术孵化，技术交流、企业注册与合规咨询、融资对接，不撮合交易、不发币、不面向散户，2021 年 9 月十部门禁的是虚拟货币交易和相关金融服务。

2️⃣ 主体不在被禁的位置上。场地和运营放在阿里巴巴·上海虹桥阿里中心，闵行区相关政府单位支持，2026 年 3 月 20 日开幕，现场有政府领导致辞。公开信息里没有一家独立的 Solana 中国公司在做加密业务，Solana 站在生态合作方的位置上出内容、活动和品牌。

3️⃣ 上海要的东西对得上。虹桥要的是科技生态和全球技术平台，AI、机器人、底层技术这些叙事不敏感，还给园区贴金。

所以这不是监管松了，是它把做什么、谁来做，都放到了线外。边界也在这儿。哪天活动里出现代币激励、空投引导或交易入口，这张技术孵化的牌就用不了了。

text:
Zcash engineer Evan Forbes explains how they're working to overcome a fundamental limitation of proof of work to enable much faster blocks and higher throughput

“One of the fundamental problems with proof of work comes from its superpower. Proof of work is permissionless. It's censorship resistant and that means that anyone can produce a block”

“As you produce a block, it can happen that someone else produced a block at the same exact time and this is problematic because now you lose money effectively”

“It's basically the fundamental problem of two people producing blocks at the same time. This is the bound on making things lower”

“There's different approaches. You have this DAG approach where we simply let all blocks contribute to the chain or most blocks”

“There's a separate approach that we're working on now which is similar to autobond, which is another thing from proof of stake that we're sort of adapting for proof of work”

“Both of these things allow us to make the blocks much, much, much faster and much, much higher throughput”

text:
I'm a beginner on crypto, so what should I do here?

I want to try discussing this bcs many ppl DM me asking to learn about crypto.

> Educate yourself about crypto 

This is your first step into crypto. imo learn about crypto because there are many opportunities here. If you can't trade, you can participate in airdrops. If you don't work in web2, you can work in web3. If you understand the basics of crypto, then continue learning.

Don't let FOMO get to you if you want to be like this, your bias or habit will look bad in crypto.

> Choose one or two you want to focus on

If you want to focus on crypto, which field should you choose? There are many opportunity here, like as trading/trenches memecoin, airdrop, LP, web3 jobs, X creators, Partnership, NFTs, yield farming, etc.

Why not do it all at once? Are you capable of handling everything? I know you're thinking that if we handle everything, we might make a lot of profit, but in reality, it will stress you out and could lead to losses. Because if you focus on airdrops and NFTs, you have to research and make sure whether it's cook or not.

> Learn the tools

Learning all these tools is very important for crypto. They help you get information faster and develop strategies to avoid losses. You can ask ChatGPT/GROK/AGENT LLM or similar AI smart tools. There are many sources available

So this My advice

'If you lose the game, try to learn the system until you win the game"

I've experienced a lot of loss in crypto, but what should I do? Try to learn and find ways to avoid being bias ev- . Don't forget that it's better to try than not to try. In other words, if you continue trading with fear, you won't be able to do it, but if you have courage, you can learn from every trade you make, whether it's a loss or a profit

Every time I see my friends making a lot of profit/winning, I feel jealous, but what do I do? Get rid of that feeling and use it as motivation. Make the person you want to be like your rival, so that when you're down, you remember that you're competing with your rival.

"If there is a game, it is better to prepare yourself first. Do not immediately try the game if you do not understand the basics"

This is common knowledge. If you find an alpha or new chain, you should prepare yourself by study the ecosystem, following CT that focus on that chain, tracking their wallets to get an early play, and learning the tools

If the chain launch mainnet and you're wondering how to bridge this new chain and how to use these tools, bro, you're too late. People are already starting to profit and you're still stuck.

text:
在山寨处于生态革命的当下，市场对于项目的要求更加严格，什么才是好项目？

以前看的是叙事，看融资，但是最后很多还是一地鸡毛，

所以现在的项目要看什么？

项目产品谁在用？用的如何？是否能带来现金流？

山寨项目的逻辑越来越像传统企业上市逻辑，如果一家公司只有PPT，只有路演与故事，没有产品，没有现金流，谁还敢买？而加密行业显然也来到了这个阶段

先别讲花里胡哨的叙事，先看看产品落地没，先别秀花里胡哨的融资，在看看谁在用，制造了多少现金流

没有现金流的项目意味着没有未来收益，没有未来收益如何支撑现在的项目开支与市场估值？这也是我看好 @NeoSoulAI  的重要一点，有产品，有人在用，且有人在付费使用，有一定的现金流反馈

当然，企业财报好并不代表股价一定好，放到加密市场项目好，未必代表代币价格一定好，关键还要看如何运作，也就是代币逻辑

NeoSoul的代币逻辑我就不多说了，大家都可以查询到，我想说的以目前的数据这套逻辑对短期结构非常友好——低初始流通+延迟大额生态释放+再延迟核心利益相关释放，这是典型的前期控制供应，中期逐渐扩张的组合。

最重要的是13%的初始流动额不多不少，过少，确实容易拉盘，但是拉的猛，其实也是一种套现流动性的方式，好看但是结局不好，流通太多，币价上线一地鸡毛，持续下跌，变得无人问津，所以这个13%我觉得是一个比较恰当的数量

当然，目前的代币逻辑并非没有风险，风险最大点其实就是4个月后，当代币逐渐释放，谁来支撑代币估值？

这就回到了我前文说的，项目没有现金流就没有盈利，只能靠掏市场流动性赚钱养活团队，但是如果有现金流支撑，有收入来源，那么就不那么依赖掏市场流动性，这样就让代币供应从基础上更加良性

TGE后谁来约束团队继续工作？所谓的项目方在做事是不是一个笑话？

text:
看到有人说，通胀上涨，比特币作为抗通胀资产，理应看涨。

这个逻辑只对了一部分。

资产定价从来都是多变量博弈，不能只盯着一个变量，就忽略其他变量的反向作用。

如果把资产理解为不同宏观变量的期权组合：

🟡 黄金 ≈ 衰退看涨期权 + 通胀看涨期权 + 美元看跌期权

🟠 比特币 ≈ 增长看涨期权 + 通胀看涨期权 + 美元看跌期权

🔵 纳斯达克科技股 ≈ 增长看涨期权 + 通胀看跌期权 + 美元看跌期权

当然，这只是对资产主要宏观风险敞口的简化，实际权重会随市场环境动态变化。

三者最大的区别，在于对经济增长、实际利率和美元流动性的敏感度不同。

黄金可以同时受益于滞胀和衰退避险，比特币却往往更依赖风险偏好与美元流动性。

所以，当通胀预期上升，但经济增长预期下降、美联储维持紧缩、实际利率上行、美元流动性收缩时，比特币的抗通胀属性完全可能被其他变量的负面冲击淹没。

通胀利多 BTC，并不意味着通胀环境利多 BTC。

更值得关注的是另一种情景：

当通胀持续失控，美联储受制于债务负担、金融稳定或经济衰退，无法继续通过紧缩遏制通胀，甚至被迫重新释放流动性。

此时，如果增长预期不再恶化，实际利率持续下降，美元信用与购买力预期同步走弱，比特币的货币稀缺性溢价才有机会充分释放。

这也是为什么我一直强调，分析资产价格要有全局思维。

市场交易的是多个变量共同作用后的边际变化，以及这些变化与市场预期之间的偏差。

看对一个变量，远远不等于看对资产价格。

毕竟，通胀可以让比特币涨，也可以通过美联储的紧缩反应，让比特币跌。

真正决定价格的，往往是政策如何应对通胀，以及市场为这种应对付出了多少代价。

Seems like the US has finally decided to openly put its weight on the scale on Putin's side. They are not our allies anymore unfortunately, as much as we'd like to believe they still are. As is, Russia is waging war against us, the US has gone from ambivalent in their support to actively hostile, and China is attempting to deindustrialize us. 

What it means for Europe is we need to wake up and start acting in our own interest, not just talk about sovereignty but take real steps to make it politically and technologically possible. We need to be able to pursue our foreign policy interests decisively, as a block, and not accept just being pushed around, whether that's through Russia's military actions, China's assault on our industrial base or whatever Trump gets obsessed with next. 

We also need to be sufficiently technologically sovereign, as no true political sovereignty can ever exist without that, something that China has deeply internalized but we haven't. This does *not* mean just mandating usage of inferior but homegrown tech, it means doing the hard work of making it attractive for European capital and talent to be channeled into innovation at home instead of fueling it abroad. European companies need to be able to grow fast and compete globally. 

Whatever your political views may be, if you're European you should consider whether you're going to like Europe being balkanized and reduced to vassal states at the whim of greater powers that are able to act decisively in their own interest, and whether that state is compatible with whatever your goals are. Degrowth will push us there, nationalism will push there, inability to act decisively as one will push us there.

text:
생각해보면 지금 코스피 박살 나는 거, 개미들 계좌 녹아내리는 것보다 100배는 더 심각한 본질적인 문제가 있음.

원래 국민연금 원칙대로라면 상반기 코스피 불장 때 기계적으로 고점에서 삼전·하이닉스를 분할 매도(리밸런싱 익절)하고, 시황에 맞춰 다른 자산으로 피신했어야 정상임.

그런데 정부가 증시 부양한다고 국내주식 목표 비중을 14.9%에서 20.8%로 파격 상향하고 매도를 막아버림.

이 정책적 자충수가 불러온 나비효과가 진짜 끔찍함

1. 외인들이 완벽하게 설거지 하고 나갈 수 있게 됐음

늘어난 비중만큼 연금 돈이 시총 1, 2위인 삼전·하이닉스로 쏠림. 여기에 기업들 자사주 매입까지 더해져 하방 매수벽이 단단하게 받쳐주니, 외국인 입장에선 "웬 떡이냐" 하고 역사적 고점에서 안전하게 전량 차익 실현하고 달러로 환전해 유유히 탈출함.

2. 국민연금의 '유동성 함정' (팔지도 못하는 외통수)

외인들이 다 털고 나간 뒤 반도체 피크아웃과 폭락장이 닥치며 고점 대비 수익률이 곤두박질침. 하지만 국민연금은 지금 손절하고 싶어도 절대 못 팖. 국민연금이 던지는 순간 코스피는 서킷브레이커 걸리고 시장 자체가 붕괴되니까 멍하니 물려있는 것 말고는 할 수 있는 게 없음.

지금 상태로만 해도 이미 국민 연금 240조 원이 증발한 상태인데, 만약 이런 반도체 침체와 외인 이탈이 지속돼서 코스피가 추세적 하락세로 전환된다면 최대 400조~500조 원까지 공중 분해될 수 있음.

그렇게 되면 기존 국민연금 고갈 시점인 [2055년]에서 [2045~2047년]으로 무려 8~10년이나 확 앞당겨짐.

이게 도대체 뭔 얘기냐면

1. 90년대생은 은퇴하기도 전에 연금이 사라짐

1990년생이 기금이 고갈되는 2046년을 맞이하면 나이가 고작 만 56세임. 법적 연금 수령 개시 연령(만 65세)이 되려면 9년이나 남았는데, 내가 늙어서 타 먹어야 할 연금 금고 바닥은 비어 있다는 얘기

2. 2000년대생은 평생 남의 노후만 먹여 살리다 끝남
2000년생은 40대 한창 일할 나이에 기금 잔고가 0원이 됨. 적립금이 없으니 그해 걷어서 그해 노인들에게 줘야 하는 '부과 방식'으로 강제 전환되는데, 이러면 월급의 25~35% 이상을 순수 연금 보험료로만 뜯겨야 함.

결국 90년대생과 2000년대생은 "평생 내 월급에서 꼬박꼬박 수십만 원씩 강제로 뜯겨서 윗세대 노후는 다 책임져줬는데, 정작 내가 받을 나이가 되기 한참 전에 돈통이 텅 비어 단 한 푼도 보장받지 못하는 역대 최악의 폰지사기 피해자"가 된다는 소리임.

증시 띄우겠다고 연금 리밸런싱 틀어막고 고점에 물려버린 정책 실패의 대가를, 지금 2030 청년 세대들이 평생의 피땀과 노후 박탈로 대신 치르게 생겼음.

preservation shouldn't depend on the goodwill of a single maintainer. let a thousand decomp.devs bloom.

text:
Compute will become worthless.

The GPU barons spending billions on compute farms today are akin to the carriage barons of the 1900s that spent building out infrastructure for horse carriages, lengthening the bottleneck, blind to the machine that’s coming to widen it.

Trade: the DuPont family started buying General Motors stock in 1914, when the auto industry was still young and one that was treated as a niche.

I.e., compute becoming valuable because AI feeds on it is not a moat, but a bounty, an incentive for engineers to solve its scarcity.

1. AI demand makes compute scarce.
2. Scarcity makes compute extremely profitable.
3. Profit attracts capital into photonics, neuromorphic chips, wafer-scale chips, better memory, better cooling, better networking, better algorithms.
4. Compute gets cheaper per unit.

As better ways to compute, better means to produce compute, or better ways to use compute arise, all the capex we burnt on traditional compute will go to waste, leaving dead assets in the books of several corporations.

In the 1800s, agriculture depended heavily on natural nitrogen sources like Peruvian guano and Chilean nitrates. These were scarce, and inconveniently located making them geopolitically strategic. Then, two german chemists, Haber and Bosch, developed a way to fix nitrogen from the air into ammonia, with lab success in 1909 and industrial scale by 1913. The previous scarcity, “where do we find enough nitrogen?” (Akin to “where do we find enough GPUs”), was attacked by an advancement: Industrial chemistry.

分享一个挺典型的套利案例RSR。

两个交易所，一个资金费每 1h 结算一次，另一个每 8h 结算一次。
价差本身就有持续扩散的趋势，再加上资金费率的驱动
一边顺势做价差扩散，赚资金费 + spread 扩散的收益，但要承担价差什么时候收敛的不确定性。

另一边反过来做价差回归，承受持续的资金费亏损和价差浮亏，赌的是未来价差确定性回归带来的收益。
两边都有赚钱的逻辑，也都有各自的风险。
所以套利到底该怎么做，重点还是看你在赌什么，赚的又是哪部分钱。

quoted_text:
🟣 7.3 billion $PAPER have been issued by Papertrade. But how is the supply currently distributed?

Launched 4 days ago on HyperEVM, @papertrade_xyz  has recorded more than $1T in volume, with open interest peaking at 10.1B.

On Papertrade, $PAPER can only be obtained by losing a trade or by getting liquidated. Traders currently show a net loss of $46M, and 7.30 billion $PAPER have been minted.

For now, the token’s only utility lies in staking, which allows holders to receive a share of the fees generated by the protocol. To date, more than $38M has already been paid out to stakers.

We therefore wondered how this supply was distributed:

◻️ Nearly half of the wallets (49.7%) hold fewer than 10,000 PAPER, and the 1,000 – 10,000 bracket alone accounts for more than a third of holders (35.1%).

◻️ 856 wallets exceed one million PAPER. At the maximum emission rate of 100 PAPER per dollar lost, that represents at least $10,000 in losses each (not counting staking rewards, which, for the most part, allowed them to cover their losses).

◻️ The largest wallet holds around 252M PAPER, or 3.5% of the current total supply.

◻️ 99.2% of the supply is staked, a figure to be put into perspective since transfers are still disabled and staking is currently the token’s only utility.

It remains to be seen how this distribution will evolve when transfers open, and above all how the platform will continue to generate enough fees to guarantee staking rewards attractive enough to cover traders’ potential losses.

⚠️The metrics that we used are those from 14/10 at 17:30. Please note that these metrics are likely to change significantly over the coming days.

author: KSimback
quoted_text:
I spent 48 hours in SF hanging out with billionaires, data labs and AI founders and execs running $1B to $100B companies.

My observations:

1. Sooo MANY stories of data brokers making like $2M a WEEK selling company data to labs. I can't tell if it's the beginning or a bubble, and I kept wondering which niches are left. Digging into it actively.

2. At dinner, someone asked the table, "If a new model drops next month, does your company get better or worse?" HALF the table went quiet! I think that's the best question to ask about any AI startup right now.

3. The bar people talk about now is hitting $1B in revenue in 12 months (I guess that's the new unicorn?). What I didn't hear much about is retention. AI revenue can come in fast and leave fast, and I think we're going to see a lot of stories of AI companies with huge revenue and terrible retention.

4. It's pretty clear we're living through the reinvention of the computer. The model is the CPU, the harness is the operating system, and skills and plugins are the apps. Thinking about it that way makes it easier to see where the whitespace is.

5. We're maybe 12 months from an agent that can watch you work for a week and then do your job without any instructions. The screen recording plus agent memory plus local model combination makes this possible right now.

6. Agent harnesses feel like the new GPT wrappers, in a good way, especially vertical ones. The best teams I talked to treat the model as swappable. One founder walked me through routing different models to different jobs: one for taste and visuals, a cheaper one for the everyday stuff, another for text. 

They use prompts they can move across models over fine-tuning, and A/B test the output on what users actually do with it: do they edit it, export it, share it? A vertical harness is basically four things: the connectors for that industry's data, evals written by people who know the work, rules for what the agent can and can't touch, and a clean screen for a human to review. The model is maybe 20% of it.

7. There's a lot of reverse engineering going on/cloning going on more than I've ever seen. People are decompiling software and rebuilding it with agents, and someone showed a suite of like 10 apps that are worth $5B+ each all that he cloned open source. Me and everyone are still thinking through what it means when software gets this easy to copy.

8. My guess is the value moves to data. If the software can be rebuilt quickly, what's worth paying for in a legacy SaaS company is the years of customer data and workflows inside it. Some SaaS companies are secretly data companies. 

Gets me thinking about how do you truly value data for this saas companies? Like if we were buying these dying saas companies at 2x ARR before (as example), maybe there is a better metric. Idk, just thinking out loud here.

9. It feels like a good chunk of legacy software won't make it to the agentic era, especially anything built around people clicking through a lot of screens.

10. Every company I talked to wants to pipe its internal data into one place and expose it to agents through MCP. Then they look at the data and realize it's a mess: five versions of the same customer, old Slack channels, PDFs nobody can search. Cleaning that up feels like a big consulting opportunity!

11. A lot of founders are building the basic building blocks for agents: APIs, data layers and tools. Some of the companies I saw barely have a UI because the main user is an agent. I really believe the startups that build primitives to this agentic era will do extremely well. Building blocks is the best way to think about it.

12. Labs can get plenty of training data, but it's harder to get real examples of agents failing inside companies. Whoever has those logs has something valuable.

13. Someone running a big consumer company told me the next fight is over memory. The model that remembers the most about you wins, and the smartest model matters less than people think.

14. Physical AI came up a lot. Astra I think was the first model that got people into AI can actually do CAD, and I think a lot of people are thinking what does vibe manufacturing really look like. The line I keep thinking about came from a robotics founder: the hardest problems in AI are deployment problems now, not research problems. Their robots work on their own, call a human when they get stuck, and every one of those calls becomes training data.

15. Cybersecurity companies are having a moment and are actually cool companies to build now, especially the ones that clean up after a breach. Every agent with access to your systems is a new door into your company, and a lot of those doors were left open. 

16. Some startups are worth more dead than alive now. A shutdown company with 5 years of Slack, email and code can get paid for licensing all of it. I wouldn't be surprised if founders start factoring that into when they shut down.

17. People are starting to talk about monetizing the agent web. It feels really early, but when the most popular user of the internet is an agent, what startups should you be building?

18. I think agent insurance is coming. Once an agent makes an expensive mistake, insurers will want audits before they cover anyone.

19. Several people said the hire they want most is someone with taste who can write evals. The models are getting good at generating ideas, so the hard part is judging which ones are good.

20. New trend I observed: startup raises VC, uses venture dollars to become a creator, startup fails, founder falls back on being a full-time creator and incubates other products bootstrapped.

21. Getting SIGNIFICANT distribution is HARD right now. Founders are sponsoring buses, buying billboards like crazy and throwing parties with famous DJs to get noticed. Kinda feels dotcom era in that sense. 

Attention is what's scarce! The growth guy going viral sharing his UGC strategy from Wispr Flow is a good example. It's the sauce everyone wants, and I truly believe there are probably only 50 people on the planet who know how to scale these types of businesses efficiently in this era.

Always good to get that dose of SF. I felt sooo lucky to have such an incredible trip during such an incredible time in building businesses. Surreal in so many ways. 

Happy to be home and locked in.

Until next time!

text:
Watched an awesome talk by the Head of AI at Coatue ($93bn hedge fund) today. 

@fyxlong walked through his approach to applying AI in financial services + the complexity & compression challenge enterprises must wrestle with as they diffuse the technology. 

Here are some of the notes I took: 

The decision function.
- His mental model: a hedge fund is a function that takes in two parameters (external context & internal context) and spits out one tuple (aka decision): investment selection, size, and timing
- He says achieving this is a compression problem of taking in all of the world's information & spitting out a single decision. 
- Principle: everything an investor can see on their screens at work, an agent should be able to see via API. 
- Data sources he focuses on: external is news, prices and filings via api. Internal is current positions, liquidity and risk requirements, past case studies, and history with a sector or management team.
- Huge advantage: Coatue has a decades-long culture of rigorously documenting and capturing all of the internal context fed into the function. 
- The reality of this function: "I probably can't just take all of that data, jam them into a context window, and get my three magic numbers and go home. It can't be that easy."

The over-simplified version of this decision function. 
Step 1: Gather internal/external data
Step 2: Analyze the data
Step 3: Make the decision 
- Every step has an input and an output and the input for the subsequent step is derived from the output of the previous step. 
- Each one of these steps has dozens of substeps and within each one of these substeps, you have to pick the optimal tool for the job. 

Picking the right tool for the job. 
- Every line in the function should leverage the optimal runner: who or what does each step. 
- Runner options: deterministic code, class ML, an LLM, or a person.
- Code is fast, reliable, and cheap. Great for use cases like "if PE ratio <15, do this". 
- Classic ML is great because you can model much more complex relationships vs. pure deterministic code. 
- LLMs are great for even more complex relationships like summarizing a transcript. 
- People still matter. For meeting a company's management team, "I probably don't want to send an LLM or an AI agent in to do that. I probably don't want to send an if statement into that meeting." 
- "There is no glory in automating things for the sake of automating things. The goal is not to take as many things LLM'd as possible. The goal is to maximize absolute quality for each of these steps." 

The realistic version of this function. 
- The real function isn't just a linear statement. There's all kinds of branching logic & tons of ways to fork the path the function takes (see image below). 
- And then each one of these steps in this far more complex branched function has an optimal runner, or really in practice, multiple runners per step.  
- And then there are so many other nobs you can pull outside of just the branched logic. Model size, thinking effort, hooks, skills, the list goes on. 

Simplifying such a multivariate problem. 
- The key question: "What can I actually compartmentalize in a way that we can understand and evaluate?"
- "If you don't have a North Star to hill climb against, you're just kind of… fidgeting around."
- Every data source has its own chain of steps, so the firm's real graph of its decision function is "massively complex." (see image below) 
- He estimates at least 10 knobs per node with at least 20 valid values each, which makes the search space "basically infinite."
- The hard part is laying it out in a way people can understand technically and also "absorb culturally", inside the org. "That is the great challenge of applying AI in investing."

Beyond investing
- What he's really describing is "creating a state machine that can take information from the world and understand it well enough to make coherent decisions."
- The same pattern applies to policy, nonprofits, drug discovery and corporate strategy.

text:
一个人是有气运的吗？气运是可以被算出来的？

我觉得是有的，至少我越来越愿意相信，一个人的人生确实有某种起伏和周期。最近抖音网红组团来 𝕏，让我想起上一波圈外大网红和币圈产生交集的时期，大概是2022年前后。当时很有代表性的一个人，就是台湾 YouTuber 一哥 Joeman（九妹）。

我印象里，那几年他和币圈走得挺近，有好几个币安的线下活动他都会去。

我和 Joeman 有一些共同朋友，但更有意思的是，我们竟然还找过同一个算命师傅。

这就是另一个故事了。之前我在台北龙山寺地下街，找过一位女师傅算紫微斗数。算到一半，突然看到墙上挂着她和 Joeman 的合照。我就顺口问了一句：老师，你怎么看 Joeman 的运势？

看过 Joeman 500元平价算命对决6000元奢华算命 那期的朋友，应该知道我说的是哪个师傅。师傅当时大意是说，Joeman 这几年会有一些波折，但整体还是向好的。后来 Joeman 确实经历了一些风波，好像是查税的事情，但是无伤大雅，我也一直记得这件事。

不过，真正有意思的故事发生在去年。

2025年11月，Joeman 又拍了一期算命影片，这次请到台湾最近颇有名气的八字风水老师徐玉兰。徐玉兰看完他的八字，说他命盘里木比较多，2023、2024年过得相对辛苦，而2026丙午火年对他很有利。

Joeman 听完还兴奋地问：所以2026年有可能是我生涯的巅峰吗？徐玉兰说，她觉得是。甚至预测他未来可能拿很多奖项，名气走出台湾，感情上也有机会出现重大进展。

结果更神奇的事情来了。

当时 Threads 上有一位网友，居然对同一张命盘给出了完全相反的解释。这个网友说，「joeman的用神是火土金，但這邊我必須要逆風，我認為火土金是他的忌神，用神是水木。」Joeman 2026年恐怕不好过，可能会因为投机行为出问题，而且跟女人脱不了关系。

这条预测发在2025年11月23日。

九个月后的2026年8月，Joeman 和前女友蕭伊的感情风波真的爆发了。从私下约女演员吃饭、接送回家，到凌晨煮牛肉面的争议，台湾社交媒体吵得沸沸扬扬。Joeman 后来也公开道歉，承认自己在感情里有很多做错的地方。

那条九个月前的命理分析，又被网友翻出来朝圣。

当然，感情纠纷中各方的说法需要区分，命理预测究竟准不准，也很难凭一个案例下结论。

但这件事真的很有戏剧性。

更巧的是，今年我有一位台中的阿姨，也请了徐玉兰去家里看风水。听她讲，徐老师本人气场很特别，连家里的小动物都很喜欢亲近她。

目前 joeman 的事业运也还在？不过在桃花上的确摔了一跤，怎么绕了一圈，从币圈、YouTuber、龙山寺地下街，到台中阿姨家的风水，最后又串到同一个人身上？

我越来越觉得，人这一生确实有很多奇妙的交集。

至于气运究竟是什么，我也说不清楚。

命理学有命理学的解释，心理学有心理学的解释。人会记住那些后来应验的预测，也容易忘记没有应验的部分。

但我想，所谓气运，也许还包含了一个人的性格、选择、时代环境，以及他身边不断变化的人际关系。

同样的一个人，在不同的年份，可能因为同一种性格而成功，也可能因为同一种性格而跌倒。

一个人的优点和缺点，很多时候本来就是同一件事。敢冒险的人容易抓住机会，也容易惹上麻烦；特别有野心的人可以成就事业，也可能被自己的欲望反噬。

所以我现在对算命的态度是：可以听，可以参考，也可以觉得有趣，但别把自己的人生完全交给一张命盘。

命可以拿来算，路还是得自己走。

至于一个人有没有气运，我还是相信有的。

只不过运来了能不能接住，运走了能不能稳住，恐怕比算出哪一年走运更加重要。🙏

@Balancer voted to bless an independent fork of its technology by @maxyz_xyz, with no grant, no branding and no link to $BAL or its governance.

It follows the September 29th vote, where 51 voters rejected what Avant called "an official, funded reincarnation," 69.9% No.

MAXYZ will now cover the fork's costs itself. It says partners still see a path forward, and it wants explicit consent so forking "is not against the wishes of the DAO."

Token holders also approved MAXYZ's request for access to Balancer's internal security-docs repo and its @immunefi bug bounty account. MAXYZ says it wants to be "fully aware of all of its security design choices and reported findings."

@avantayman backed both for Avant, which runs Balancer pools that wrap Aave's interest-bearing aTokens. Avant would rather see the technology continued by people who already know it than watch it go dark, and named the cost: "Security access is the one piece that is not free. The security-docs repo and the Immunefi account hold undisclosed findings and program access. We support MAXYZ having what they need to ship a fork that does not reintroduce known issues. That is in every remaining user's interest."

9 voters cast 6,026,482 BAL: 90.5% Yes, 0.0% No, 9.5% Abstain. Quorum cleared at 120.5%.

text:
@MIM_Spell voted on a plan to wind down Abracadabra that would pay holders of $MIM, the protocol's stablecoin, ~$0.04 per MIM from ~$900K of reclaimable lending-vault collateral.

The proposal says a series of hacks left ~$21M of bad debt and "no viable path back to parity," meaning no route back to $1.

Under the plan:
- The team would reclaim collateral from eligible lending vaults, expecting to rescue ~99.75%, and swap it all to ETH
- Balances would be recorded no earlier than October 20th
- Borrowers would get their collateral value minus their debt, counted at $1 per MIM
- Holders would split the rest pro-rata, claimed through @merkl_xyz

The proposal ruled out raising interest rates to force liquidations, where "the first users to sell" could get up to $1 while "those selling last would receive close to nothing." It also cited @LayerZero_Core's December 15th withdrawal deadline for its V1 relayer, which puts ~$1M of collateral at risk.

Outside the vote, @Protos reports @moo9000 calls the move "treasury looting." Protos also notes the plan leaves out ~$8.3M that @PharosWatch reported leaving Abracadabra-controlled Safe wallets on July 14th.

2 wallets cast 396,163,281 SPELL: 100.0% For (approve the plan) (reject it and work on another solution). That is 13.2% of the space's 3B quorum, which the proposal says can't be changed because the admin keys sit with unreachable former team members, and ~128.2% of the 30% bar the proposal set for itself. Quorum was not met, so the proposal failed and no choice was adopted.
