Barker 上已经挖出 430 万+ 枚 $PAPER，到底值多少钱？-----挖矿算账篇

先说结论：挖一枚 PAPER 的成本在 $0.015 以下，大概率划算。直接在 Papertrade 亏着挖，现在一枚约 $0.059；用 Barker 对冲挖，页面按默认参数实时估算约 $0.0095，大家实际跑下来平均每枚约 1 美分。

用 Barker 挖不用自己盯盘换腿，选市场、填金额、点一下，开仓、止损、重开全自动，挖到的 PAPER 一键质押、分红一键领取，入口放在下面！

【这几天的账】

｜每天总亏损：约 2,000 万美元
｜每天净亏损：380～530 万美元
｜赢家拿走：总亏损的 77%～83%
｜现在的分红：每 1 万枚质押的 PAPER，一天约分 9 U

最大的变数就是 House 被打穿：House 净值变负，赢家的盈利要排队等兑付。不过按现在每天 2,000 万的亏损，模型里 House 约 2.7 天就能补回来；日亏损掉到 100 万，补窟窿才要 44 天左右。

所以多少成本挖算划算：

｜$0.015 以下：大概率划算
｜$0.03：每天 2,000 万的亏损能撑 90 天，就可能划算
｜$0.05：要每天 2,000 万的亏损撑半年以上

Barker 对冲挖：页面估算约 $0.0095，实际平均约 1 美分，都在 $0.015 这条线以下。

【为什么对冲挖便宜这么多】

直接亏着挖：每亏 1 美元拿约 17 枚，一枚约 $0.059，比上面大部分估值都贵。

对冲挖：同一个账户里开一多一空两条腿。价格不管往哪走，总有一腿先亏到止损，这笔亏损照样给 PAPER；另一腿同时在赚，赚到止盈就平掉。两腿一抵，大部分亏损被赚了回来，真正花掉的只有一小部分。

同样亏 1,000 U，按现在的挖矿率估算：

｜直接亏着挖：约 1.7 万枚
｜Barker 对冲挖，页面默认参数（ETH，100 倍，止损 0.3%，止盈 0.6%）：约 10.5 万枚
｜同样参数挖 BTC：约 11 万枚

【怎么挖，四步】

1. 打开 Barker 的 Paper 对冲 Farm 页面不用登录，先调参数看每枚成本
2. 选「一键配置」：市场（ETH / BTC）、总投入（最少 30 USDC）、杠杆。
3. 点「一键开启」：连钱包 → 把 USDC 存进你自己的 Papertrade 账户 → 授权交易密钥 → 开跑。USDC 不在 HyperEVM 上，页面里「兑换 / 跨链」能直接换过来；钱包留一点 HYPE 付 gas
4. 挖到的 PAPER 点「一键质押」才有分红，分红点「一键领取」。嫌麻烦就签「自动质押和申领」，攒够了自动质押、自动领

授权的是一把只能在你 Papertrade 账户里开仓、平仓的交易密钥，不能提现、不能转账，随时可撤。

text:
上午跟 StandX 项目方电话聊了几分钟，了解情况如下：

1/ StandX 项目决定关闭。

2/ 会以 DUSD 的方式给所有有积分的用户，发放空投，作为最后的补偿；之前参与了 KOL 轮的用户，也会根据贡献度再给一点空投，金额不会很多。KOL 轮的本金，我了解到的，今年 4 月已经全部退还。

3/ 创业之初，团队对 StandX 项目的期待是大成，现在肯定是没有达到预期；最后发币割一波，不是团队的风格；继续苟着也没啥意思，时间和机会成本不小。长痛不如短痛。

我也创业过、关过项目，能理解 StandX 团队的想法。项目之前没有面向 VC 融资。

不确定 StandX 团队是否在这一年多赚到钱了？收入主要是撸毛玩家们贡献的手续费、成本主要是团队工资和服务器。项目方的说法是亏钱了。

回顾 StandX 项目早期，之所以快速得到巨大关注，有一个重要的背景是：Aster 的币价当时涨得非常猛，而 StandX 团队同样出自币安 (之前介绍过 https://t.co/vtcRg8RzFA)，错过 Aster 的用户和 KOL 对 StandX 抱有非常高的预期，其实就是典型的 FOMO 了。

今年以来，行业对于 DeFi 类、应用类项目的期待，全面转向了对已验证的 PMF、真实用户、真实收入/利润的期待，不符合这些标准的项目，相比以往会更加困难

Blast, Abstract, StandX 相继关闭只是一个缩影，当没有链上新山寨币的浪潮爆发，更多小交易所，不管是 CEX 还是 Perp DEX，在流动性、用户增长上面临的挑战时都会更难。

晚上听了 StandX 的 co-founder @StandX_Justin 参加的一个 𝕏 Space，简单记录下关键信息。

Ethena 先做稳定币，在 $USDe 达到 100 多亿规模后，也会进入 Perp 业务；而 Hyperliquid 先做 Perp DEX，后面又推出了 $USDH (由生态项目来做)。

坚持不做 copycat

StandX 会对界面 UI 进行大幅 redesign
从第一性原理出发
重新思考 Perp DEX 应该长什么样子
每一行代码都是自己写

首先是一定要从官网加入 waitlist
产品内测只会开放给加入到了 waitlist 的人

4/ $DUSD 收益来源

DUSD 跟 BFUSD 和 USDe 的收益原理类似
也是这个周期市场上最流行的策略
StandX 拿到用户 mint 的 DUSD 之后，通过稳健的 Delta 中性策略去生息，再把利息返还给用户
最近一周 TVL 从 $30M 涨到 $140M，也是超出了团队预期

5/ 关键时间点

主要都在 Q4 了

1) 国庆结束后，10 月内会上线 testnet，会持续 3-4 周
2) 计划 11 月会上实盘，主要是完善风控体系、基础产品体验，这样才能支撑更多币对、杠杆倍数

跟 Lista, Pendle 的很多合作都已经谈好了
但还是需要先 focus 在基础产品的开发上
更多主流 DeFi 协议的合作会持续推进

◦ 联创 @StandX_Justin 之前是币安合约业务的增长负责人，更早是在传统金融 (衍生品行业) ，2019 年加入币安。
◦ 另一位技术背景的合伙人，更早是在 Amber 负责链上交易策略，再之前是在高盛负责写相关的交易系统。

团队在币安做永续合约业务多年，相关背景比较容易找币安的员工进行 verify。团队在币安工作期间，积累了很多难得的一手经验。

text:
Zenith has joined the ERC3643 Association, bringing our experience in interoperability standards and settlement design to the work on compliant tokenization.

@ERC3643Org was originally created in 2018 as the T-REX (Token for Regulated EXchanges) protocol by Tokeny Solutions. ERC-3643 is an open-source token standard for the issuance, management and transfer of permissioned tokens. It enables issuers to enforce compliance requirements, including investor eligibility and transfer restrictions, even on public blockchains. The ERC3643 Association brings together TradFi institutions and blockchain technology providers to advance the adoption of this standard. Its founding members include: Apex Group, @ArchaxEx , @BitstampSupport, @Capgemini, @DLA_Piper, @InvescoUS, @0xPolygon Labs, @TokenySolutions, and others.

This matters because tokenizing a regulated asset is only the beginning. Once issued, these assets need to participate in financial workflows involving settlement, collateral, lending, and trading, often across different applications and environments.

That second step is what Zenith is built for. As the EVM and SVM extension for @CantonNetwork, Zenith allows Solidity applications to interact atomically with Canton-native assets and workflows. This opens a path for applications using Ethereum standards such as ERC-3643 to connect with Canton's institutional financial infrastructure while retaining their established Ethereum tooling.

We look forward to working with the Association and its members as regulated tokens move into production.

More about the ERC3643 Association and its members: https://t.co/EOYFGBZA3E

author: sacha
quoted_text:
So not to go all Yudkowsky Monocause Theory.  But a lot of AI company talk that *sounds smart* did come from me, or me via Bostrom or other diffusion modes.  High-powered ideas like "recursive self-improvement" and "AGI" are ideas they did not invent themselves, but got off higher-quality outside thinkers.  There's a big intellectual history behind me in turn, but the AI companies did not study this history independently; they got it downstream of my writing it up.

I naturally spent some time trying to figure out what the positive vision for AGI and ASI would look like, back in the mid-2000s.

But I considered it a lower priority to write up.

And AI company executives are not at the intellectual level where they can invent coherent answers to questions like that, if they don't have my answer sheet to copy from.

They can't tell you what the positive vision for AGI or ASI looks like, because I didn't prioritize writing up that part of my earlier thoughts.  They can't copy it off from the same answer sheet they used to produce smart-sounding conversation like "general intelligence" or "recursive self-improvement" or "extinction risk" or "AI alignment problem".

If they're not reading off my answer sheet, AI company executives are pretty ordinary as intellectuals.  Being able to spend billions on GPUs does not make you a genius inventor, even if we're used to amazing inventions coming from genius rather than black-box optimization.  AI company executives are not going to give you better answers about "what's the positive vision" than any other random intellectual challenged with a question beyond their wits.

If you start hearing good-sounding answers from Anthropic or OpenAI, it means that Mythos or HPIM advanced to the point of learning how to sound convincing about utopia to humans.

I did do an *abstract* writeup on constraints and requirements over positive ASI scenarios (see eg "31 Laws of Fun"); but that does AI companies no good, because they would need to be able to sketch a concrete AGI scenario from those abstract ideas.  That again is beyond them if I have not done their homework.

It is of course not in humanity's interest that I try to do this homework for the AI companies now.  It would only be a lie.  They have no utopia to offer.

The IRS sent armed agents into a family bakery and drained $68,382 from its bank account.

Their “crime”? Depositing their OWN CASH in amounts under $10,000.

Then the government demanded ANOTHER $160,000 and a guilty plea to a FELONY.

The IRS called it “structuring”: deliberately keeping deposits small to dodge bank reporting rules.

DAVID VOCATURA: “I said to them, ‘Maybe I should get a lawyer.’ And they said, ‘You don’t need one, step in the back.’”

“Until the day they came in, I had no idea what structuring was.”

“I’m a law-abiding citizen. I can’t remember the last time I got a speeding ticket.”

Nearly three years after seizing the money, a prosecutor came back with a deal that carried up to FOUR YEARS IN PRISON:

DAVID VOCATURA: “They wanted us to pay another additional $160,000 in fines and plead to a felony charge of structuring.”

They refused.

You bake bread for three generations.
You pay your taxes.
You put your own money in the bank.
And the IRS treats you like a criminal, demanding nearly a quarter million dollars.

CONTEXT: Fortunately, the IRS didn’t get away with this one. Hours after the Institute for Justice sued, the IRS agreed to return all $68,382.22. Two weeks later, it withdrew a grand jury subpoena demanding eight years of the bakery’s business records. Crazy that they tried to ruin a business over depositing money into their own bank account.

服务器有两个核，1G内存，每月1T的流量，走的协议是Trojan，配了自有的域名，和加密证书，代理访问会伪装成网页
费用：50刀每年
IP：自带独享的固定IP，不额外收费，重启虚拟机，关机IP都不会变

第二层备用：Google cloud搭建的VPS（东京机房）
这是刚回国，大概六年前搭建的，一直用到现在，我一直以为东京机房会快，直到最近才发现所有gcp的流量在东京会传回谷歌总部绕一圈才到我这边，所以现在这个vps延迟特别严重，这也是我最近准备重搭vps的原因

费用：按用量计算，最低月费5刀，用的多会到10刀

IP：新开虚拟机会分配一个临时日本的IP，但是关机重启会换IP，优势是IP非常干净原生，基本上不会有被污染然后被封的风险

第三层兜底：海獭的机场
机场没啥好说的，选择一个靠谱的不跑路的就行

费用：15块100g，100g对我来说经常不够用

IP：完全是机场随机分配，存在被污染的风险，这个问题见仁见智

域名：独立域名每年12刀左右

刚刚把主力切换成搬瓦工了，但是这里还是存在一个潜在风险，虽然分配给我的是独立的IP，但是历史上好像发生过搬瓦工整个网段被封。

对于国内玩X 的朋友来说，VPN的IP干不干净也很重要，已经看到很多人因为IP不干净被封了，所以大家用VPN一定需要注意。

text:
最近在给硅谷 AI Startup 做增长，分享一些经验：找 UGC，而不是 KOL；找 KOS，而不是 KOC

做了几年全球 KOL Marketing，接触过欧美、日韩、东南亚等市场的 2000 多位 Creator，最近越来越觉得，AI Startup 的增长逻辑，和传统消费品牌完全不一样。

尤其是早期 AI 产品，预算有限、产品迭代快、用户认知还没建立。如果还按照传统的 KOL Marketing 逻辑，找大博主、谈报价、发视频、看曝光，ROI 很容易惨不忍睹。

分享几个我自己的观察。

1️⃣找 UGC，而不是 KOL

很多 AI Startup 一上来就想找几十万、上百万粉丝的科技博主合作。但实际上，早期产品更缺的不是曝光，而是能够证明产品价值的内容。

一个有 100 万粉丝的科技 KOL，可能只能给你带来一波短期流量；但一个只有 3000 粉丝、真正理解产品的 Creator，可能帮你跑通一个高转化的内容模板。

我更倾向于寻找能够持续生产 UGC风格内容的创作者，而不是单纯买 KOL 的流量。

尤其是 AI 工具，用户最想看的往往不是产品发布会，而是这个工具能帮我完成什么？比原来的工作流快多少？能不能直接复刻？

真正有价值的是内容资产，而不只是创作者的粉丝资产。

2️⃣找 KOS，而不是 KOC

KOC强调普通消费者的真实体验，KOS（Key Opinion Sales）则更接近懂产品、懂场景、能够影响购买决策的人。

我觉得 AI Startup 尤其需要后者。

比如你做的是 AI Coding 产品，与其找泛科技博主，不如找真正每天用 Cursor、Claude Code、Codex 写代码的开发者。

做 AI Design，就去找设计师、独立创作者。做 AI Agent，就去找正在利用 Agent 自动化工作流的人。

这些人的粉丝可能不多，但受众足够精准，而且他们知道用户真正的痛点。

AI 产品的投放，本质上是在寻找能够替你完成用户教育的人。

3️⃣不要先找达人，先找到有效的 Content Format

我见过不少 Startup，产品刚上线就开始大规模联系达人，结果投了几十条视频，播放量还不错，注册却寥寥无几。

问题可能根本不是达人，而是内容形式没有跑通。

我的建议是先测试 3～5 种不同的内容方向，例如Before / After：使用 AI 前后的效率对比、Tutorial：30 秒完成一个具体任务、Challenge：用 AI 挑战过去需要几小时的工作、Comparison：和竞品做同场景对比、Build in Public等

每种形式找几个小体量 Creator 测试，观察留存、点击、注册和激活，再决定放大哪一种。

4️⃣全球化投放不是把英文视频翻译成十种语言

这是很多 AI Startup 容易犯的错误。

美国用户可能更关注效率提升、个人生产力和商业回报；日本市场往往需要更清晰的操作演示与信任建立；东南亚市场则需要结合当地用户的实际使用场景与价格敏感度。

当然，这些只是市场假设，最终还是要通过数据验证，不能简单用国家给用户贴标签。

我个人比较推荐先在英语市场跑通内容模型，再寻找当地 Native Creator 进行本地化创作，而不只是翻译字幕。

甚至同一个 AI 产品，不同市场应该强调完全不同的 Use Case。

Localization ≠ Translation。

5️⃣不要迷信 Viral，要建立 Creator Growth Loop

很多团队把一条视频做到百万播放，当成一次非常成功的 Marketing Campaign。

但如果第二天流量归零，产品留存也没有改善，那这次投放的长期价值可能很有限。

Creator 生产内容 → 测试不同 Hook → 追踪注册与激活 → 找出高转化模板 → 复用到更多 Creator → 将有效内容用于广告投放 → 持续优化。

6️⃣AI Startup 应该把 Creator 当成产品增长的一部分，而不只是营销渠道

我认为这是最重要的一点。

传统品牌找达人，通常是为了让更多人知道品牌。

但对于 AI Startup，Creator 还可以帮助团队发现真实 Use Case，测试不同的用户群体，甚至反向影响产品 Roadmap。

比如，一个 AI 工具最初定位给设计师，但投放过程中发现很多电商卖家正在用它批量生成商品素材，而且付费意愿更强。

这时候，Creator Marketing 实际上帮助团队找到了新的 ICP，所以早期 AI 产品最应该追踪的，未必是 CPM、CPE，甚至不只是 CAC。

而是哪些 Creator 带来了真正激活、留存和付费的用户。

未来 AI Startup 的 Creator Marketing，会越来越像一套轻量化的增长实验系统。

一个拥有 1000 个精准用户的专业创作者，可能比一个拥有 100 万泛娱乐粉丝的博主更有商业价值。

而真正厉害的增长团队，不是认识多少头部 KOL，而是能否以足够低的成本，持续找到有效的内容、创作者和用户场景。

不要花钱购买影响力，要花钱验证增长。

author: ViktorBunin

text:
being a fintech isn’t enough anymore. everyone wants to be a bank:

a growing number of fintech companies want to own the banks behind their apps.

the reason becomes pretty clear when you look at how these businesses work.

you can build the app, acquire the customers and handle the entire user experience. but if another bank holds the license, that bank still has a say in which products you can offer, what risks you can take and how much it costs to serve each customer.

owning a bank can give you more control over those decisions. it can also let you take deposits and use that funding to lend.

that changes the economics of the business. it also changes what you’re responsible for.

why companies are buying the bank

@Chime is a useful example.

it agreed to pay $590M for Stride Bank (@BankStride), a banking partner it has worked with for more than seven years. Chime projects more than $100M in net synergies from reducing partner-bank fees, expanding lending and lowering its funding costs.

the deal is expected to close in the first half of 2027, subject to approvals. those savings are still projections, but they explain why owning the bank could be worth the investment.

a fintech that already has millions of customers has already done much of the work of building distribution. acquiring a bank can help it offer more products to those customers and keep more of the revenue those products generate.

@Payward, the parent of Kraken (@krakenfx), is pursuing a similar opportunity through its agreement to acquire Saldo Bank.

the acquisition would add European banking capabilities, including interest-bearing deposits and lending, to its existing infrastructure. closing is expected in 2027, subject to regulatory approval.

the same interest in owning banking infrastructure is showing up across Latin America.

@cocoscap completed its acquisition of Banco Voii (@banco_voii) in Argentina on June 29. @Revolut received BCRA approval to acquire Cetelem in September, although that approval is separate from closing the acquisition and launching services to customers.

@nubank agreed to acquire Porto Real in Brazil. in that case, the acquisition also addresses rules around the use of banking names by adding a banking license to Nubank’s existing authorizations.

the reasons vary by company and market. some want better economics. some want new capabilities. others have a specific regulatory requirement to meet.

buying an existing bank is only one route

companies can also apply to build a bank from scratch.

Nubank, @mercury and Revolut received conditional approvals to establish national banks in the US.

for digital asset companies, national trust banks are another route, with a different scope of activities.

in December 2025, the OCC announced conditional approvals for new national trust banks for @circle and @Ripple, alongside conditional approvals for @BitGo, Fidelity Digital Assets (@DigitalAssets) and @Paxos to convert their state-chartered entities to the federal regime.

Agora (@withAUSD), the group behind AUSD, received preliminary conditional approval on September 18, 2026, to establish Agora National Trust Bank. its plan includes moving AUSD issuance into the bank once established. it still needs final authorization to open.

this distinction matters when you’re evaluating what these companies will actually be able to offer.

a charter focused on custody, stablecoin issuance or trust services does not automatically provide the same permissions as a full-service commercial bank. you have to look at the specific entity, its approved activities and the conditions attached.

“received approval” also doesn’t necessarily mean customers can start using the bank.

@Mercury continues to operate through partner banks while working toward final approval. Revolut’s announcement identifies remaining approvals from the FDIC, the Fed and the OCC.

the economics have to work after the acquisition

owning a bank can reduce some dependencies, but it brings costs that a fintech previously shared with, or paid to, its banking partners.

the company needs capital, liquidity, experienced management, compliance systems and an operation that can meet ongoing supervisory requirements.

regulators also assess the buyer. the ECB, for example, reviews financial soundness, reputation, management suitability, continued prudential compliance and money-laundering risk.

LevelField (@LevelfieldEx) shows why the funding requirements matter. Burling Bank confirmed that its proposed acquisition did not close because the buyer missed the regulatory deadline to raise capital. the bank’s board decided to continue independently.

even when a transaction closes, attracting deposits is only part of the job.

if customers move their savings to your app because you offer the highest rate, you need to understand how much of that money will stay when the rate changes. you also need to earn enough from your permitted activities to cover funding, operating costs and credit losses.

owning the license gives you more ways to build the business. it doesn’t make those economics work automatically.

what this means for the next generation of fintech

the acquisitions are happening in both directions.

@CapitalOne completed its acquisition of @brexHQ in April. @Mastercard completed its acquisition of @BVNKFinance in August. established financial companies are also buying technology, distribution and stablecoin capabilities that would take time to build themselves.

my read is that these companies want to handle more of the customer’s financial life within their own businesses.

once someone uses your app to get paid, keep savings and make payments, there is an opportunity to serve their borrowing and investment needs too.

i think this is where consumer fintech is heading: companies trying to become the place where you get paid, keep your savings, spend and borrow.

owning the bank can make more of that possible within one business. whether it is worth doing comes down to how much customers use it, what it costs to run, and whether the company can manage the risks.

Some choice quotes from the report: 

Banks as cops: these efforts distracted the banks from objective assessments of financial risks and increased the risk of misuse by some to refuse service to subjectively disfavored customers or industries. Moreover, it put banks in a quasi-legislative position of limiting banking services—or imposing values-based conditions on the availability of banking services—for lawful businesses disfavored by some activists and political leaders who lack the legal basis or legislative power to restrict or outlaw these business activities

Mere allegations: Mere allegations, negative press, or negative reviews contributed to some banks declining to serve average Americans, even in the absence of any validation of the underlying facts or concerns; yet some banks were able to find ways to get comfortable with the reputation risks posed by high-net-worth clients.

Inconsistency: The OCC found that, in response to general reputation risk policies, bank employees escalated customers or prospective customers that held potentially contested viewpoints outside the perceived “mainstream” and that those views were often equated with higher potential reputation risk. The OCC found that decisions related to such escalations were not universally consistent across transactions the OCC sampled, illustrating the subjective nature of the banks’ ambiguous and open-ended reputation risk policies

NGOs: The banks also relied on various sources to inform these decisions, including the results of negative news searches and non-traditional sources, such as the opinions of advocacy organizations

Whipsaw: When banks rely on difficult-to-quantify factors to decide whether to provide financial services, there is significant risk that bank decisions will whipsaw back and forth with the current political or social climate. This report confirms that value judgments and assumptions regarding the current views held by elected officials and policy makers can factor into banks’ decision making. The report also observes that as the political and social climate changed, so too did banks’ application of industry restrictions. Past experience suggests that industries may continue to suffer this whipsaw effect with the change of each administration or Congress, even in the absence of statutory changes.

text: For over two decades, BitTorrent has shown that distributed networks scale best when idle capacity meets real utility. #BTTInferGrid applies that exact logic to AI inference.
author: BitTorrent
quoted_text:
𝗕𝗶𝘁𝗧𝗼𝗿𝗿𝗲𝗻𝘁’𝘀 𝗘𝘃𝗼𝗹𝘂𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻: 𝗙𝗿𝗼𝗺 𝗗𝗶𝘀𝘁𝗿𝗶𝗯𝘂𝘁𝗲𝗱 𝗙𝗶𝗹𝗲 𝗦𝗵𝗮𝗿𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝘁𝗼 𝗗𝗲𝗰𝗲𝗻𝘁𝗿𝗮𝗹𝗶𝘇𝗲𝗱 𝗔𝗜 𝗖𝗼𝗺𝗽𝘂𝘁𝗲

The next phase of digital infrastructure is not just about moving data. It is about making computing resources more accessible, productive, and efficient.

Since 2001, BitTorrent has demonstrated how distributed networks can enable participants to share resources without relying entirely on centralized infrastructure.

Now, that underlying principle is being explored in a different domain: decentralized AI computing.

This is where #BTTInferGrid enters the conversation.

♤ 𝗙𝗿𝗼𝗺 𝗙𝗶𝗹𝗲 𝗗𝗶𝘀𝘁𝗿𝗶𝗯𝘂𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻 𝘁𝗼 𝗖𝗼𝗺𝗽𝘂𝘁𝗲 𝗗𝗶𝘀𝘁𝗿𝗶𝗯𝘂𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻

Traditional file-sharing networks coordinate the distribution of data across participating peers.

Decentralized AI compute applies a related concept to computing capacity, connecting available GPU resources with workloads that require processing power.

As AI inference demand expands, distributed compute networks could offer developers additional options beyond conventional cloud infrastructure.

The principle remains familiar: coordinate independent resources to serve a broader network of users.

♤ 𝗙𝗼𝗿 𝗚𝗣𝗨 𝗣𝗿𝗼𝘃𝗶𝗱𝗲𝗿𝘀 — 𝗺𝗮𝗸𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗶𝗱𝗹𝗲 𝗰𝗮𝗽𝗮𝗰𝗶𝘁𝘆 𝗽𝗿𝗼𝗱𝘂𝗰𝘁𝗶𝘃𝗲

AI workloads require substantial computing power, yet some GPU capacity may remain underutilized.

BTTInferGrid explores a model in which providers can contribute available GPU resources to AI inference workloads, creating an opportunity to monetize otherwise idle computing capacity.

Unused resources → Network participation → Potential additional revenue.

The long-term opportunity depends on whether providers can earn sustainable returns while delivering consistent performance.

♤ 𝗙𝗼𝗿 𝗗𝗲𝘃𝗲𝗹𝗼𝗽𝗲𝗿𝘀 — 𝗲𝘅𝗽𝗹𝗼𝗿𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗺𝗼𝗿𝗲 𝗰𝗼𝗺𝗽𝘂𝘁𝗲 𝗼𝗽𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻𝘀

Developers building AI applications need computing resources that balance cost, speed, availability, and reliability.

A distributed inference marketplace could expand their access to GPU capacity and introduce alternatives to depending exclusively on a limited number of providers.

However, decentralization alone does not guarantee lower prices or better performance. Hardware compatibility, workload scheduling, data security, uptime, and output verification remain essential.

𝗧𝗵𝗲 𝗕𝗶𝗴𝗴𝗲𝗿 𝗣𝗶𝗰𝘁𝘂𝗿𝗲 — 𝗰𝗼𝗼𝗿𝗱𝗶𝗻𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗱𝗶𝘀𝘁𝗿𝗶𝗯𝘂𝘁𝗲𝗱 𝗿𝗲𝘀𝗼𝘂𝗿𝗰𝗲𝘀

The broader significance of BTTInferGrid lies in the infrastructure model it explores.

GPU providers contribute computing capacity.

AI developers bring inference demand.

The network aims to connect both sides through a coordinated marketplace.

If these components work effectively together, distributed compute could become a more practical part of the AI infrastructure landscape.

The challenge is turning the promise of decentralized participation into measurable value: competitive costs, dependable execution, sustainable incentives, and consistent results.

From sharing files to exploring AI compute, BitTorrent’s journey reflects an enduring infrastructure idea:

Resources become more useful when independent participants can contribute them to a network that connects supply with real demand.

That is the broader vision behind #BTTInferGrid.

@BitTorrent @justinsuntron

text:
.@UNCX_token was exploited across multiple chains for ~$1.5M. The root cause was inconsistent accounting of _totalTokenShares between release() and cancel(). This variable tracks the total outstanding shares of all schedules for a token.

Specifically, after release(), a schedule with _depositedShares = D and schedule.released = R has only D − R shares remaining in _totalTokenShares. However, cancel() removes D − V, where V is the recalculated vestedShare.

This accounting assumption can be broken through a donation followed by a top-up, which increases schedule.totalAmount while minting very few new shares and pushes V below R. Consequently, D − V exceeds the schedule’s remaining D − R shares, causing cancel() to deduct shares already removed by release(). This reduces the shared _totalTokenShares denominator and inflates the payout from the schedule retained by the attacker.

The key attack steps are illustrated using this exploit transaction:
https://t.co/se7slWXock
1. Set up three schedules: The attacker created schedules 5058, 5059, and 5060. They fully released 5059 and 5060 while retaining 5058 for the final withdrawal.
2. Donate: The attacker transferred tokens directly to the vesting contract, inflating the asset-per-share value without minting new shares.
3. Top up and cancel: The attacker topped up schedules 5059 and 5060 with future-vesting tokens. Due to the manipulated share price, the top-ups greatly increased schedule.totalAmount while minting very few new shares, pushing vestedShare below schedule.released. Cancelling the schedules then deducted previously released shares from _totalTokenShares again.
4. Extract profits: With _totalTokenShares artificially reduced, the attacker released schedule 5058 at an inflated redemption value and repaid the flash loan.

The attacker repeated this process to drain assets from the vulnerable contract.

UNCX Vesting V2: Security Incident Update

Following the security incident affecting our Vesting V2 contracts across several chains earlier today, we want to share an update on the measures taken, the affected tokens, and what comes next.

1. Security measures and containment

We have implemented several measures to prevent further exploitation of the affected contracts:

> Introduced substantial flat fees exceeding 1,000 ETH per lock.
> Removed all clients and contract interactions that previously allowed these fees to be bypassed.
> Increased token fees to the maximum permitted by the Vesting V2 contracts (5%), making repeated vesting top-ups economically unviable.

These measures are designed to prevent further exploitation through the identified methods. While our investigation and monitoring remain ongoing, we firmly believe we have taken the necessary steps available to us to contain the incident.

2. Scope of the incident

As previously communicated, all LP lockers remain unaffected, across every protocol and chain supported by UNCX.

The incident is isolated to UNCX Vesting V2. Our legacy vesting contracts are also unaffected and have undergone additional checks and review.

The incident currently involves 10 tokens across 4 chains:

Ethereum (6): $pepecoin, $EDGEN, $ZC, $X, $LO0P, $PAAL

Base (1): $IMO

BNB Chain (1): $BTCLE

Robinhood Chain (2): $CASHCAT, $RKST

3. Next steps for affected projects and communities

We are already in contact with most of the affected teams, communities or individuals impacted. 

We expect to share further guidance and next steps with affected teams this week.

We will also publish a comprehensive incident report covering the technical findings, financials, and the details of our proposed recovery plan.

Important: For all impacted tokens, we strongly advise against trading in the affected pools until further guidance is provided by the respective token teams. We will be coordinating directly with those teams over the coming days.

4. Investigation and recovery efforts

Our investigation remains active, and we are coordinating with law enforcement and @seal911.

To date, no funds have been returned by the attackers (primary and copycats) on any affected chain. We strongly encourage the responsible party to contact us directly to discuss a resolution.

We understand the seriousness of this incident for affected projects, holders, and communities. 

Our immediate priorities remain preventing further exploitation, establishing the full extent of the impact, and working closely with affected teams toward a recovery plan.

We will continue to communicate when any meaningful updates become available.

Thank you for your patience.

The UNCX Team

Ledger 调查用户丢币时，在一台受害者的硬件钱包里发现了额外装进去的窃密组件。按它 10 月 13 日披露的分析，用户初始化钱包、抄下屏幕上的 24 个助记词时，这个组件也在读取屏幕，再通过内置 eSIM 和移动网络把助记词传出去。拿到这组词，就能在另一台设备上恢复钱包、转走资产。

这套东西没有改动原来的安全芯片和操作系统。Ledger 官方说明也明确写着：只要原装安全芯片保持完整，真伪检测就无法识别这种额外植入的窃密硬件。芯片能证明自己是真的，机壳里却可能多了别的东西。

截至这份声明，Ledger 称已确认的相关资产损失都涉及东南亚经销商 CryptoBilis 售出的设备，并已要求该经销商停止销售。已确认的植入物证来自一台受害设备，其他受影响设备仍在调查。

来源：[Ledger 10 月 13 日调查声明](https://t.co/P7HLxiEevN) · [官方真伪检测能力说明](https://t.co/rjzyK0AP7q)

quoted_text:
Update from Ledger Donjon on the CryptoBilis investigation 🔽

@DonjonLedger is investigating Ledger signers sold by CryptoBilis, a reseller in Southeast Asia, that contained an unauthorized hardware implant. Ledger confirmed this on October 10th for one affected user's signer. All confirmed fund losses tied to the incident disclosed on October 9th involve signers sold through CryptoBilis. We have not verified a drain linked to a signer bought elsewhere. CryptoBilis has confirmed it stopped selling Ledger signers while the investigation continues.

Based on the Donjon's analysis of the attack, the implant sits inside the enclosure and reads the data shown on the screen. During setup, the signer displays the 24-word recovery phrase. When the implant detects these screens, its microcontroller decodes the words and transmits them over LTE using a provisioned eSIM. The implant is a separate component. It does not modify the Secure Element or the Ledger operating system, and it does not alter transactions or signatures.

The Donjon will analyze the signers it receives and will share more as the investigation continues.

We have not confirmed the total number of affected users or the total value lost. Figures circulating online come from third parties and Ledger has not fully verified them. If your funds were drained and you have not contacted us, please do so through Ledger Support so we can include your case. We are also reviewing reports of implants in other signers and locations. We will continue to share information as the investigation progresses. Rest assured the Ledger team is going above and beyond to leave no stone unturned to investigate this situation to the strongest possible outcome.

If you bought a Ledger signer from CryptoBilis and have not set it up, do not set it up and contact Ledger Support. If you have set it up, transfer your assets promptly to a new signer with a new recovery phrase. Do not enter or restore any recovery phrase on a signer bought from CryptoBilis. Never enter your recovery phrase into a website, app or form.

If you lost funds or hold a tampered signer, contact Ledger Support at https://t.co/QzukOZdEzq and file a report with local law enforcement. Do not send the signer to anyone before speaking with Ledger Support or local law enforcement. If you lost funds, coordinate with law enforcement before opening the signer. Researchers and others with relevant information can write to security@ledger.com.

If you did not buy from CryptoBilis and want to inspect the inside of your signer, the guide is at https://t.co/Bh9DHQulIv. Use caution and make sure your recovery phrase is backed up first, because opening a signer can damage it.

Ledger will never call you, message you directly, or ask for your 24-word recovery phrase. We will update this post when we verify new information.

text:
Burn & mint

A burn & mint bridge burns tokens on one chain and mints them on another, usually with minting authority across the connected deployments.

For this reason, risks from the bridging mechanism and the connected chains can affect the entire token supply, as long as the bridge has unrestricted minting authority across those deployments. In the case of a multichain token wrapper, the risk can instead be limited to the amount initially locked.

text:
Yes, AI is rapidly advancing mathematics (and theoretical physics problems that are essentially mathematical). Like Ramanujan’s notebooks, human mathematicians will spend months (years?) poring over the stream of papers that AI effortlessly generates, hoping to verify and understand them, probably until math itself (via Lean) becomes a branch of computer science like almost everything else.

However, after math and physics, there is still a next scientific frontier: chemistry, and especially biology and medicine.

I mean, it was already the frontier, but it’s the next one too. AI can crush deterministic math problems on the computer, but biomedicine is a highly empirical, noisy, multivariate, and yet often predictable domain.

Thus, AI radically increases our ambitions in biomedicine. All the omics data, all the messy literature, it can all be synthesized and analyzed in a flash. This is what the labs mean when they talk about curing all diseases. The tooling is available to take cracks at biomedical problems previously thought impossible.

Midjourney is doing this, Chan Zuckerberg is doing this, Anthropic is doing this, but there will be so much more.

text:
Agent 自己改 Harness，最难的其实并不是「怎么改」。

而在于没有标准答案时，怎么知道这次改动到底有没有变好。

Google 团队这篇 Harness²，专门研究开放世界里的 Harness 自进化。

它设计了两层递归。

第一层针对当前任务：先提出 Harness 修改，再让新旧版本在相同条件下执行，通过行为差异判断哪些改动值得保留。

也就是说，它不依赖 ground-truth verifier，也能用真实执行结果来指导修改。

第二层更有意思：

每次改 Harness 的过程也会被总结成经验，记录什么问题、用了什么修改、为什么有效，再拿去指导未来的新任务。

所以它积累的，不只是更好的 Harness，还有「怎么改 Harness」这件事本身。

在 WorkBuddy-Bench、JobBench 和法律 Agent Benchmark 上，单轮改进就能稳定提升 GLM-5 和 Gemini 3.5 Flash，最高分别提升 11.5、4.5 和 11.8 个百分点；继续增加递归预算，表现还能进一步上涨。

我更关注第二层递归。

单次把 Agent 调得更好并不难，真正接近长期自进化的，是系统开始积累「过去怎么把自己调好」的经验。

Harness² 往前走的一步，就是让改进机制本身也开始有记忆。

text:
Did quantum and AI cryptography fears wake up dormant Bitcoin?

Coins dormant for 7+ years have been waking up faster every year, rising from 10 wallets per day in 2023 to 23 in 2024, 40 in 2025, and 45 so far in 2026, with about 300,000 dormant BTC ($31B) moving in 2025 alone, partly because each year another cohort of coins ages past the 7-year mark.

Against that backdrop, we tested six quantum headlines since 2024, including Google’s Willow chip, Google’s ECDSA paper, OpenAI’s math release, and Justin Drake’s “bunker mode” tweet, and found that dormant coins showed no consistent response across them (p = 0.23).

October was the one exception, as wallets with exposed public keys, which are the coins most at risk if ECDSA breaks, made up 43% of the wallets waking up compared with 19% normally, but most of that came from a single source, with 76 of the 87 exposed wallets that moved on 10/06 sweeping about 181 BTC ($15M) over the week into wallets created on 09/21 that Arkham’s model tentatively attributes to the Japanese exchange GMO Coin, which looks like an exchange consolidating thousands of old legacy deposit addresses rather than reacting to the headlines.

Excluding the GMO Coin sweep, October still ranks in the 96th percentile, although only 41% of the remaining exposed movers sent coins to fresh addresses as “bunker mode” advises, compared with 55% normally, while total dormant BTC moved from 10/06 to 10/13 was just 3,499 BTC ($291M), below a typical week of about 4,100 BTC, as the price slipped from $85.5K on 10/06 to $81.7K today.

So far, quantum fear has changed which dormant wallets move, mostly through one exchange sweep (which may have already been planned), while the amount of dormant BTC moving has stayed normal, and the signal to watch is large exposed-key balances moving to fresh addresses, which would show holders actually following Justin Drake’s “bunker mode” advice.

text:
I think I have solved one of the most common problems in secondary markets with AI inference - how can the user know that the reseller did not log or change the prompt, while making sure the selected model is the one they agreed to and that the billing is correct?

Traditional solutions are very cumbersome. They rely on the ability of the client to audit a TEE enclave, meaning understanding the whole operating system - how the keys are generated, if the operator can't log to the server, etc. Most clients trust "any" attestation (it's attested, it must be right), some trust the fact that the same enclave runs for everyone (which is not nothing, this rules out targeted attacks, given someone audits the enclave), some people at least look if the enclave has published source code.

Very few (usually lim=>0) actually do the reproducible build and audit the code and whole operating system reselling the inference.

Routstr-confidential uses cryptography and PKI to achieve the desired outcome of private and secure inference, without needing to audit anything specific for the operator. It can be used for many other API call use cases.

@routstrai itself is a permissionless way to find your inference provider on a secondary market. They usually have much lower prices than upstream. And now you can verify that you are not paying with your data, or you are not being cheated by paying for more expensive model than you get.

Feel free to use the protocol with any other reseller proxy though, it's all open-source.

In an updated investigation into the recent hardware wallet tampering incident, Ledger disclosed that an organized criminal syndicate spent months purchasing authentic Ledger devices, disassembling them to implant custom hardware designed to exfiltrate recovery phrases (seed phrases), and then redistributing the compromised units through Southeast Asian resale channels. The attackers also engineered a multi-million-dollar infrastructure to intercept seed phrases, drain user assets, and launder illicit proceeds.

Ledger emphasized that the incident constitutes an isolated attack on local third-party distribution channels, confirming that its proprietary secure element chips, operating system (BOLOS), and internal server infrastructure remain fully intact and uncompromised. The company has instructed authorized resellers and distributors across Southeast Asia and Hong Kong to temporarily suspend all sales, while enforcing stricter operational security protocols—including prohibiting devices from being displayed on open shelves or exhibition areas and strictly banning the resale of returned units.

text:
这几天SK海力士（SK Hynix）在股票市场跌得很惨，但我盯盘时发现一个很有意思的背离：它在币安上的合约持仓量（OI），反而逆势暴增了。

我把北京时间 10月12日 08:00 到 15日 18:00 的链下数据拉出来盘了一遍：

• 海力士韩股合约：价格跌了约 23.2%，但币本位未平仓数量暴增 108.3%，U本位名义持仓从 3.15亿 涨到了 5.04亿 USDT。
• 海力士ADR合约：价格跌了约 19.3%，未平仓数量增加 46.8%，名义持仓从 1.91亿 升到 2.26亿 USDT。

现货在杀跌，场内的衍生品头寸却在疯狂堆积。

再看多空结构，倾向性非常明显：韩股合约的多头账户占比从 78.02% 飙到了 86.13%；ADR合约也从 60.78% 升到了 72.38%。

衍生品是一手多对应一手空，OI增加本身不代表多空方向。但“OI翻倍 + 多头账户占比飙到86%”这两个指标叠在一起，盘面语言就很清晰了：这波下跌里，大量散户在币安逆势抄底接飞刀，而做市商和机构大户则在另一端接下了庞大的空头对手盘。

这帮用稳定币炒股的人，到底打出了多大的量？我把币安的成交额和美股、韩股现货拉在一起做了个对比。

先看海力士美国ADR（10月12日-14日三天，USDT按1:1折算美元）：
• 10月12日：美股ADR成交 23.89亿 | 币安成交 2.47亿（占 10.4%）
• 10月13日：美股ADR成交 34.87亿 | 币安成交 5.56亿（占 16.0%）
• 10月14日：美股ADR成交 33.62亿 | 币安成交 4.92亿（占 14.6%）
• 三天合计：美股ADR成交 92.38亿 | 币安成交 12.95亿（占 14.0%）
（注：美股这三天分别成交约1472万、2220万和2279万份，按每日成交量×收盘价估算）

再看韩国正股，币安的相对体量更夸张：
同样三天，韩国正股成交额折合约 138亿美元，而币安韩股合约打出了 37.33亿 USDT 的成交量，直接干到了韩国本土现货成交的 27%。

把两个盘子加总：
三天时间，币安海力士合约总成交 50.28亿 USDT；同期美韩两个现货市场合计成交约 230.4亿美元。单看名义成交额，币安一家就已经相当于传统现货主战场总量的 21.8%（超过两成）。

这个量级，哪怕放在传统二级市场也绝对无法忽视了。

当然，在商言商，数据口径得拎清楚：永续合约自带高杠杆、高频换手，50亿的名义成交额不代表有50亿真金白银的净流入；这21.8%也不能直接算作市场份额，因为分母还没算上传统市场庞大的期权和股指期货。

但哪怕剔除杠杆水分，还有一组盘口数据非常说明问题：

这三天里，币安海力士ADR合约有 69.8% 的成交，发生在美股常规交易时段（6.5小时）之外。如果只算美股开盘时段，币安ADR合约三天成交约 3.91亿 USDT，大概是美股日成交额的 4.2%。

也就是说，股票永续合约目前最大的PMF（产品市场契合度），是承接了全天候的交易需求。虽然盘前盘后、夜盘和韩国时区也在提供价格发现，但这近70%的盘外成交说明，有相当一批资金正在把加密交易所当成7×24小时的全球股票风险对冲池。

这背后的资金属性和传导机制，才是最值得琢磨的：

第一，交易习惯的降维碰撞。对习惯了Crypto高波动的资金来说，传统龙头股连续大跌20%，简直是天然的盈亏比洼地。现在不需要经历繁琐的出入金去开传统券商账户，直接在熟悉的U本位账户里就能一键开干。

第二，跨市场Delta对冲带来的真实买盘。当币圈散户在币安疯狂开多海力士，做市商（MM）被动接下空头头寸后，为了保持Delta中性，MM大概率需要去韩国现货或美股ADR市场买入正股进行对冲（当然具体对冲比例取决于MM的内部库存、跨所头寸和净敞口，不会是1:1传导）。

这意味着，稳定币市场里的FOMO抄底情绪，正在通过做市商的套利和对冲机制，穿透壁垒，变成传统股票市场里的真实买盘。

以前我们总是单向研究“美股怎么带崩/带飞币圈”。但随着股票永续合约的流动性起势，稳定币交易体系已经开始反向渗透传统资产的定价过程。

我一直觉得，早晚币圈会逐步掌握美股定价权，海力士这波超50亿U的博弈证明，传统股票市场已经多了一群资金充沛、极其嗜血的稳定币玩家。以后做热门股的微观结构和情绪分析，除了盯紧传统的期权Gamma和暗池数据，加密交易所里的OI、资金费率（Funding Rate）和盘外成交，恐怕也得放进交易员的监控面板里了。

author: elonmusk
quoted_text:
The only other person who’s ever made me this excited about a product unveil was Steve Jobs. Watching him introduce the first iPhone is a huge part of why I fell in love with technology.

Elon brings that feeling back for me, but honestly, I think he takes it to a whole different level. Tomorrow, he and the Tesla team are unveiling the next-gen Roadster, and I seriously cannot wait. 

The Roadster they showed in 2017 already promised 0–60 mph in 1.9 seconds. Since then, Elon has talked about a Tesla–SpaceX collaboration, having it fly, and getting that time below ONE second, and calling it “the least interesting part” of the car. 

How do you say something like that and expect me NOT to be excited?!

But beyond how fast it goes, I want to see something that makes me sit there and say, “Wow… how in the world did they build that?” I honestly don’t know what they’re going to show us, and that’s part of what makes this so much fun. I really want to be surprised and see the unthinkable.

These days I feel many older people don’t get that excited about things… I only see that spark in kids. But imo, we should still get excited about people building cool things. We should still root for the nerds, engineers, and designers trying to do something that has never been done before.

And I hope there’s a kid watching tomorrow who feels what I felt watching Steve Jobs introduce the iPhone. Someone who sees this car and starts wondering how it works, sketching their own ideas, or thinking about what they could build someday.

I hope y’all are ready to have your minds blown. 

I’m rooting for you, Elon, and the entire Tesla team behind this car. 

Go give us a night we’ll never forget!

text:
Bernie Sanders says the top 1% owns more than the bottom 93%, that fewer than a thousand billionaires got $2.2 trillion richer last year, and that it's "obscene."

It's the most seductive and most wrong economic argument of our time. Let me explain why.

First, wealth distribution follows a power law. Always. Everywhere. Books, music, startups, followers on X, goals in soccer. A small minority captures most of the value. That's not a bug of capitalism. It's the mathematical signature of every system where value gets created.

So the only question that matters isn't "how big is the rich's slice?" It's "is the cake growing, and is the slice of the poorest growing with it?"

And the answer is yes. In 1990, more than one human in three lived in extreme poverty. Today it's about one in ten. During exactly the period when billionaires multiplied.

Bernie shows you the slice. He never shows you the cake.

Second thing he won't tell you: past a certain level, wealth stops being consumption. It becomes capital allocation.

Elon Musk isn't sleeping on a pile of cash. He owns stakes in Tesla, SpaceX, xAI. Jeff Bezos owns Amazon stock. That "$2.2 trillion" isn't sitting in a checking account. It's factories, rockets, data centers, millions of jobs. Nobody can eat $100 billion. You can only decide where to invest it.

Once you understand that, the whole debate changes. The real question becomes: who allocates capital better?

The people who built Amazon, SpaceX and Nvidia? Or politicians?

A 5% wealth tax isn't "taking money from the rich." It's taking investment decisions away from people who proved they can create value and handing them to people who proved the opposite.

Because the fundamental difference between an entrepreneur and a politician is consequences.

The entrepreneur invests his own money. If he allocates badly, he loses everything. The market corrects him brutally, no appeal. That's why most startups die: the system kills bad decisions.

The politician invests other people's money. If he allocates badly, nothing happens. Worse, he gets a bigger budget to "fix the problem."

Milton Friedman put it better than anyone. There are four ways to spend money. Your money on yourself: you care about price and quality. Your money on others: you care about price. Others' money on yourself: you care about quality. Others' money on others: you care about nothing.

Government is the fourth box. By design.

Perfect example: California high-speed rail. Approved in 2008 for about $33 billion. Current estimated cost: over $100 billion. Passengers carried: zero. No entrepreneur would have survived that. The politicians who pushed it built careers on it.

And when allocation has no consequences, it eventually finds a buyer. A politician who controls billions without accountability becomes the most profitable target in the world for anyone who wants to steer that money.

The irony is that the left that rails against billionaires is itself funded by billionaires. George Soros is one of the biggest Democratic donors in history. The Gates Foundation shapes public health policy across the planet.

Politicians don't fight billionaires. They pick their own. The ones who fund the state over the ones who compete with it.

So if we actually want fewer poor people, we have to stop judging ideas by their intentions and start judging them by their results. And the results are brutally clear.

China, 1978: Deng Xiaoping opens the economy to markets. More than 800 million people escape extreme poverty. The largest retreat of misery in human history. Not through redistribution. Through the freedom to build.

India, 1991: liberalization. Same movie.

South Korea and North Korea: same people, same language, same starting point in 1953. One became one of the most advanced economies on earth. The other has famines.

Poland and Ukraine: comparable living standards in 1990. Today the average Pole is more than three times richer than the average Ukrainian.

Argentina: a year and a half of liberalization, and the poverty rate falls from over 50% to around 30%.

No country in history escaped poverty by punishing the people who build. Every single one did it by letting them build.

And if you want to see what Bernie's program looks like in real life, you don't have to imagine it. It exists. It's called France. We've been running it for 45 years.

Mass nationalizations in 1981. Two years later, Socialist president Mitterrand has to reverse course into austerity.

Retirement at 60. The 35-hour workweek.

A wealth tax for 35 years. Hundreds of wealthy households left every year for Belgium, Switzerland, London, taking their capital, their companies and their future taxes with them. Macron finally scrapped it in 2018.

Hollande's 75% tax: raised a few hundred million, drove talent out, abandoned after two years.

One of the highest tax burdens in the OECD. Public spending around 57% of GDP, a record in the developed world.

Last balanced budget: 1974. Public debt: over €3.4 trillion. Mass unemployment for four decades.

If taxing the rich and growing the state made people prosperous, France would be the richest country on the planet.

It isn't. GDP per capita in France is barely more than half of America's. It's lower than Mississippi, the poorest state in the US. Not a single global tech giant. Our best engineers build Silicon Valley instead. I've been going back and forth between Paris and San Francisco for years. I see it every week.

And California is about to replay the movie. Prop 40, on the ballot November 3rd, would take 5% of billionaires' net worth. Even Gavin Newsom, a Democratic governor, opposes it. The state's own nonpartisan budget analyst warns that income tax revenue could drop every year if the wealthy leave. Larry Page, Sergey Brin and Peter Thiel have reportedly already started moving their assets out.

You don't fight poverty by shrinking the top. You fight it by growing the cake.

Bernie wants a society where nobody has too much. I want a society where nobody has too little.

The first has been tried everywhere and produces equality in stagnation. The second lifted a billion people out of misery.

Choose.
author: BillAckman
quoted_text:
The top 1% owns more wealth than the bottom 93%.

1 man owns more wealth than the bottom 53% of households.

Less than a thousand billionaires got $2.2 trillion richer in the last year.

Obscene.

Yes. We need a 5% billionaire wealth tax in California and throughout America.

quoted_text:
I don't recommend anyone scramble to move their funds to new wallets today. But we should take the risks to cryptography from AI-accelerated math seriously, and minimize our exposure to not just quantum-vulnerable cryptography, but also potentially AI-vulnerable cryptography.

The core new area of risk from this viewpoint is, unfortunately, ML-DSA / FHE / lattices.

(and it's also another reason, along with quantum, why ECDSA might fall even faster than expected, hence the "fresh address" recommendation)

So far most people have been in the mode of thinking "elliptic curves broken, hashes safe, lattices safe". But there is a good chance that the concrete security of lattices will take serious hits from the next two years of AI math.

The basic threat model is: factoring is something that naively takes 2^(n/2) time, but over decades smart people have found and optimized number field sieves, and degraded that to 2^O(n^(1/3)), which is why RSA keys and signatures need to be ~400 bytes (and not 64 bytes). What if there are skeletons in the closet like that, both for elliptic curves and lattices, that we are simply not smart enough to discover - but bots soon will be?

This is a major part of the reason why for the past year ethereum's lean roadmap has been going in the "hash-only" direction: no lattices, no ML-DSA, no Falcon, no lattice-based commitments inside ZK proofs, etc. Signatures in lean ethereum are all hash-based, either WOTS or SPHINCS-.

For signatures and proofs, we already know how to go hash-only. The bigger challenge is for *public-key encryption* - and this goes far beyond blockchains. Secure communication, anonymizing protocols, lots of things need public-key encryption.

And unfortunately there are long-standing mathematical theorems showing why public-key encryption cannot be done with hashes alone. You have to have some kind of trapdoor object that has at least one form of usable "structure" - either group theory (incl. isogenies) or lattices or code-based or potentially in the future even more newfangled and spooky things (local mixing?). But for anything that has structure, you should assume that AI will make at least some progress in breaking that structure. Here, one reasonable inference is that if you want to make something plausibly long-term secure, multiply the key sizes by 10.

To me that's a very plausible world and something not at all extreme to predict. If AI will bring us 50 years of math in 2 years, then that 50 years of math may very plausibly include a "naive factoring -> GNFS" level of improvement to our ability to break lattices. In that world, lattices will still exist, but they will have to be significantly bigger to guarantee the same level of safety.

And at those new larger sizes, hash-based constructions will beat lattice-based constructions on concrete efficiency in every use case where hash-based constructions are possible at all.

Theoretically, of course it's possible that hashes are broken too (eg. P = NP would imply that). But I think P = NP is very unlikely. And intuitively, it's much more likely that a mathematical object has exactly no exploitable structure (like hashes are intended to), than that a mathematical object has exactly ~3 forms of exploitable structure (for elliptic curves: associativity, Schoof, pairings) and not some secret fourth form of structure we have not yet discovered that greatly degrades its security (for elliptic curves, ECDLP and pairing security). Similar for LWE, SVP, RLWE and the zoo of lattice problems.

For this reason, we do not yet see any reason to worry and start padding the byte size of hashes (if we start to worry more, we would pad the round count first before doing anything to the byte size).

Concrete TLDR, my own personal views:

* Hash-based > lattice-based, in those situations where hash-based is possible at all
* For anything lattice-based, be much more paranoid on param sizes. Remember that blockchains are only a small portion of the cryptography story; this point goes far beyond blockchains and applies to eg. access to websites, secure messaging, Tor / VPNs ...
* For privacy protocols, strongly favor NOT putting encrypted notes onchain. Instead, send them offchain through some third-party mechanism.
* If it's not difficult for you, keeping your funds in addresses which have not yet been used to make a transaction is a good idea. If it's easy for you, do it. **But be careful about migrations; I personally have lost more money in botched migrations than I have lost in all hacks combined**.
* For multisig wallets, doing confirmations offchain is better than onchain, because this way the signatures of signer wallets do not get exposed to the public, so if ECDSA falls to AI much faster than expected, at least the multisig "gracefully degrades" to a 1-of-1 where the 1 is whoever was gathering the signatures - a much better place to be than "anyone can take the money"

Alexandr Wang 和 Jeff 参加的是 HRT 第一届实习项目，共 10 人。实习是三周竞赛制，Jeff 和 Scott Wu 几乎每轮都包揽前两名。

text:
最近在给硅谷 AI Startup 做增长，分享一些经验：找 UGC，而不是 KOL；找 KOS，而不是 KOC

做了几年全球 KOL Marketing，接触过欧美、日韩、东南亚等市场的 2000 多位 Creator，最近越来越觉得，AI Startup 的增长逻辑，和传统消费品牌完全不一样。

尤其是早期 AI 产品，预算有限、产品迭代快、用户认知还没建立。如果还按照传统的 KOL Marketing 逻辑，找大博主、谈报价、发视频、看曝光，ROI 很容易惨不忍睹。

分享几个我自己的观察。

1️⃣找 UGC，而不是 KOL

很多 AI Startup 一上来就想找几十万、上百万粉丝的科技博主合作。但实际上，早期产品更缺的不是曝光，而是能够证明产品价值的内容。

一个有 100 万粉丝的科技 KOL，可能只能给你带来一波短期流量；但一个只有 3000 粉丝、真正理解产品的 Creator，可能帮你跑通一个高转化的内容模板。

我更倾向于寻找能够持续生产 UGC风格内容的创作者，而不是单纯买 KOL 的流量。

尤其是 AI 工具，用户最想看的往往不是产品发布会，而是这个工具能帮我完成什么？比原来的工作流快多少？能不能直接复刻？

真正有价值的是内容资产，而不只是创作者的粉丝资产。

2️⃣找 KOS，而不是 KOC

KOC强调普通消费者的真实体验，KOS（Key Opinion Sales）则更接近懂产品、懂场景、能够影响购买决策的人。

我觉得 AI Startup 尤其需要后者。

比如你做的是 AI Coding 产品，与其找泛科技博主，不如找真正每天用 Cursor、Claude Code、Codex 写代码的开发者。

做 AI Design，就去找设计师、独立创作者。做 AI Agent，就去找正在利用 Agent 自动化工作流的人。

这些人的粉丝可能不多，但受众足够精准，而且他们知道用户真正的痛点。

AI 产品的投放，本质上是在寻找能够替你完成用户教育的人。

3️⃣不要先找达人，先找到有效的 Content Format

我见过不少 Startup，产品刚上线就开始大规模联系达人，结果投了几十条视频，播放量还不错，注册却寥寥无几。

问题可能根本不是达人，而是内容形式没有跑通。

我的建议是先测试 3～5 种不同的内容方向，例如Before / After：使用 AI 前后的效率对比、Tutorial：30 秒完成一个具体任务、Challenge：用 AI 挑战过去需要几小时的工作、Comparison：和竞品做同场景对比、Build in Public等

每种形式找几个小体量 Creator 测试，观察留存、点击、注册和激活，再决定放大哪一种。

4️⃣全球化投放不是把英文视频翻译成十种语言

这是很多 AI Startup 容易犯的错误。

美国用户可能更关注效率提升、个人生产力和商业回报；日本市场往往需要更清晰的操作演示与信任建立；东南亚市场则需要结合当地用户的实际使用场景与价格敏感度。

当然，这些只是市场假设，最终还是要通过数据验证，不能简单用国家给用户贴标签。

我个人比较推荐先在英语市场跑通内容模型，再寻找当地 Native Creator 进行本地化创作，而不只是翻译字幕。

甚至同一个 AI 产品，不同市场应该强调完全不同的 Use Case。

Localization ≠ Translation。

5️⃣不要迷信 Viral，要建立 Creator Growth Loop

很多团队把一条视频做到百万播放，当成一次非常成功的 Marketing Campaign。

但如果第二天流量归零，产品留存也没有改善，那这次投放的长期价值可能很有限。

Creator 生产内容 → 测试不同 Hook → 追踪注册与激活 → 找出高转化模板 → 复用到更多 Creator → 将有效内容用于广告投放 → 持续优化。

6️⃣AI Startup 应该把 Creator 当成产品增长的一部分，而不只是营销渠道

我认为这是最重要的一点。

传统品牌找达人，通常是为了让更多人知道品牌。

但对于 AI Startup，Creator 还可以帮助团队发现真实 Use Case，测试不同的用户群体，甚至反向影响产品 Roadmap。

比如，一个 AI 工具最初定位给设计师，但投放过程中发现很多电商卖家正在用它批量生成商品素材，而且付费意愿更强。

这时候，Creator Marketing 实际上帮助团队找到了新的 ICP，所以早期 AI 产品最应该追踪的，未必是 CPM、CPE，甚至不只是 CAC。

而是哪些 Creator 带来了真正激活、留存和付费的用户。

未来 AI Startup 的 Creator Marketing，会越来越像一套轻量化的增长实验系统。

一个拥有 1000 个精准用户的专业创作者，可能比一个拥有 100 万泛娱乐粉丝的博主更有商业价值。

而真正厉害的增长团队，不是认识多少头部 KOL，而是能否以足够低的成本，持续找到有效的内容、创作者和用户场景。

不要花钱购买影响力，要花钱验证增长。

text:
.@UNCX_token was exploited across multiple chains for ~$1.5M. The root cause was inconsistent accounting of _totalTokenShares between release() and cancel(). This variable tracks the total outstanding shares of all schedules for a token.

Specifically, after release(), a schedule with _depositedShares = D and schedule.released = R has only D − R shares remaining in _totalTokenShares. However, cancel() removes D − V, where V is the recalculated vestedShare.

This accounting assumption can be broken through a donation followed by a top-up, which increases schedule.totalAmount while minting very few new shares and pushes V below R. Consequently, D − V exceeds the schedule’s remaining D − R shares, causing cancel() to deduct shares already removed by release(). This reduces the shared _totalTokenShares denominator and inflates the payout from the schedule retained by the attacker.

The key attack steps are illustrated using this exploit transaction:
https://t.co/se7slWXock
1. Set up three schedules: The attacker created schedules 5058, 5059, and 5060. They fully released 5059 and 5060 while retaining 5058 for the final withdrawal.
2. Donate: The attacker transferred tokens directly to the vesting contract, inflating the asset-per-share value without minting new shares.
3. Top up and cancel: The attacker topped up schedules 5059 and 5060 with future-vesting tokens. Due to the manipulated share price, the top-ups greatly increased schedule.totalAmount while minting very few new shares, pushing vestedShare below schedule.released. Cancelling the schedules then deducted previously released shares from _totalTokenShares again.
4. Extract profits: With _totalTokenShares artificially reduced, the attacker released schedule 5058 at an inflated redemption value and repaid the flash loan.

The attacker repeated this process to drain assets from the vulnerable contract.

UNCX Vesting V2: Security Incident Update

Following the security incident affecting our Vesting V2 contracts across several chains earlier today, we want to share an update on the measures taken, the affected tokens, and what comes next.

1. Security measures and containment

We have implemented several measures to prevent further exploitation of the affected contracts:

> Introduced substantial flat fees exceeding 1,000 ETH per lock.
> Removed all clients and contract interactions that previously allowed these fees to be bypassed.
> Increased token fees to the maximum permitted by the Vesting V2 contracts (5%), making repeated vesting top-ups economically unviable.

These measures are designed to prevent further exploitation through the identified methods. While our investigation and monitoring remain ongoing, we firmly believe we have taken the necessary steps available to us to contain the incident.

2. Scope of the incident

As previously communicated, all LP lockers remain unaffected, across every protocol and chain supported by UNCX.

The incident is isolated to UNCX Vesting V2. Our legacy vesting contracts are also unaffected and have undergone additional checks and review.

The incident currently involves 10 tokens across 4 chains:

Ethereum (6): $pepecoin, $EDGEN, $ZC, $X, $LO0P, $PAAL

Base (1): $IMO

BNB Chain (1): $BTCLE

Robinhood Chain (2): $CASHCAT, $RKST

3. Next steps for affected projects and communities

We are already in contact with most of the affected teams, communities or individuals impacted. 

We expect to share further guidance and next steps with affected teams this week.

We will also publish a comprehensive incident report covering the technical findings, financials, and the details of our proposed recovery plan.

Important: For all impacted tokens, we strongly advise against trading in the affected pools until further guidance is provided by the respective token teams. We will be coordinating directly with those teams over the coming days.

4. Investigation and recovery efforts

Our investigation remains active, and we are coordinating with law enforcement and @seal911.

To date, no funds have been returned by the attackers (primary and copycats) on any affected chain. We strongly encourage the responsible party to contact us directly to discuss a resolution.

We understand the seriousness of this incident for affected projects, holders, and communities. 

Our immediate priorities remain preventing further exploitation, establishing the full extent of the impact, and working closely with affected teams toward a recovery plan.

We will continue to communicate when any meaningful updates become available.

Thank you for your patience.

The UNCX Team

台积电 $TSM 最新财报数据出了

净利润连续六个季度刷新记录

但是

我们会发现第三季度，台积电的晶圆出货量同比只增长了9.6%，实际上已经是这6个季度中最低的水平

与之形成反差的数据除了净利润，还有营收的同比增速

如我做的图所示，红蓝线在过去几个季度几乎是同步变化，唯独这个季度相比最近几个季度分化格外明显

（1）晶圆出货同比增速从16.6%进一步放缓至9.6%，美元营收增速却从33.7%提高至41.2%
（2）两者相差31.6个百分点，是过去六个季度中最大的一次分化

如果只是半导体行业普遍复苏，带来更多芯片订单

我们应该更容易看到晶圆出货数量的同步增加

但现在收入增长远远快于出货数量，说明单纯增加晶圆出货数量，并不足以解释这轮增长，同时也没法借此推导半导体行业普遍复苏的这一结论

更多的可能来自客户购买的产品组合变化

那么，究竟是哪类客户在推动这种变化？

答案是高性能计算业务(HPC)

HPC是台积电按照终端应用划分的一项业务，包含AI加速器、服务器处理器以及其他高性能计算相关芯片

这类芯片通常对性能、功耗和制造工艺要求较高，不少产品需要使用先进制程，有些还需要复杂的先进封装

去年同期HPC占台积电总营收的57%，在最新的财报数据中，这个数字已经提高到了68%

如果按照各季度的营收和业务占比粗略推算，第三季度HPC收入同比增长约80%

更夸张的是，台积电本季度同比增加的营收当中，接近90%可以由HPC业务的增长解释

也就是说，其他业务当然也在创造收入，但主要拉动台积电增长的，已经高度集中于高性能计算相关订单

这也解释了为什么台积电的收入和晶圆出货数量越来越不成比例

_____________________________________

不过，HPC增长很快，并不是第三季度才发生的新变化

在前两个季度HPC环比增速都在20%及以上，所以更难能可贵的是，在它已经占到总营收将近七成的情况下，依旧能够维持20%左右的季度增长

HPC能够贡献如此高比例的新增营收，究竟是因为台积电卖出了更多晶圆，还是因为这些订单本身就能创造更高的收入？

结合前面晶圆出货增速与营收增速的反差，我更倾向于认为，后者在这轮增长中的作用正在变得越来越重要

而本季度的先进制程收入结构，也提供了一些佐证

比如2纳米制程的晶圆收入占比，上季度还只有3%，本季度就提高到了8%，3纳米也从30%进一步提高至33%

两者合计已经占到晶圆收入的41%，相比上季度提高了8个百分点

从这几个季度的数据来看，可以联想为台积电可能已经不需要依靠晶圆出货量同比例增长，就能创造更高的营收

增长的来源高度集中在高性能计算及相关先进制造需求上

同时也因为主要增长归因为先进制造的需求，所以不能简单拿台积电的业绩表现，去证明整个半导体行业都在同步复苏

这也是为什么，市场上很多观点都表示半导体并未迎来复苏

毕竟对于那些主要生产成熟制程芯片的厂商来说，它们面对的客户需求和市场环境，可能完全是另一回事

crypto made it possible to launch almost any asset onchain, but most markets still work exactly the same way. create a token, pair it with liquidity, collect fees and hope trading activity follows.

programmable markets open up a much bigger design space.

imagine a memecoin that automatically accumulates BTC or tokenized NVDA from trading fees. that treasury could deploy capital into DeFi, earn yield, provide liquidity or fund buybacks, all according to predefined rules.

now add agents that can monitor liquidity, manage treasury allocations and execute strategies within limits enforced by smart contracts.

the next wave of DeFi could be less about launching new assets and more about inventing entirely new ways for markets to behave.

text:
Imagine placing a trade, then watching the price move while your transaction waits.

For a bank moving millions, that delay becomes a risk it has to manage.

In his @_TalkingTokens interview, @lepsoe explains how @ETHGasOfficial wants to make Ethereum faster and more predictable.

The idea has three parts:

• Faster feedback.
ETHGas says it can provide early updates in as little as 50 milliseconds. These “preconfirmations” offer an advance commitment for a transaction; Ethereum still must confirm and finalize it through its normal process.

• Reserve space ahead.
Ethereum has limited transaction capacity. Apps and traders can pay to reserve future space, like booking a seat. Validators, the operators who help run Ethereum, earn revenue by supplying that space.

• Add safeguards.
Banks need to know who they’re dealing with, and prevent others from jumping ahead of their trades for profit. ETHGas’ tools enable transaction screening, order control, and identification of the operators involved.

Together, those features could make Ethereum easier to use for payments and trading. Businesses would have more clarity about when transactions should happen and who is responsible.

So are you still thinking Ethereum is slow and obsolete?

text: The only four real moats btw https://t.co/UveHglUaGt
author: lennysan
quoted_text:
Moats! Does anyone have one anymore?

Yes. Yes, they do.

But only a small subset of what people call moats create real long-term value and defensibility.

Not actually a moat:
1. Distribution: This does matter more than ever. Building products has gotten easier, but getting them to customers has not. Distribution, however, does not create durable defensibility. It helps create the raw ingredients for one, but it is not itself a moat.

2. Execution: Yes, speed is critical for startups. But a company that has to sprint forever is not a good business. Ultimately, it will misstep, slow down, and competition will catch up. Speed gives a company more shots on goal as it tries to build a great product and a great business, but it must eventually find something more durable.

3. Brand: The idea is that when everyone is building the same thing, the most resonant brand will win. But for startups, brand works more like customer acquisition spend: Put money in, get growth out. It’s not something that will effectively keep others from competing long-term. Brand can become a true moat over time (as with Coke or Nike or Apple), but it just takes too long to really matter for most startups.

What you're looking for is compounding advantages: a self-reinforcing flywheel that gets stronger and stronger over time, ultimately making a company very hard to compete with long-term.

There are only four compounding advantages that really matter. Every major tech company has at least one:

1. Switching costs: The more deeply embedded a product is in the way a customer works, the harder it is for that customer to switch. This increases retention and revenue per customer, which can be reinvested into the product.

2. Network effects: The more users a product has, the better it gets for everyone. This increases engagement and attracts more users.

3. Scale economies: The more volume a company has, the larger and more efficient its operations can be. This lowers unit costs, funding lower prices or a better product at the same price, further driving up volume.

4. Data effects: The more usage a product has, the more data it generates. This data can be used to improve the product and increase usage.

If you can’t see the potential for any in the startup you’re considering joining, that’s a red flag.

In today’s incredible post, @danhockenmaier shares a simple framework you can run in about an hour after getting an offer:
1. Identify a startup’s compounding advantage
2. Gauge how strong it could get
3. Measure whether it’s working

Inside: dozens of real company examples, the specific metrics to track, and benchmarks for what good and great look like.

Read it here: https://t.co/jMdyoPpeF6

An update on the data incident announced on 8 October

We recognise that this incident has caused concern to many of our cardholders, and we sincerely regret the concern and inconvenience caused.

This update sets out the steps taken since our last announcement and the precautions that cardholders are advised to take.

What we have done since our last update

- We have filed a police report and are working with the police and the relevant authorities on their investigation.
- We have engaged independent security experts to carry out a security audit of our systems related to card services.
- We have paused new Based Visa Card signups until the independent security audit of our card services systems is complete.
- Requests to close accounts have been processed. Our operations and compliance team is handling the orderly withdrawal of funds for those accounts.
- We are strengthening our internal security controls and working towards recognised third-party security certifications.

Support for affected cardholders

We are finalising further support measures for affected cardholders, which will include identity monitoring services. Eligible cardholders will be contacted directly by email once the arrangements have been confirmed.

What has not changed

Based on our investigations to date:
- The Based Wallet, including perps trading and onchain swaps, was not affected and continues to work as normal.
- Card numbers, CVVs, PINs, ID photographs and liveness check images were not affected.
- Funds on your Based Visa Card are safe, and cards continue to work as normal. Cashback and rebates continue to accrue.
- Be careful of anyone who contacts you using your personal details
- We will never ask for your card number, PIN, CVV, passwords or seed phrase.
- Based Visa Card support is only available through the in-app support chat.
- Our team members will never DM you on Telegram or X about your account.
-  Do not click links or sign wallet transactions from unsolicited messages.
- Our emails about this incident will direct you to check details in the app. They will never ask you to enter card details, payment information or passwords through a link.

Further updates will be shared with affected cardholders directly by email. 

This update reflects our understanding as of today and may change as the investigation continues.
author: shu_bit_
quoted_text:
Based Visa Card: Security Incident Update

On 5 October 2026, we were alerted that an unauthorised party has gained access to an internal dashboard used to manage the Based Visa Card program. The attack was swiftly stopped and contained as soon as it was discovered.

KYC data collected by our card issuer for some cardholders, including name, ID or passport number, date of birth and address, may have been obtained by the attacker.

What was NOT affected:
- Card numbers, CVV and PIN
- Photographs of IDs and liveness check images
- Based Wallet, which was used for trading
- Funds on the Based Visa Card. Your funds are safe and Visa cards continue to work as normal.

Affected cardholders have been notified by email today, and relevant authorities have been informed.

What can you do next?

If you are one of the affected users, assume that the data is compromised. Be careful of impersonation attempts from anyone who possesses that information. Sophisticated attackers may use this information to perform social engineering attacks.

Also, support for Based Visa Card is only done on the in-app support chat, and no team members will DM you on Telegram or X for account servicing purposes. For security reasons, comments on this tweet is disabled on purpose.

We are sorry about this incident, and we are working closely with our card service provider to tighten access controls and enhance monitoring.

text:
One detail from @chainlink's Swift corporate-actions demonstration deserves attention: the shareholder snapshot.

Imagine a tokenized stock exists on four blockchains.

A dividend is announced, but investors are transferring shares between networks around the record-date cutoff.

Who actually receives the dividend?

If each blockchain is treated independently, the same position could be counted incorrectly or missed. Chainlink's demonstrated workflow reconciles holder positions across networks into a single register and applies rules for transfers occurring around the cutoff.

That's an important problem to solve as tokenized assets scale onchain.

A tokenized security can move across networks, but its economic rights still need to remain consistent.

Interoperability has to preserve those rights, not just transfer the token.

Study CRE.

- We have engaged independent security experts to carry out a security audit of our systems related to card services.
- We have paused new Based Visa Card signups until the independent security audit of our card services systems is complete.
- Requests to close accounts have been processed. Our operations and compliance team is handling the orderly withdrawal of funds for those accounts.
- We are strengthening our internal security controls and working towards recognised third-party security certifications.

Support for affected cardholders

We are finalising further support measures for affected cardholders, which will include identity monitoring services. Eligible cardholders will be contacted directly by email once the arrangements have been confirmed.

What has not changed

Based on our investigations to date:
- The Based Wallet, including perps trading and onchain swaps, was not affected and continues to work as normal.
- Card numbers, CVVs, PINs, ID photographs and liveness check images were not affected.
- Funds on your Based Visa Card are safe, and cards continue to work as normal. Cashback and rebates continue to accrue.
- Be careful of anyone who contacts you using your personal details
- We will never ask for your card number, PIN, CVV, passwords or seed phrase.
- Based Visa Card support is only available through the in-app support chat.
- Our team members will never DM you on Telegram or X about your account.
-  Do not click links or sign wallet transactions from unsolicited messages.
- Our emails about this incident will direct you to check details in the app. They will never ask you to enter card details, payment information or passwords through a link.

Further updates will be shared with affected cardholders directly by email. 

This update reflects our understanding as of today and may change as the investigation continues.

text:
The financial system works better the closer you are to New York and London.

I said this in a recent interview with Seoul Economic Daily. Between emerging economies, the same payment still takes longer and costs more. That gap is where stablecoins matter most.

When both currencies exist as stablecoins, they can be exchanged directly. The intermediary banks drop out, and businesses save both time and fees.

We talked about Korea too, where card payments already work well. Used only locally, a won stablecoin risks becoming little more than a marketing tool. Its real value is in foreign exchange.

It’s the same lesson we learned early at @CodexFX. Customers wanted to convert the money they held into the currencies they needed, across both fiat and stablecoins.

Once we built around that, volume grew quickly. In August alone, it topped $1B.

Stablecoin FX is only beginning, and the decisions made over the next 5 to 10 years will determine how the financial system works for the next 100.

Thanks to Do Ye-ri for a sharp conversation.

This gives Flare a path to bring private reserves, credit data, payments data and other restricted financial information into smart contracts without requiring institutions to publish the underlying records.

text:
we just launched something pretty interesting under jupiter labs.

introducing YOLO. 500x to 1000x leverage.

yes, 1000x.

we’ve been experimenting with a different approach to high leverage trading, and YOLO is our first attempt at it.

the idea is pretty simple. what if we could let people trade with extremely high leverage, without actually having to execute these massive leveraged positions in the market?

so we took inspiration from the JLP model and built YOLO, where positions are simulated against real market prices, but the profits and losses are real.

this allows us to offer leverage that goes far beyond what we currently have on jupiter perps, using a completely different approach.

of course, this also comes with some tradeoffs.

since profits are paid out from the pool, if there isn’t enough liquidity to pay out a winning position, the payout can be queued instead of being paid immediately.

it’s a different model from traditional perps, with its own risks and limitations, but i think it’s an interesting experiment worth exploring.

one thing i’ve always liked about building onchain is how much room there is to experiment with new financial products and trading experiences.

and that’s also why we’re launching YOLO under jupiter labs. to give ideas like this a place to be tested, without necessarily having to fit into our existing products.

i’m quite excited to see how people use YOLO and what we can learn from it.

it’s still early, and there are probably many things we can improve along the way.

but that’s the fun part of building and experimenting.

give it a try, understand the risks, and let us know what you think.

text:
On Wednesday, UNCX Vesting V2 was drained on Ethereum, BNB Chain, Base and Robinhood Chain.

@GoPlusSecurity puts the total at about $1.5M, with copycats and MEV bots joining in.

The root cause is one of the oldest bugs in DeFi: two functions that disagree about the same number.

Here is the mechanism, per @Phalcon_xyz and @SlowMist_Team.

The contract pools each token and tracks a global _totalTokenShares.

release() pays a schedule its slice of the pool, then subtracts the released shares (R) from that global.

cancel() later subtracts deposited shares minus vested shares (D minus V), with V recalculated from the schedule's current totalAmount.

That only works if V never drops below R.

The attacker made it drop.
- Step one, fully release two schedules and keep a third.
- Step two, send tokens straight to the contract, which raises the token value per share without minting any shares.
- Step three, top up the released schedules, so totalAmount jumps while very few new shares are minted, and V falls below R.
- Step four, cancel them, so shares already removed by release() get removed again.

Now the global denominator is too small, and the third schedule redeems far more than it should.

Wrap it in a flash loan and repeat.

So here is my checklist, learned from someone else's very bad Wednesday.

If two functions both edit a global total, write the invariant down: the sum of every position's remaining shares equals the global.

Put that in a Foundry invariant test, and let the fuzzer call release, topUp, cancel and plain token transfers in any order.
Never price shares off balanceOf if anyone can donate to the contract.
Track assets internally, or you have built a donation attack with extra steps.
When you subtract something, assert it is no bigger than what is left, and revert if not.

UNCX says LP lockers and legacy vesting were not affected, and a full incident report is coming.

This is not exotic, it's the ERC-4626 donation lesson showing up in a vesting contract, which means audits keep checking functions one at a time instead of the state they share.

text:
Yes, AI is rapidly advancing mathematics (and theoretical physics problems that are essentially mathematical). Like Ramanujan’s notebooks, human mathematicians will spend months (years?) poring over the stream of papers that AI effortlessly generates, hoping to verify and understand them, probably until math itself (via Lean) becomes a branch of computer science like almost everything else.

However, after math and physics, there is still a next scientific frontier: chemistry, and especially biology and medicine.

I mean, it was already the frontier, but it’s the next one too. AI can crush deterministic math problems on the computer, but biomedicine is a highly empirical, noisy, multivariate, and yet often predictable domain.

Thus, AI radically increases our ambitions in biomedicine. All the omics data, all the messy literature, it can all be synthesized and analyzed in a flash. This is what the labs mean when they talk about curing all diseases. The tooling is available to take cracks at biomedical problems previously thought impossible.

Midjourney is doing this, Chan Zuckerberg is doing this, Anthropic is doing this, but there will be so much more.

text:
we just launched something pretty interesting under jupiter labs.

introducing YOLO. 500x to 1000x leverage.

yes, 1000x.

we’ve been experimenting with a different approach to high leverage trading, and YOLO is our first attempt at it.

the idea is pretty simple. what if we could let people trade with extremely high leverage, without actually having to execute these massive leveraged positions in the market?

so we took inspiration from the JLP model and built YOLO, where positions are simulated against real market prices, but the profits and losses are real.

this allows us to offer leverage that goes far beyond what we currently have on jupiter perps, using a completely different approach.

of course, this also comes with some tradeoffs.

since profits are paid out from the pool, if there isn’t enough liquidity to pay out a winning position, the payout can be queued instead of being paid immediately.

it’s a different model from traditional perps, with its own risks and limitations, but i think it’s an interesting experiment worth exploring.

one thing i’ve always liked about building onchain is how much room there is to experiment with new financial products and trading experiences.

and that’s also why we’re launching YOLO under jupiter labs. to give ideas like this a place to be tested, without necessarily having to fit into our existing products.

i’m quite excited to see how people use YOLO and what we can learn from it.

it’s still early, and there are probably many things we can improve along the way.

but that’s the fun part of building and experimenting.

give it a try, understand the risks, and let us know what you think.
